en: Now, we shall explain the application of the yoga for the performance of this traditional corpus (*samāmnāya*). (Darśa: Hotṛ) The rites beginning with the establishment of the sacred fires (*agny-ādheya*) are called *vaitānika* (pertaining to the sacrificial fires). (Darśa:
Hotṛ) However, we shall first explain the New and Full Moon sacrifices (*darśa-pūrṇamāsa*), because they are prescribed therein as the fundamental ritual framework (*tantra*). (Darśa: Hotṛ)

AśvSS 1.1/4: When the sacrificial oblations for the New and Full Moon sacrifices have been set out, the Hotṛ, having been addressed, stands to the northeast of the Āhavanīya fire facing east, wearing the sacrificial cord over the left shoulder (*yajñopavītin*), and having sipped water, enters the sacrificial ground (*vihāra*) by turning to the right, passing to the east of the *utkara* mound and to the west of the *praṇītā* waters.
AśvSS 1.1/5: [He passes] to the west of the fuel-bundle (*idhma*) if it has not yet been brought forward.

AśvSS 1.1.6: [The ritual] for those who have a *cātvāla* [pit] is performed at the *cātvāla*. (Darśa Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.1.7: This is called the "ford" (*tīrtha*). (Darśa Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.1.8: Its movements are always directed toward the east. (Darśa Hotṛ)
And wearing the sacred thread; (Darśa:
Hotṛ) And [wearing] the sacrificial thread and [maintaining] purity; (Darśa:
Hotṛ) And not turning away from the sacrificial ground if the ritual action is being performed there; (Darśa: Hotṛ)

AśvSS 1.1.12: When a single limb is mentioned, one should understand it as the right [limb]. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.1.13: This applies when there is no specific instruction. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.1.14:
When there is an injunction for a ritual act, the Hotṛ [is intended]. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
AśvSS 1.1.15: When [the formula] "he gives" occurs, [the Hotṛ addresses] the sacrificer.

AśvSS 1.1.16: When [the formulas] "he offers" and "he mutters" occur during an expiation (*prāyaścitta*), [the Hotṛ addresses] the Brahman priest. AśvSS 1.1.17: When a verse (*ṛc*) is recited by taking it word by word, [the Hotṛ addresses the Brahman].

AśvSS 1.1.18: At the beginning of each hymn (*sūkta*), if a verse (*pāda*) is missing, [one should recite] it. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.1.19: If a verse is in excess, one should recite a triplet (*tṛca*) in all cases.

(Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.1.20: The silent recitation (*japa*), the consecration (*anumantraṇa*), the swelling (*āpyāyana*), and the worship (*upasthāna*) are to be performed in a whisper (*upāṃśu*). (Darśa: Hotṛ)

AŚvSS 1.1.21: And the mantras are the instruments of the ritual action. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AŚvSS 1.1.22: An exception is stronger than a general rule. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AŚvSS 1.1.23: Having stepped forward with the left foot, having placed the heel level with the northern corner of the altar, having stepped onto the sacrificial grass with the forepart of the foot, holding his hands joined with the fingers pointing upward, and measuring them at the heart or at the navel, he gazes at the junction of heaven and earth.
(Darśa: Hotṛ) AsvSS 1.1/24: This is the station of the Hotṛ. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AsvSS 1.1/25: Or [he may occupy] a seat; in all cases, he is to be thus situated. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
AśvSS 1.1/26: [The Hotṛ recites] other [formulas] by command. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.1/27: Having been prompted, he mutters [the formulas]. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

Homage to the speaker! Homage to the observer! Homage to the announcer! Who will recite this? He shall recite this. May the six wide ones protect me from distress: heaven and earth, day and night, water and plants. Speech has been established; the sacrifice is successful. I enter the meters well. "I myself [name], such-and-such"—he should utter his own name. "In the past, in the future, in what is born, in what is to be born, I share in the inviolable; carry away the unrest of speech. Having drawn back the tips of his fingers, he should join them together with the mantra: "O Jātavedas, delight the cattle in me."
"May heaven and earth be my armor; may Agni be my armor; may the sun be my armor; may the *tiraścīkā* plants be my armor.
May I today attain the first [fruit] of speech. (Darśa:
Hotṛ) Having completed the *sāmidhenī* verses, he recites this. (AśvSS 1.2.2)
(Darśa: Hotṛ) (Comm:
He should recite; this is the meaning.
Having uttered the *him* sound as "him3," he mutters: "bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ oṃ. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
This is the *abhihiṃkāra*. (Darśa: Hotṛ) Having muttered "bhūr bhuvaḥ svar," Kautsa utters the *him* sound. (Darśa:
Hotṛ) And he does not mutter the preceding *japa*. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

AsvSS 1.2/7: Now follow the *sāmidhenī* verses: *pra vo vājā abhidyavaḥ*, *agna ā yāhi vītaye*, *gṛṇāna īḷenyo namasyas*, *tiro 'gnim dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe*, *samidhyamāno adhvare*, and two [verses] beginning with *samiddho agna āhutaḥ*.
(Darśa: Hotṛ) AsvSS 1.2/8:
He should recite them in a single tone (*eka-śruti*) and in a continuous flow (*saṃtatam*). (Darśa: Hotṛ)
AsvSS 1.2.9: The closest proximity of the acute (*udātta*), grave (*anudātta*), and circumflex (*svarita*) accents constitutes monotony (*ekaśruti*).

AsvSS 1.2.10: Having made the *o*-kāra at the end of the Ṛg-verse—beginning with its accentual tone and ending with the letter *m*—three morae (*trimātra*), one should pause at the middle of the following half-verse.
That is called "continuous" (*saṃtata*).
AśvSS 1.2.11: This is the conclusion. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.2.12:
Taking up [the text] from the subsequent [portion] is for the sake of avoiding confusion. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.2.13:
At the completion, the conclusion is made with the syllable *praṇava* (*om*). (Darśa: Hotṛ)
AsvSS 1.2.14: At the pause, there is a duration of four morae. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AsvSS 1.2.15:
There is the occurrence of its final [syllable]. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AsvSS 1.2.16:
Among the stops, [one should pronounce] the last letter of its own class. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

AśvSS 1.2.17: In the case of the semivowels (*antasthā*), he pronounces each one with its corresponding nasalization (*anunāsika*). AśvSS 1.2.18: In the case of the *repha* and the sibilants (*ūṣman*), he pronounces the *anusvāra*. AśvSS 1.2.19: He recites the first and the last [verses] three times each, adding half a syllable (*adhyardhakāra*) to them.
AśvSS 1.2.20: Having recited one and a half [verses], he should pause; then two [verses]. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.2.21:
Two [verses] first, then one at the end, and then one and a half [verses]. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.2.22: These [verses] amount to fifteen; by repeating them [in this manner]. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

By this [rule], the recitation of the *śastra*, the *yājyā*, the *nigada*, the *anuvacana*, the *abhiṣṭavana*, and the *saṃstavana* [are explained]. (Darśa: Hotṛ) But elsewhere, there is no repetition of more than one and a half verses; there is no silent recitation (*japa*) prior to the *abhihiṃkāra*; and there is no repetition of the *abhihiṃkāra* except when there are many [verses], in which case it follows the original form. (Darśa: Hotṛ) There is no cutting off [of the recitation] at the beginning. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
AśvSS 1.2.26: Among the *śastra* recitations, the *abhihiṅkāra* belongs to the *hotraka* priests.

(Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.2.27: At the end of the *sāmidhenī* verses, with the final *praṇava*, one pauses after the *nigada*: "O Agni, you are great, O Brāhmaṇa, descendant of Bharata. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.3.1: He chooses the ancestral lineages (*ārṣeya*) of the sacrificer, as many as there may be. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
AśvSS 1.3.2: For the first time, [he recites] the highest of the high.
(Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.3.3: For the royal clans, [he recites] those belonging to the priestly office.
(Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.3.4: Or for kings, [he recites] the royal seers. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
In case of doubt regarding all [the mantras], [the rule] "mānava" [applies]; (Darśa: Hotṛ).

AśvSS 1.3/6: Having settled [the fire] with the formula, "Kindled by the gods, kindled by Manu, praised by the ṛṣis, rejoiced by the wise, lauded by the poets, sharpened by the sacred word, offered with clarified butter, the leader of sacrifices, the charioteer of rites, the invincible Hotṛ, the swift carrier of oblations"—and having begun with, "The vessel of the mouth, the ladle of the gods, the cup from which the gods drink; like the felly around the rim, O Agni, you encompass the gods; bring the gods for the sacrificer"—he invokes each deity one by one using the second case ending, saying "bring [him]," while moistening the tip [of the ladle].
(Darśa: The Hotṛ)
AśvSS 1.3/7: "O Agni, bring hither [the gods]"—thus for the first deity.

(Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.3/8: "Agni, Soma"—these are the two portions of clarified butter (*ājyabhāgau*). (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.3/9: "Agni, Agni-Soma"—thus at the full moon sacrifice (*paurṇamāsī*). (Darśa: Hotṛ)

AśvSS 1.3.10: At the place of Agni and Soma, Indra and Agni [are invoked] on the new moon day for one who does not offer the *saṃnayya* oblation. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.3.11: For one who offers the *saṃnayya*, Indra or Mahendra [is invoked]. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.3.12: Between the two oblations, Viṣṇu [is invoked] in a low voice (*upāṃśu*), according to the Aitareyiṇas. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
AśvSS 1.3.13: [The animal sacrifice] to Agni and Soma is at the full moon; to Viṣṇu is at the new moon—some say so, others do not, nor any at all. AśvSS 1.3.14:

For other [deities] whose names are whispered, [the Hotṛ says] "Bring them" (*āvaha*) and "He has sacrificed" (*ayāṭ*) loudly, as well as "the dear abodes," "this oblation," and "to the great, the greater.
AśvSS 1.3.15: Those other [deities] mentioned therein who are remote, for those he may whisper or speak loudly.

AśvSS 1.3/16: [The offering] is performed aloud when it is visible; it is performed in a whisper when it is not. AśvSS 1.3/17: The invocation (*āvāhana*) is performed for each individual name as it is called out. AśvSS 1.3/18: Having designated all [the deities], there is a single offering made once for all.

AśvSS 1.3/19: Likewise, in the other recensions (*nigama*), he should praise as if it were a single [verse]. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.3/20: [He should praise] a deity that is common [to all recensions] and has a common purpose. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.3/21: [He should praise] one that is not separated [from the others] within the recensions, [reciting it] once. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

In the case of the *oḷhā* and *āvāpikā* [offerings], having invoked with the words, "Bring the gods who drink the clarified butter; bring Agni for the office of the Hotṛ; bring his own greatness; O Jātavedas, bring them hither; sacrifice for a good victory," he should sit with his knees raised as before, and having spread out the grass from the altar toward the north, he should make a span-measure on the ground.

AśvSS 1.3/22b: "Aditi is his mother; may she not cut me off from the intermediate space. Here, by means of Agni as the deity, by the Trivṛt stoma, the Rathantara sāman, the Gāyatrī metre, the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, the vaṣaṭ-call, and the thunderbolt, I strike down him who hates us and whom we hate.

(Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.3/23a: He should address the one about to call for the *āśrāvaṇa* with the mantra: "Make the sacrifice heard among the gods; make me heard among men for the sake of renown, glory, and spiritual luster (*brahman-varcasa*)."
"O God Savitṛ, choosing this one, he chooses you, Agni, for the office of Hotṛ, together with Vaiśvānara as his father. May Heaven and Earth protect me; Agni is the Hotṛ, I am the human [Hotṛ].

Having heard "the human" from the Adhvaryu, he should rise up with the mantra: "I have risen up with life, with good life, with the sap of the plants, with the powers of Parjanya, following after the immortals.
(Darśa: The Hotṛ)
"Sixty and ninety snares have been loosened between Agni and the Hotṛ; they bind the simple one, while the very wise one passes beyond. Having recited this, he stands up. (Darśa:
Hotṛ) "I follow the path of Truth as the Hotṛ. Having stepped forward and recited this, he should take hold of the Adhvaryu’s shoulder with his hand placed on the side. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
AśvSS 1.3/26: [He goes] to the Āgnīdhra fire by way of the corner or with his left hand. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.3/27: "We take hold of Indra, the domestic priest, at the choosing of the Hotṛ;
he by whom the gods and the Aṅgirases went to the highest heaven, to the sky. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

AśvSS 1.3.28: With the *sammārjana* grasses, he should wipe his face three times toward himself, saying: "Thou art the purifier; purify me with offspring and cattle. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.3.29: Once with the mantra, twice silently.
In all cases, when there is a repetition of the ritual action, [the procedure is as follows]:
(Darśa: Hotṛ) Having touched water, he should address the Hotṛ’s seat with the mantra: “O son of two wives, rise from here; sit on the seat of another who is more ignorant than we. (Darśa:

AsvSS 1.3/31) With his thumb and ring finger, he should pull out a blade of grass from the Hotṛ’s seat toward the west and south, saying: “Expelled is Parāvasu! Then he should sit down with his right knee raised, saying: “Here I sit on the seat of Arvāvasu.”
(Regarding the *darśa* sacrifice, the duties of the *hotṛ*:

These two acts—the throwing out [of the grass] and the sitting down—apply to all seating positions for everyone, even when the first sitting occurs on the same day day after day. (Regarding the *darśa* sacrifice, the duties of the *hotṛ*:
Gautama says they occur twice. (Regarding the *darśa* sacrifice, the duties of the *hotṛ*: AsvSS 1.4.33.

AsvSS 1.4/1: At the establishment of the sacred fires (*agny-ādheya*), when the *brahma-odana* is about to be consumed, the *brahmán* [is the officiant]. (In the *darśa* sacrifice, the *hotṛ* is the officiant. AsvSS 1.4/2:

In the *soma* sacrifice, having returned from the *bahiṣ-pavamāna* chant, [the *hotṛ* is the officiant]. (In the *darśa* sacrifice, the *hotṛ* is the officiant. AsvSS 1.4/3: Having stepped forward, the *hotṛ* [performs the ritual]. (In the *darśa* sacrifice, the *hotṛ* is the officiant.)
AśvSS 1.4/4: [The call] for taking up the offering-ladle occurs at the animal sacrifice.
(Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.4/5: It does not occur at the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.4/6: Kautsa says it does not occur elsewhere than for the Hotṛ. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

Having sat down, [he says]: "O divine *barhis*, may I sit upon you who provide a good seat. (Darśa: Hotṛ) "Be seated further forward on the *barhis*, O Hotṛ!"—having touched the *barhis* with his head resting on his knee, he should thereafter mutter [the following]. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

Homage to the Lord of the Earth! Homage to the Lord of the World! Homage to the Lord of Beings! Homage to Being! I take refuge in the out-breath; I take refuge in the in-breath; I take refuge in the diffused breath; I take refuge in speech; I take refuge in sight; I take refuge in hearing; I take refuge in the mind; I take refuge in the Self. I take refuge in the Gāyatrī; I take refuge in the Triṣṭubh; I take refuge in the Jagatī; I take refuge in the Anuṣṭubh; I take refuge in the meters. May Sūrya protect us from heaven! Homage to the great ones! Homage to the small ones!
(Darśa: Hotṛ) *AśvSS* 1.4/9c:

"O Viśvedevas, instruct me so that I may succeed here as a Hotṛ, seated as the most excellent sacrificer; may I today utter the first word of speech. Having completed this, while the fuel is blazing, he should cause [the Adhvaryu] to take up the two offering-spoons with the following formula.
(Darśa: Hotṛ)

AsvSS_1.4/10: “May Agni, the Hotṛ, know [the offering]; may he know the office of the Hotṛ; may he know the protection. O sacrificer, your deity is well-disposed toward you. Having concluded with “yo agnim,” he should mutter: “You have chosen the Hotṛ. (Darśa: AsvSS_1.4/11): Then he should complete [the rite] with: “O Adhvaryu, take up the butter-sprinkled ladle, which is turned toward the gods and possesses all boons. Let us invoke the gods; I invoke those who are to be invoked; let us pay homage to those worthy of homage; let us sacrifice to those worthy of sacrifice. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

When this recitation is completed, the Adhvaryu calls for the *āśrāvaṇa*. (Darśa: Hotṛ) The Āgnīdhra should respond with the *pratyāśrāvaṇa* while standing at the place of the *utkara*, having taken up the wooden sword (*sphya*) and the faggot-binders; according to the Śāṭyāyanaka, he faces southward.
He says "astu śrauṣaṭ," protracting the syllable "au. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
AśvSS 1.5/1: They perform the *prayāja* offerings. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.5/2: These consist of five. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.5/3:
Being prompted one by one, he performs the *yājyā* recitation. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
AśvSS 1.5/4: [The ritual procedure] begins with the *āgūḥ* and the *yājyā*, excluding the *anuyāja*s.
(Regarding the *hotṛ* at the Darśa sacrifice:
the *āgūḥ* is "ye yajāmahe. (This is the *āgūḥ*. AśvSS 1.5/5: The *āgūḥ* is "ye yajāmahe. (This is the *āgūḥ*.)

The *vaṣaṭ* call is always at the end. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AsvSS 1.5.6: It is louder and more forceful than the *yājyā*. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AsvSS 1.5.7: At the beginning of those two, one should cause [the sound] to flow over. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

AśvSS 1.5/8: And [the *praṇava* is added] at the end of the *yājyā*. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.5/9: Having separated the diphthongs, one should pronounce the vowel *a*; unless it is a dual form or ends in a consonant. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.5/10:
A *visarjanīya* that does not have a short vowel as its preceding syllable (*upadhā*) is elided. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

And the other [consonant] has a *repha* [as its following element]. (Darśa: Hotṛ) That which lacks a *repha* is elided. (Darśa: Hotṛ) The first [consonant] takes its own third [as its following element]. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
AśvSS 1.5.14: [The *vaṣaṭ* call] always [ends] with the syllable *makāra*.
(Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.5.15: "We who sacrifice: O Agni, may the kindling-sticks of the clarified butter enjoy [the offering]," thus is the *vaṣaṭ* call.
(Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.5.16: Thus is the first [offering]. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
Having uttered the *vaṣaṭ* call with the formula, "Speech, vigor, strength, power; may breath and out-breath be in me," he follows it with the consecration (*anumantraṇa*). (Darśa:
Hotṛ) The *vaṣaṭ* call belongs to the *divākīrtya* hymns. (Darśa: Hotṛ) The consecration is likewise. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

This is the illustration of the *yājyā* verses. (The Darśa Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.5.21: "O Agni Tanūnapāt, may you partake of the clarified butter"—this is the second [verse], except for the Vasiṣṭhas, Śunakas, Atris, Vadhryaśvas, and Kṣatriyas. (The Darśa Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.5.22: "O Agni Narāśaṃsa, may you partake of the clarified butter"—this is for those [latter groups]. (The Darśa Hotṛ)
*Īḷo agna ājyasya vyantu*: this is the third [verse].

(The *hotṛ* at the New Moon sacrifice) *Bahir agna ājyasya vetu*: this is the fourth. The *āgūḥ* (invocation) is as follows: having recited the names of the deities as they were invoked, according to the order in which they were enjoined—even those not formally invoked—one says: "Svāhā to so-and-so, svāhā to so-and-so! Svāhā! May the gods who drink the clarified butter, being pleased, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter!"*
(Darśa:
Hotṛ) From this point on, [he should recite] in a low tone. (Darśa: Hotṛ) And [this continues] until the *śamyuvāka*. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

AśvSS 1.5.27: With the middle [verse], the oblations up to the *sviṣṭakṛt* [are offered]. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.5.28: With the last [verse], the remainder [is offered]. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.5.29: "May Agni strike down the Vṛtras"—this is the invitatory verse (*anuvākyā*) for the first *ājyabhāga*.
"O Soma, you are the lord of the virtuous"—this is for the latter [oblation].
"May Agni, being pleased, accept the clarified butter"—this is the *yājyā* for the former. "May Soma, being pleased, accept the oblation of clarified butter"—this is for the latter.
Having uttered the *āgūr*, he performs the offering according to the instruction (*ādeśa*).
(The Darśa Hotṛ’s *āgūr*):
All [verses] are accompanied by invitatory verses (*anuvākyā*) and are without a formal call (*apraiṣa*).
[The verses] other than those [recited] for the subsequent offerings;
(Darśa: Hotṛ) AsvSS 1.5.31: and those belonging to the Soma sacrifice which lie between the Vaiśvānarīya offering and the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings;
(Darśa: Hotṛ) AsvSS 1.5.32: these two Vārtraghna verses [are recited] on the full moon day. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
AśvSS 1.5.33: Due to the specific characteristics of the invitatory verses (*anuvākyā*), there is a change in the name [of the sacrifice]; therefore, there is deliberation [on this matter].
(Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.5.34: The two *yājyā* verses are fixed.
(Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.5.35: On the new moon day (*amāvāsyā*), they are those containing the word *vṛdhat*.
"Agni with the ancient hymn, O Soma, we [invoke] you with songs"—this is the restraint of speech from that point. (Darśa:
Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.5/36: And [the interval] between the invitatory verse (*anuvākyā*) and the offering verse (*yājyā*).

And for the recitation of the *nigadas*, the *anuvacanas*, the *abhiṣṭavanas*, the *śastras*, and the *japas*, [the rule applies] from their commencement until their completion. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AsvSS 1.5.37: Anything other than the means of accomplishing the sacrifice. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AsvSS 1.5.38: In case of an accident, one should mutter: "From this, may the gods protect us. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
Alternatively, [one may offer] another [verse] addressed to Viṣṇu. (The Darśa:
Hotṛ) The deities have been stated;
[now follow] their *yājyā* and *anuvākyā* verses.

"Agni is the head of the earth, this Agni [is the head] of the sacrifice; this Agni is thousandfold. "Viṣṇu strode across this earth three times, the god. "O Agni and Soma, you two who possess equal wisdom, these luminous realms in heaven. "O Indra and Agni, come with your protection, as the inspired singer seeking fulfillment through our songs. "O Indra, bring us winning wealth; O much-invoked one, you have overcome the enemies. "Indra is great, he who by his might... "O Indra, you become great through the sacred word (*brahman*)."
(Darśa: Hotṛ) AsvSS 1.6.1c:
If there is an *upāṃśuyāja* for Agni-Soma, [the offering verse is] "O Agni and Soma, today Mātariśvan has brought you two, one from heaven... (Darśa: Hotṛ) AsvSS 1.6.2:
Then, for the *sviṣṭakṛt*, the invitatory verse (*anuvākyā*) is "Satisfy the longing gods, O youngest one... (Darśa: Hotṛ)

Having recited "ye yajāmahe agniṃ sviṣṭakṛtam ayāḷ agniḥ," and having designated the deity with the genitive case where it occurs, he should continue with "priyā dhāmāny ayāḷ. (Regarding the Darśa sacrifice:

AsvSS 1.6/4) In the same way for the subsequent [deities], but indeed the words "ayāḷ ayāḷ" are placed before them. (The Hotṛ: AsvSS 1.6/5) Having proceeded in order up to the Ājyapā, [the formula is]: "May he sacrifice to the dear abodes of the Ājyapā deities; may he sacrifice to the dear abodes of Agni the Hotṛ; may they sacrifice to their own greatness."

"May he, Jātavedas, perform the worship; may he, the knower of all beings, enjoy the oblations at the sacrifice. "O Agni, Hotṛ of the people's sacrifice, whatever [is offered] today..."—with these words, he performs the offering without pausing.
Or he may do so according to the archetype.
Having touched the two upper joints of the forefinger, he wipes them toward himself with his lips.
With the formula, "Of that which has been offered by the Lord of Speech, I partake for the sake of food and the out-breath," he eats the northern portion with his upper hand;
with the formula, "Of that which has been offered by the Lord of Mind, I partake for the sake of strength and the in-breath," he eats the southern portion with his lower hand.

(The Darśa Hotṛ) Having touched water with his joined palms, having taken up the *iḍā* and placed it in his left hand, and having placed his hand behind it with the fingers pointing northward, he should cause the *avāntareḍā* to be cut off.
AśvSS 1.7.4: Between the thumb and the fingers, he himself should take up the second [portion].
(Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.7.5: Having grasped the portion that has been taken back with the thumb and drawn it back.
(Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.7.6: Having closed his fingers into a fist and having enclosed the *iḷā* on the right side, he invokes it at the level of his mouth or at the level of his breath. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

Iḷā is invoked together with the sky, with the Bṛhat-sāman, and with Āditya; may Iḷā invoke us together with the sky, with the Bṛhat-sāman, and with Āditya. Iḷā is invoked together with the intermediate space, with the Vāmadevya-sāman, and with Vāyu; may Iḷā invoke us together with the intermediate space, with the Vāmadevya-sāman, and with Vāyu.
Iḷā is invoked. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

Together with the earth, with the *rathantara*, with Agni—may Iḷā invite us! Together with the earth, with the *rathantara*, with Agni—the cows have been invited; together with the milk-mixture (*āśir*), may the cows invite me!

The milch-cow has been invited together with the bull; may the milch-cow invite me together with the bull! The cow, whose tracks are dripping with ghee, has been invited; may the cow, whose tracks are dripping with ghee, invite me! The seven divine Hotṛ-priests have been invited; may the seven divine Hotṛ-priests invite me!

(Darśa: Hotṛ) *AśvSS* 1.7/7d: "The companion, the portion, has been invited; may the companion, the portion, invite me. The *iḷā*, the rain, has been invited; may the *iḷā*, the rain, invite me"—this he says in a whisper. Then aloud: "The *iḷā* has been invited; the *iḷā* has been invited; may the *iḷā* invite us; the *iḷā* has been invited. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

AsvSS 1.7/7e: [The portions are] for Manu, for Ghr̥tapadī, for Mitra and Varuṇa, for Brahman, for the gods, the prepared, the invited; the divine Adhvaryus are invited, the human ones are invited. AsvSS 1.7/7f: May they protect this sacrifice and increase the lord of the sacrifice. The two ancient, law-abiding goddesses, Heaven and Earth, mothers of the gods, are invited.

This sacrificer is invited to the subsequent worship of the gods; he is invited to the preparation of more abundant oblation. "O gods, may you enjoy this my oblation"—thus, in that [portion], he says, "I am invited. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

Having invoked the intermediate *iḍā*, he should eat it with the mantra: "O *iḍā*, enjoy our portion; make the cows swell, quicken the horses; you are the mistress of the increase of wealth—grant us of that, give us of that; may we partake of that portion of yours. (Darśa: Hotṛ) "May we be whole-bodied, whole-limbed, having all heroes, having all men," or "having all men, having all men. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

AśvSS 1.8/1: Having performed the purification, they proceed with the after-offerings (*anuyāja*). (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.8/2: Having placed his joined palms over the sacrificial grass strewn around the altar, he pours water [into them]; that is the *mārjana* (purification). (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.8/3:
The after-offerings are addressed to the gods and others. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
AśvSS 1.8.4: [The verses] have their word-breaks removed.
(Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.8.5: There are three [sets].
(Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.8.6: Being prompted one by one, he performs the *yajati* offering. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
"May the divine *barhis* partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining wealth.
May the divine *narāśaṃsa* partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining wealth.

May the divine Agni Sviṣṭakṛt—the giver of good riches, the delightful sage, whose thoughts are true, the sacrificing priest, the invoker of the invoker—O Agni, those gods whom you have sacrificed to and whom you have gratified, they have rejoiced in your office as Hotṛ. Send this sacrifice, which has won the prize and goes to the gods, to heaven among the gods. And you, O Agni, having become the Sviṣṭakṛt and the Hotṛ, partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining wealth; say 'Namas' and accept [the offering]," thus he says without pausing.
(Darśa: Hotṛ) AsvSS_1.9/1a:

Having been prompted for the *sūktavāka*, [the Hotṛ recites]: "This has become auspicious for Heaven and Earth; we have attained the *sūktavāka* and the word of homage. May we succeed in this hymn. O Agni, you are the speaker of the hymn. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
At the hearing of Heaven and Earth: "May those two, the Heaven and Earth, full of favor for you, O sacrificer, be present at this sacrifice.
May they, the source of joy, the givers of life, the tireless, the unassailable, the wide-pastures, create safety. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

AsvSS_1.9/1c: Having recited "vṛṣṭidyāvā rītyāpā śambhuvau mayobhuvā ūrjasvatī payasvatī sūpacaraṇā ca svadhicaraṇā ca tayor āvidi," and having paused, he should designate the deity with the first case-ending and continue: "They have accepted this oblation; they have caused it to increase; they have made it great and more excellent. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AsvSS_1.9/2:
The subsequent [formulas] are in the same manner. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
AsvSS_1.9/3: "They have performed; they have performed," according to the circumstances. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AsvSS_1.9/4:

That which pertains to the *upāṃśu* [offering] has been stated. (Darśa: Hotṛ) AsvSS_1.9/5a: Having recited up to the end of the *āvāpika* [section]: "The gods who drink the clarified butter have enjoyed the clarified butter; they have increased; they have made it greater and more glorious. By means of the *agnihotra*, this oblation has been enjoyed; they have increased; they have made it greater and more glorious."

(Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.9/5b: "In this divine *hotrā* that leads to the gods, may he prosper. Having addressed [the sacrificer] by name—saying "this sacrificer, so-and-so, so-and-so"—he should whisper the two names in the presence of his guru. He prays for long life; he prays for abundance of offspring; he prays for increase of wealth. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

He prays for a dwelling among his kinsmen; he prays for the subsequent sacrifice to the gods; he prays for the further preparation of the oblation; he prays for the celestial abode; he prays for everything dear. (Darśa:

AsvSS 1.9/5d) Whatever he prays for with this oblation, may that be successful for him in this world; may the gods grant it to him; may the divine Agni protect it from the gods, and we, as men, [protect it] from Agni. (Darśa: AsvSS 1.9/5e) May both Heaven and Earth protect us from distress—both our sacrifice and our wealth.
"Your path is this; this is homage to the gods. (Darśa:

Hotṛ) When prompted for the *śamyu-vākā*, he says, "That of Śamyo we choose," like an invitatory verse (*anuvākyā*), but without the syllable *oṃ*. (Darśa: Hotṛ) The Adhvaryu hands the Veda to him. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
He should take hold of it with the formula: "Thou art the Veda; may I obtain the Veda. (Darśa:

Hotṛ) Having stood up with the verse, "Upward with life," and having sat down behind the Gārhapatya fire, they sacrifice with clarified butter to Soma, Tvaṣṭṛ, the wives of the gods, and Agni Gṛhapati.
(Darśa: Hotṛ)

AsvSS_1.10/5: “May you swell; may the milks meet you; may the strengths meet you; may Tvaṣṭṛ, the foremost, [come] here; that fourth of ours, the nourisher of wealth; may the desiring wives of the gods protect us”—these two [verses], and “Agni is the Hotṛ, the lord of the house, the king; Agni is the bearer of oblations, our ageless father”—these are the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings.
AsvSS_1.10/6: Now, one who desires offspring should sacrifice to Rākā, Sinīvālī, and Kuhū before the sacrifice to Gṛhapati.
*Rākām ahaṃ sinīvālīṃ kuhūm aham*— these two pairs are the *yājyā* and *anuvākyā* verses [for the Hotṛ at the Darśa sacrifice].
*Kuhūm ahaṃ suvṛtaṃ vidmāpasaṃ asmin yajñe suhavāṃ johavīmi | Sā no dadātu śravaṇaṃ pitṝṇāṃ tasyā ete devi haviṣā vidhema ||*
"Kuhū, the wife of the gods and of immortality, may she hear our invocation of this oblation. (The Hotṛ at the Darśa sacrifice): "May she bestow abundant wealth upon the giver;

may she grant increase of riches to the sacrificer. Thus he should have clarified butter placed upon the palm of his hand. Having invoked the *iḍā*, he should consume it all. (At the Darśa sacrifice, as per Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 1.10/9):
There may or may not be the *śamyuvāka* recitation. (The Hotṛ at the Darśa sacrifice).

Having handed over the *veda* to his wife, the *hotṛ* or the *adhvaryu* should cause her to recite: "Thou art the *veda*; thou art acquisition; may I acquire. Thou art action; thou art the instrument; thou art performance. Thou art the gathering; thou art the gatherer; may I gather. May the *veda* grant me wealth—abounding in ghee, well-established, thousandfold, and vigorous.
(Darśa: Hotṛ) "He whom many depend upon, who is the controller of people..."
"May I obtain him; may I obtain offspring; for the sake of desire, I take hold of you. (Darśa:
Hotṛ) If she desires offspring, she should touch the navel region with the head of the *veda*. (Darśa:
Hotṛ) Then he should untie her yoke-thong with the mantra: "I release you from the noose of Varuṇa. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
AśvSS 1.11/4: Having placed that [cord] double the length of the Gārhapatya fire-altar with its loops facing east, he places blades of *vedatṛṇa* grass upon it with their tips pointing north.
AśvSS 1.11/5: To the east [of the cord], he places a full vessel so that it touches the *vedatṛṇa* grass.

AśvSS 1.11/6: Having touched it, he should cause [the sacrificer] to recite: "Thou art full; mayest thou be full for me. Thou art well-filled; mayest thou be well-filled for me. Thou art existent; mayest thou be existent for me. Thou art all; mayest thou be all for me. Thou art imperishable; mayest thou not perish for me."

(Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.11/7a: Then, while pouring water from the full vessel toward the direction of the husband, or while she is pouring it, he makes her recite: "May the gods and the officiating priests purify me in the eastern direction; may the months and the ancestors purify me in the southern direction; may the houses and the cattle purify me in the western direction. AśvSS 1.11/7b:

"May the waters, the plants, and the trees purify me in the northern direction; may the sacrifice, the year, and Prajāpati purify me in the upward direction—may they purify me! Or [he says] simply, "May they purify me!"
(Darśa:

Hotṛ) Now, having placed her upturned joined palms beneath the cord and pouring out the full vessel over his own left [hand], he should cause her to recite: "May I not scatter away my offspring, you who are our companions;
I pour you into the ocean; drink your own portion. (Darśa: Hotṛ)

Having first taken up Veda-grass, and spreading it continuously without shaking it, he goes from the Gārhapatya fire to the Āhavanīya fire with his left hand, reciting: "Stretching the thread, follow the light of the atmosphere.

Having set aside the remainder [of the grass] and standing to the west-north of the Āhavanīya fire, he should take [ghee] from the pot with the *sruva* spoon and offer all the expiations (*sarva-prāyaścitta*) with mantras ending in *svāhā*, provided that [the expiation] was not already recited in the mantra.
(Darśa:
Hotṛ) Whatever [the Hotṛ] may sacrifice, even when not prompted by a *praisha*, it is likewise [done] elsewhere. (Darśa:
Hotṛ) Being thus [prepared], he performs the indistinct (*avyakta*) oblations, the placing of fuel, and the standing in attendance. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
AśvSS 1.11/13a: *Ayāś cāgne 'nabhiśastīś ca satyam it tvam ayā asi | ayāsā vayasā kṛto 'yāsan havyam ūhiṣe yā no dhehi bheṣajaṃ svāhā.* (Darśa: Hotṛ) AśvSS 1.11/13b:
With the two verses beginning *ato devā avantu naḥ*, with the *vyāhṛtis*, and with the utterances: *bhūḥ svāhā*, *bhuvaḥ svāhā*, *svaḥ svāhā*, and *bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā*. (Darśa: Hotṛ)
Having offered the oblation and completed the rite with the *saṃsthājapa*, he should lie down; then, having gone out to a sacred bathing place (*tīrtha*), there is no further restriction.
(The *hotṛ* at the *darśa*) "Om and my voice, and my tone, and the sacrifice, and your approach, and homage.
Whatever in you is deficient, for that [I offer]; whatever in you is redundant, for that [I offer]—homage! This is the *saṃsthājapa*. (The *hotṛ* at the *darśa*)
Thus for the Hotṛ. (Darśa:
Hotṛ) Now for the Brahman.
(General Brahman)
AśvSS 1.12/2: The duties of the Hotṛ priest, sipping water for purification, wearing the sacrificial thread, and rules of purity [apply].
(General rule for the Brahman priest) AśvSS 1.12/3: These are constant for all rites, whether the sacred fires are stationary or being moved to the south.
(Brahman: General Rule) AśvSS 1.12.4: In that case, whichever direction the sacrificial grass, the altar, or the pathway face is considered to be the east.
(Brahman: General Rule)
In the case of ritual actions not accompanied by mantras, there is an option regarding standing or sitting.
One should stand during those oblations which do not involve the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*.
(Brahman: general) He should sit elsewhere.
(Brahman: general)
Having circumambulated the Āhavanīya fire with the tips of all the fingers and the thumb together, he should sit down on *kuśa* grass to the south.
(General rule for the Brahman priest: Having sat down, he should mutter: "Bṛhaspati is the Brahman; he shall sit upon the seat of the Brahman. O Bṛhaspati, protect the sacrifice."
(Brahman: General) This is the recitation of the *brahman* formula for all sacrificial procedures involving fire where [the Brahman] is seated.
(Brahman: General)
When [the Adhvaryu] has sat down, he gives permission [to the Brahman].
(General rule for the Brahman:

Having heard [the Adhvaryu say], "O Brahman, I shall lead forward the waters," and having murmured, "bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, impelled by Bṛhaspati," he should grant permission everywhere with the words, "oṃ, lead forward."
(Brahman: General) The instructions are according to the specific ritual action.
(Brahman: General)
The *praṇava* and so forth are to be recited aloud. (General rule for the Brahman priest) Or else, [the *praṇava*] may be recited aloud after [the mantra].
(Brahman:
General) From this point forward, he remains seated with his speech restrained until the call for the preparer of the oblation (*haviṣkṛt*).
(Brahman: General)
Up to the wiping of the animal [victim], [the Brahman remains seated].
(Brahman:
General) Up to the *subrahmaṇyā* call, [he remains seated] during the Soma sacrifice, as well as at the Gharma offering and subsequent rites, and from the *atipraiṣa* onwards.
(Brahman: general) From the morning litany up until the Antaryāma cup.
(Brahman: general)
AsvSS_1.12/20: At each pressing, [the portion] up to the *iḍā* belongs to Harivat.
(General rule for the Brahman priest) AsvSS_1.12/21: In the *stotra*s, [the Brahman's duties] begin with the *atisarjana* and continue until the *vaṣaṭ*-call.
(Brahman:
General) [The Brahman should remain seated] until the conclusion of the *pavamāna* chants.
(Brahman: General)
And whatever [is performed] accompanied by a mantra;
(General Brahman) the remainder belongs to the Hotṛ.
(Brahman: general) And there is also the occurrence of an offense.
(Brahman: general)
But wherever the fire is carried forward—even if it is accompanied by the Soma sacrifice—from that point onward there is the restraint of speech.
(General rule for the Brahman priest) Walking to the south, he recites the hymn beginning with "The swift one, sharpening... (*āśuḥ śiśānaḥ*).
(Brahman: General) Having completed [the sacrifice], the sitting down and so forth are as previously stated.
(Brahman: General)
But at the *praṇayana* of the Soma sacrifice, there is no chanting by the Brahman priest.
(General rule for the Brahman:
elsewhere, he should release his speech only sparingly, speak little, and keep his mind fixed on the sacrifice.)

(Brahman: General) In the event of an inversion, an omission, a forgotten mantra, or a ritual act that has been performed incorrectly— or upon noticing it after it has already been declared— one should bend the knee and offer an oblation.
If [the fire] is from the *ṛc*, [he offers] "bhūḥ" in the *gārhapatya* fire; if from the *yajus*, "bhuvaḥ" in the *dakṣiṇa* fire;
and in the case of *soma* sacrifices, in the *āgnīdhrīya* fire.
(Brahman: General) He says "Sāmataḥ svar" over the Āhavanīya fire; or, if [the fire] is not recognized from any side, he says "bhūr bhuvaḥ svar" over the Āhavanīya itself.
(Brahman: General)

Before the *prājya* oblations, he should press down the charcoal that has emerged outside the enclosing sticks with the handle of the *sruva* ladle, saying: "May neither the heat nor the sacrifice burn me; may the lord of the sacrifice not burn me.
Homage be to you as you come, homage, O Rudra, as you go away.
Homage where you sit down."
(Brahman: General) "Do not harm so-and-so! Do not harm so-and-so!"—thus the Adhvaryu and the Sacrificer [should recite] toward each direction if [the danger] is from the east;
the Brahman and the Sacrificer if it is from the south.
The *hotṛpatnī* and the sacrificer [are seated] behind;
the *āgnīdhra* and the sacrificer [are seated] to the north.
(General rule for the Brahman)
Then he should throw it into the fire with the mantra: "I take up the sacrifice from the lap of Nirṛti; I entrust it to the gods, being wise.
Grant me good offspring for a hundred winters; O gods, bestow protection upon me here.
(General Brahman)

He should offer an oblation to it with the verse: "The thousand-horned bull, Jātavedas, whose back is the *stoma*, who is full of ghee and fair-faced—may he not harm us when harmed; I place you [within me]; I do not abandon you. Grant us prosperity in cattle and prosperity in heroes, svāhā!
(General Brahman).

He looks at the *prāśitra* as it is being brought forward, saying: "I gaze upon you with the eye of Mitra. He receives it with his joined palms, saying: "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I receive you.
Having received it with his joined palms, he places it down, saying: "I set you on the navel of the Earth, in the lap of Aditi."
(Darśa:
Brahman) Having placed the stalk of *kuśa* grass with its tip pointing eastward upon other *kuśa* grass, he should eat it without chewing it between his thumb and ring finger, saying:
"I eat thee with the mouth of Agni, with the face of Bṛhaspati."

(Darśa: Brahman) Having sipped water, or having sipped again, he should touch his navel with the formula: "By truth I sprinkle thee; may those deities who are within the waters pacify this [impurity]; do not harm my sight, hearing, or breaths; I place thee in the belly of Indra. Having washed the vessel for the *prāśitra* portion, he pours water toward himself three times with this [formula].
(Darśa: Brahman) Having performed the ritual sprinkling, he should place the portion for the Brahman in this [spot].
(Darśa: Brahman)
AśvSS 1.13/3: [The Brahman] places the sacrificer’s portion on the kuśa grass behind [the fire].

AśvSS 1.13/4: He should gaze upon the Anvāhārya rice with the formula: "Thou art the portion of Prajāpati; thou art full of vigor, full of milk, and imperishable. Do not look at me in this world nor in that world."
(Darśa:

Brahman) "Protect my out-breath and in-breath; for desire, I take thee"—saying this, without touching [the vessel] but smelling it, he should take the remainder with his thumb and ring finger and place it in the portion for the Brahman.
(Darśa: Brahman)

Having heard [the call], "O Brahman, we shall set forth," Bṛhaspati, acting as the Brahman priest, sat upon the seat of the Brahman. [The Adhvaryu says: "O Bṛhaspati, you have protected the sacrifice; protect the sacrifice, protect the lord of the sacrifice, and protect me. (Darśa:
Brahman) Having murmured, "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, impelled by Bṛhaspati," he should authorize the fuel-stick with the words, "Om, be established! (pratiṣṭhā).
When the officiating priests have finished their work, he should offer all the expiatory oblations (*sarvaprayāścitta*); the others should touch him, or the Hotṛ priest.
(Darśa: Brahman) AśvSS 1.13.8: [or] the Hotṛ.
(Regarding the Darśa sacrifice:
Brahman) The daily oblation for these two [fires] is performed [at this time].
(Regarding the Darśa sacrifice: Brahman)
AsvSS_1.13/10: They perform the worship with the recitation common to all the sacrificial sessions; they perform [it] repeatedly.
(The Brahman at the New Moon sacrifice) AsvSS_2.1/1: The Iṣṭi, Animal, and Soma sacrifices are taught by means of the Full Moon sacrifice.
(General Rules) AśvSS 2.1/2: With these [oblations], one should sacrifice on either the new moon day or the full moon day.
(General Rules)
A Kṣatriya may also perform the Agnihotra sacrifice.
(General rules) At other times, he should offer food to an ascetic Brāhmaṇa.
(General Rules) AśvSS 2.1.5: One who is devoted to the practice of *ṛta* and *satya*, and who presses the Soma, should always offer oblations.
(General Rules)

AsvSS 2.1/6: When there are many [deities], the assignment of many [verses] follows the principle of immediate succession. (General Rules) AsvSS 2.1/7: However, there are two *yājyā*s and two *anuvākyā*s [for each deity].
(General Rules) AŚvSS_2.1/8: [The rites] are to be performed constantly when no specific instruction is seen.
(General Rules)
The establishment of the sacred fires (*agnyādheya*).
[It should be performed] under the asterisms of Kṛttikā, Rohiṇī, Mṛgaśiras, the two Phalgunīs, Viśākhā, or the two Uttaraproṣṭhapadās.
(Agnyādheya) AśvSS 2.1.11: At one of these [times].
(Agnyādheya)
A Brāhmaṇa should establish the sacred fires at the full-moon festival in spring. A Kṣatriya, a Vaiśya, and those of mixed caste may do so in summer, the rainy season, or autumn.
(Agnny-ādheya) AśvSS 2.1/14: One may establish the fires in whichever season one chooses.
(Agnny-ādheya)
AśvSS 2.1.15: One who is about to sacrifice with Soma need not inquire about the season nor the lunar mansion.
(The Establishment of the Fires) AśvSS 2.1.16: He should fetch the two kindling woods from an Aśvattha tree that has grown from within a Śamī tree, without looking at them.

(On the Establishment of the Sacred Fires): "The Aśvattha tree which has grown upon the Śamī tree, together with thee—I bring that to thee with the sacred word (brahman), along with sacrifices and emblems. Thus ends the establishment of the fires with the full oblation.
(On the Establishment of the Sacred Fires) AśvSS 2.1/18: But if they should perform the *iṣṭi* sacrifices [at this time].
(On the Establishment of the Sacred Fires)
At the first [verse]: "Agni, Agni Pavamāna. (The Establishment of the Fires) [The verses:
"O Agni, you purify the lives"; "O Agni, you who are skillful, purify yourself."

(Agnyādheya) AśvSS 2.1/21: When it is stated, "He is the bearer of oblations, Agni the Hotṛ, the domestic priest," these are the two *saṃyājyā* verses for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering; one should follow them with the verses belonging to the *sauviṣṭakṛta*.
(Agnyādheya) AśvSS 2.1/22: In all cases where there is the arrival of a deity, there is the displacement of the obligatory [deities].
(Agnyādheya)

AśvSS 2.1.23: Those [oblations] which are for the *sviṣṭakṛt* and those between the two *ājyabhāgas* take its place. (The Establishment of the Fires) AśvSS 2.1.24: This is the common rule for all classes.
(On the second day: The two [verses] containing the word *vṛdh*.
"Agni the purifier, Agni the bright; may he, the purifier, O shining one, O Agni, with thy purifying luster; Agni, most pure in his vows; up, O Agni, thy pure [flames]. (AśvSS 2.1/25)
(On the *agnyādheya*):

"Sāhvān viśvā abhiyujaḥ, agnim īḷe purohitam" are the two *saṃyājyā* verses. In the second [offering], he inserts two *sāmidhenī* verses before the penultimate one: "pṛthupājā amartyaḥ" and another [verse].

(Agnyādheya) AśvSS 2.1/27: When the word *dhāyye* has been uttered, one should respond with these two verses containing the word *puṣṭi*: "May he obtain wealth through Agni" and "Gayasphana, the remover of disease.
*Agnīṣoma*, *Indrāgni*, and *Viṣṇu* are the optional [deities].
(On the establishment of the sacred fires) AsvSS 2.1/28: Aditi.
(On the establishment of the sacred fires) AsvSS 2.1/29: And you, O Aditi, the great, the mighty mother of those who observe holy vows, the consort of Ṛta—we invoke her for our protection.
"Aditi, who possesses great dominion, who is undecaying, far-reaching, providing excellent protection, and a good leader.
(Regarding the *agnyādheya*:
"O Agni, kindled! and "O Agni, these [oblations]!")—it is stated that the two *virāj* verses are the *saṃyājyās*; one should understand that these three [verses] are to be used.
(Agnyādheya) AśvSS 2.1/31: Only the first and the last [of the verses] should be used.
(Agnihotra)
Or rather, [the first two verses] are [the dhāyyās]. (Agnny-ādheya) In that case, these two Virāj verses themselves shall be the dhāyyās.
(Agnny-ādheya)
AśvSS 2.1.34: One should understand that these variations [of the ritual] are based on the Vairāja system.
(The Establishment of the Sacred Fires) AśvSS 2.1.35: For twelve nights after the establishment of the fires, they must be kept burning without interruption.
(On the establishment of the sacred fires:
But for those whose prosperity has utterly departed, [the fire should be established].
(On the establishment of the sacred fires)

AśvSS 2.2/1: At the time of the formal abandonment [of the fires], having kindled the *gārhapatya* fire in the afternoon and having brought the *dakṣiṇa* fire—from a family of *viś* (commoners) or from one who is wealthy—some say it should be from those of a single origin; or, having kindled it while it is still maintained, or having churned it from a fire-drill (*araṇi*) that possesses them, he should draw out the blazing *āhavanīya* fire from the *gārhapatya*.
AśvSS 2.2/2: "I draw thee, a god, for the gods, with glory," saying this, he should draw it out. (The Agnihotra)

AsvSS_2.2/3: While being lifted up, he should pour it forth with the mantra: "Lift me up from whatever evil I have done unknowingly or knowingly; from whatever sin has been committed by day, protect me, having been lifted up, from all that. (Agnihotra) AsvSS_2.2/4: "I offer the immortal oblation into the immortal [fire] on the earth, the fire in the womb of immortality."

"By that [offering], may I conquer infinite desire; Prajāpati was the first to conquer this; Agni in Agni, svāhā!"—with these words he should place [the oblation] while facing the sun. (Agnihotra) AsvSS 2.2/5: Thus in the morning, when it has dawned, [he places it] while facing the end [of the night].
(Agnihotra) AsvSS 2.2/6: But he should offer [the oblation] with the verse, "Whatever of the night... (rātryā yad ana...). (Agnihotra)

AsvSS_2.2/7: From this point forward, for one who has established the sacred fires, the observance of the vow lasts until the oblation is offered. (Agnihotra) AsvSS_2.2/8: And for one who offers the oblation before sunrise, it lasts until sunrise. (Agnihotra) AsvSS_2.2/9: The oblation is offered after sunset. (Agnihotra)

AśvSS 2.2.10: Water-sipping (*ācamana*) is obligatory. AśvSS 2.2.11: Having murmured, "With *ṛta* and *satya* I sprinkle thee around," he should sprinkle around [the fire] three times each, taking up water again and again. (The Agnihotra) AśvSS 2.2.12:
If there is no interval [between the acts], there is an option. (The Agnihotra)

It is understood that the southern [fire] comes first; for this southern fire is the father of the fires, the Gārhapatya is the son, and the Āhavanīya is the grandson. Therefore, one should sprinkle around [the fires] in this manner. One should carry an unbroken stream of water from the Gārhapatya to the Āhavanīya with the mantra: "Stretching the thread, go forth toward the light of the atmosphere. Having sat down behind the Gārhapatya, one should push the embers toward the north with the mantra: "You are makers of well-offered oblations; you shall perform the well-offered oblation. (Agnihotra)

AśvSS 2.2.16: Upon these [hearth-stones], he should place the *agnihotra* oblation; having placed it, he should say, "It has been placed, it has been placed, it has been placed, it is cold. AśvSS 2.2.17: Or [he may offer it] with the formula: "The footprint of Iḷā, rich in ghee, moving and unmoving; O Jātavedas, enjoy this oblation. May there be nourishment for me from those seven domestic animals that possess all forms.
AśvSS 2.2.18: He should not place curd upon [the fire]; some say he should place it. (Regarding the *agnihotra*)

AsvSS 2.3/1: The daily oblation is performed with milk. (Agnihotra) AsvSS 2.3/2: Gruel, boiled rice, curd, and clarified butter are for those desiring a village, those desiring the enjoyment of food, those desiring sensory power, and those desiring splendor, respectively. (Agnihotra) AsvSS 2.3/3:
Once the milk has been placed on the fire, one should ignite it [with a flame]. (Agnihotra)
AsvSS 2.3/4: Without placing it on the fire, he should add curd [to the ghee], saying: "O Agni, do not take away his splendor. (Agnihotra) AsvSS 2.3/5:
He should sprinkle [the mixture] with the *sruva* ladle, or he may not; [if he does, he says]: "Peace be unto him; you are immortality. (Agnihotra) AsvSS 2.3/6:
There should be no transposition between these two [acts]. (Agnihotra)

(Regarding the Agnihotra: He should carry [the fire] around it while it is burning again, saying three times: "The Rakṣas is excluded; the enemies are excluded. (Regarding the Agnihotra: Drawing [the embers] as if toward the edge, he should take them out toward the north, placing them down with the words: "For the sky thee! For the intermediate space thee! For the earth thee! (Regarding the Agnihotra: Having released the embers with the words, "You have made a good offering; you have performed a good offering," he should heat the *sruk* and *sruva* ladles, saying: "The Rakṣas is burnt away; the enemies are burnt away. The Rakṣas is scorched; the enemies are scorched."
AśvSS 2.3.10: Having placed the *sruva* ladle to the north of the pot, he should give the command: "Om, let me draw up [the ghee]. AśvSS 2.3.11:

The one who has established the sacred fires, having sipped water (*ācamya*), having passed behind the altar (*vedi*) and sat down to the south, and having heard this, should give the command: "Om, let me draw up. AśvSS 2.3.12:
Having been given permission, he should draw up the *sruva* ladle until it is full, saying: "Bhūr iḷā, bhuva iḷā, svar iḷā, vṛdha iḷā. (Agnihotra)
Agniya. One who desires the prosperity of his sons should fill the *agniya* vessel completely for the eldest son.
(Agnihotra) He should pour it out full toward whichever son of his is dear to him.

(Agnihotra) Having touched the pot, the fuel-stick, and the ladle, and having carried them over the *gārhapatya* fire, he should place them on *kuśa* grass near the *āhavanīya* fire at the level of his nose. Then, bending his knees, he should offer the fuel-stick with the formula: "I place thee, O silver-colored brick, whose light is Agni, as the night; svāhā! (Agnihotra)

(Agnihotra) AśvSS 2.3/16: Having placed a fuel-stick on the fire and touched water while reciting, "Thou art lightning; light up my sin in the fire; faith," he should offer the blazing stick at a distance of two finger-breadths [from the flame] with the mantra: "bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ om agnir jyotir jyotir agniḥ svāhā.
(Agnihotra)
Having offered the first oblation and set it down on *kuśa* grass, he should gaze at the *gārhapatya* fire, saying: "Grant me cattle.
(Agnihotra) Then he offers the second oblation silently, in greater quantity, without letting it touch the first, either to the east, to the north, or to the north-east.
(Agnihotra) In all silent offerings, he should meditate mentally upon Prajāpati. (Agnihotra)

AsvSS 2.3.20: Having left the greatest portion in the *sruva* ladle, having shaken it three times [over the fire], and having wiped it, he wipes it on the roots of the *kuśa* grass with the formula, "For the animals, thee.

(Agnihotra) AsvSS 2.3.21: To the south of those [roots], he makes his fingers palm upwards; wearing the sacrificial cord over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvītī*), he does so silently or with the formula, "Svadhā to the ancestors!
(Agnihotra) AsvSS 2.3.22: Having poured out water. (Agnihotra)
AśvSS 2.3.23: "Thou art rain; cut off my evil; faith is in the waters," having touched water thus. (Agnihotra) AśvSS 2.3.24:

One who has established the sacred fires (*āhitāgni*) should consecrate [the fire] with a mantra. (Agnihotra) AśvSS 2.3.25: Having recited the formula for the establishment of the fires, he should place a fuel-stick [with the words]: "By that seer, by that Brahman, by that deity—like Aṅgiras, sit thou firm. (Agnihotra)
AśvSS 2.3/26: With the verse, "Tā asya sūdadohasaḥ," he offers the first oblation.

(Agnihotra) AśvSS 2.3/27: Having performed the worship (*upasthāna*), he should desire the second [oblation] while gazing [at the fire], saying: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! May I be rich in offspring through my children, rich in heroes through my men, and rich in nourishment through my possessions.
(Agnihotra) AśvSS 2.3/28: And with verses addressed to Agni. (Agnihotra)
AśvSS 2.3/29: [He offers] with the three verses beginning "O Agni, you purify the lives... (Agnihotra). AśvSS 2.4/1:
Year after year. (Agnihotra) AśvSS 2.4/2:
On the full-moon day, he himself should offer either barley-gruel or milk. (Agnihotra)
AśvSS 2.4/3: [The rule applies] to the officiating priests; at one time or the other. (Agnihotra) AśvSS 2.4/4: Or a pupil [may eat it].
(Agnihotra) AśvSS 2.4/5: Having touched water and having turned toward the north, he should consume [the remains]. (Agnihotra)
Or, having offered in the two other [fires] (the *āhavanīya* and *gārhapatya*), he consumes [the remains of the oblation]:
"I consume thee for long life," he says for the first [portion]; "For the eating of food, thee," he says for the latter. (Agnihotra)
Having silently placed a fuel-stick on the Gārhapatya fire, he offers with the words: "To Agni Gṛhapati, svāhā! (Agnihotra).
The subsequent [offering] is constant.
Having silently placed a fuel-stick on the Dakṣiṇāgni fire, he offers with the words: "To Agni Saṃveśapati, svāhā! (Agnihotra).
Or [he may offer] with the formula: "To Agni, the eater of food, the lord of food, svāhā!
(Agnihotra, ĀśvSS 2.4.11). The latter [formula] is obligatory.

(Agnihotra, ĀśvSS 2.4.13): Then, having washed it with *kuśa* grass, he should pour out four full [ladles] toward the northeast, saying: "To the seasons, svāhā! To the quarters, svāhā! To the seven seers, svāhā! To other people, svāhā!"
On the fifth [occasion], on the ground in a place strewn with *kuśa* grass, he offers with: "I offer nectar to Agni Vaiśvānara; svāhā!
On the sixth, behind the *gārhapatya* fire, he offers with: "I offer breath into nectar; I offer nectar into breath; svāhā!
(Agnihotra) Having heated it, he should place it within the altar (*vedī*). (Agnihotra)
AśvSS 2.4.16: He should give [the wood] to the attendant.
AśvSS 2.4.17: Having gone around the front of the Āhavanīya fire, he should place three fuel-sticks each time while standing facing north.
AśvSS 2.4.18: The first [stick] is accompanied by a mantra.
AśvSS 2.4.19: [He offers] with "Shine in the Āhavanīya," "Shine in the Gārhapatya," and "Shine in the Dakṣiṇa.
(Agnihotra) AśvSS 2.4.20: The sprinkling around has been explained. (Agnihotra) AśvSS 2.4.21: With those two [verses], the sweeping around [of the fires is performed]. (Agnihotra)
AśvSS 2.4.22: [The Agnihotra is performed] before the sprinkling around [the fire]. AśvSS 2.4.23: Likewise in the morning.
AśvSS 2.4.24: At the break of dawn, when it has become light, or after the sun has risen.

With the formula, "By means of truth and cosmic order, thee," he sprinkles water around [the fire]. With the formula, "Om, I shall lead thee forth," he grants permission. With the formula, "Thee, the tawny one, having the sun as thy light, the brick of the day, I place; svāhā! he lays on the fuel-stick. With the formula, "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ om; the sun is the light, the light is the sun; svāhā," he performs the oblation and the wiping. (Agnihotra) AsvSS_2.5/1:
When about to depart on a journey, having kindled the fires, sipped water, and stepped across [the altar], he worships them.
To the Āhavanīya fire: "O Śaṃsyapaśu, protect my cattle. To the Gārhapatya fire: "O Naya, protect my progeny. To the Dakṣiṇa fire: "O Atharvan, protect my nourishment."
He should look at the *gārhapatya* and *āhavanīya* fires, saying: "O Mitra and Varuṇa, protect these houses of mine for me—you two—unimpaired and undisturbed; may Pūṣan guard them until our return.
Having returned as before and having gone around the *āhavanīya* fire keeping it to his right, he worships it, saying:
"O Jātavedas, whatever name was first given to me by my father and mother, O Agni..."
"Maintain the truth until my return; I shall bear your name as the foremost. (Agnihotra) AśvSS 2.5.4:
He should depart without looking back, reciting the hymn "Do not bow down to me" (mā praṇama). (Agnihotra) AśvSS 2.5.5:
He should release his speech at a distance from the fires. (Agnihotra)

AsvSS 2.5/6: Having descended onto the path, [he recites]: "May the path of my father be ever easy to traverse. (Agnihotra) AsvSS 2.5/7: If one who has not yet established the sacred fires should go on a journey, [he should say]:
"Remaining right here, O Agni, I sustain you who are there with my heart, my speech, and my mind."

"May you not abandon me while I am out of sight; I worship you with the Vaiśvānara light"—having thus worshipped the fires in each direction, he returns with the verse, "We have come to the path. Then, with hands joined and speech restrained, having heard that the fires are blazing, he approaches and gazes at the Āhavanīya fire.
Bringing [offerings] at all times with an unailing mind, O Agni, may we, your neighbors, not come to harm.
Let there be homage to you, the bountiful one; homage to you, who delight in the sacrificial seat.
"O Agni, adorn your bodies; unite me with wealth.
(Agnihotra) Having placed fuel-sticks upon the fires, he worships the Āhavanīya fire [with the verse]:
"O Jātavedas, bearing our names as if wearing two garments, may we move about."
"May they bear [thee] for skill and for life, according to our bodies, O Jātavedas. (Agnihotra) AśvSS 2.5/11:
Then he should place fuel-sticks upon [the fire]. (Agnihotra) AśvSS 2.5/12a:
Upon the Āhavanīya [fire]: "The Agni who possesses all knowledge, the best finder of wealth for us..."
"O Agni, sovereign ruler, bestow splendor and power; svāhā!
[He offers] into the Gārhapatya fire: "This Agni is the master of the house, the Gārhapatya, the best winner of wealth for his progeny.
O Agni, master of the house, bestow splendor and power; svāhā!"
To the south: "This Agni Purīṣya is wealthy and the increaser of prosperity. (Agnihotra, ĀśvSS 2.5/12b):
"O Agni Purīṣya, bestow upon us splendor and power, svāhā!
He should look at the Gārhapatya and Āhavanīya fires [with the mantra]: "O Mitra and Varuṇa, you two have protected these houses of mine."

"Pūṣan has protected these [fires] from being destroyed or displaced until our return. (Agnihotra) Having returned by the same way he went, having swept around [the fires], and having sat down to the north of the sacrificial ground (*vihāra*), he should release his speech with the words: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ. (Agnihotra)

AśvSS 2.5/14: Having been away for more than ten nights, one should offer clarified butter taken four times with the mantra: “May the mind, the light, enjoy my clarified butter; may it restore this interrupted sacrifice.
Those dawns that have been sacrificed and those that have not been sacrificed, I join together with the oblation of ghee, svāhā! (Agnihotra) AśvSS 2.5/15:
And [this same rite applies] when the Agnihotra has not been offered. (Agnihotra)
AsvSS 2.5/16: Some [prescribe] a supplementary oblation for each [error]. (Agnihotra) AsvSS 2.5/17:

He should look at his house—even one who has not established the sacred fires—with the mantra: "O House, do not fear; may prosperity be yours; may you multiply among us; and may no harm come to your master.
Then he should enter with the mantra: "I enter the house, well-disposed, rich in heroes, possessing heroes, and full of brave sons."
"Carrying the earth, sprinkling ghee—may I enter among them with a well-disposed mind," he says, looking back three times with the words, "Auspicious, effective, for peace, for peace.

(Agnihotra) Even if it is known, they should not announce on that day anything that is false. (Agnihotra) It is understood from the tradition: "May there be safety for you; may there be safety for us"—with these words he should perform the *upasthāna* rite when departing, or every day upon returning. (Agnihotra)
AśvSS 2.6/1: On the afternoon of the new moon day, the Piṇḍapitṛyajña is performed.
AśvSS 2.6/2: One should carry a single firebrand from the Dakṣiṇāgni toward the south-east, [reciting]: "The Asuras, assuming various forms, who move about with the svadhā-call."
"May Agni drive away from this world those who bring Parāpuṇas and Nipuras. (Piṇḍapitṛyajña) All ritual acts [are directed] toward that direction.

(Piṇḍapitṛyajña) AśvSS 2.6/4: Having kindled the fires and strewn grass around both, he should place the vessels one by one to the south of the Āhavanīya fire—either facing east, north, west, or north—namely: the pot for the caru, the winnowing basket, the wooden sword, the mortar and pestle, the *sruva* ladle, the *dhruvā* ladle, the black antelope skin, the *sakṛdācchinna* grass-bundle, the fuel-stick, the stirring-spoon, and the water-pot.
(Piṇḍapitṛyajña)
AśvSS 2.6.5: Having climbed onto the post standing nearest the fire from the south, he should wipe a pot filled with rice grains.
(The Piṇḍapitṛyajña) AśvSS 2.6.6: He should set it down on the leveled ground.
(Piṇḍapitṛyajña) Having placed the mortar upon a black antelope skin, the wife should pound the other grains without separating the husks.
(Piṇḍapitṛyajña)

Having brought [the rice] and washed it once, he should cook it over the southern fire. (The Piṇḍapitṛyajña) Before the *atipraṇīta* fire has been carried forward, he should draw a line with the wooden sword (*sphya*), saying: "Struck away are the Asuras, the Rakṣasas who sit upon the altar."

(Piṇḍapitṛyajña) Having sprinkled that [ground] and having spread it once with *sakṛd-ācchinna* grass, he should set down the cooked rice from the pot after pouring clarified butter over it; or, using unstrained ghee or strained fresh butter, having placed the clarified butter in the *dhruvā* vessel, [he sets it down] to the south.
(Piṇḍapitṛyajña)
AsvSS 2.6.11: [The offerings consist of] collyrium, ointment, a mattress, and a pillow.

(The Piṇḍapitṛyajña) AsvSS 2.6.12: Wearing the sacrificial cord over the right shoulder, having added fuel to the fire, and having taken [the food] with a stirring-spoon, he should offer it according to the rules for taking portions, saying: "Svadhā! Adoration to Soma accompanied by the ancestors! Svadhā! Adoration to Agni, the bearer of the kavyas!"
In the Piṇḍapitṛyajña,
he should first sacrifice to Agni with the utterance of "svāhā," wearing the sacrificial cord over the left shoulder (yajñopavītī).
In the Piṇḍapitṛyajña.

Having thrown the stirring-spoon into the fire, wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvītī*), he should lead water three times over the line, saying: "May the fathers be purified; may the grandfathers be purified; may the great-grandfathers be purified.

(The Piṇḍapitṛyajña) Upon that [line], he should offer the rice-balls (*piṇḍa*) with his hand turned away from him, for the father, the grandfather, and the great-grandfather, saying: "This is for you, O so-and-so, and for those who follow you here."
(Regarding the Piṇḍapitṛyajña:
Gāṇagāri says that one should offer to each of those among them who are deceased, while worshipping the others visibly, because the rite is for their sake.
(Piṇḍapitṛyajña)
AśvSS 2.6.17: "One should offer to all [the ancestors]," says Tailvali, because the action is subordinate to its purpose.

AśvSS 2.6.18: "Even while some are living, one should offer only to those who have died, up to the third ancestor," says Gautama; for the efficacy of a ritual lies in its accomplishment of its intended purpose.
(Piṇḍapitṛyajña) AśvSS 2.6/19: This is a special method for those who are living and those who are deceased.
(Piṇḍapitṛyajña)
Because there is no authority over others,
he should not offer [the oblation] directly; he should not offer it to living beings.
(Piṇḍapitṛyajña) AśvSS 2.6/21: [One should not offer] to those among whom a living person intervenes.
(Piṇḍapitṛyajña)
AśvSS 2.6/22: One should offer oblations for those who are living.
(The Piṇḍapitṛyajña) AśvSS 2.6/23: For those who live by all [means], there is the offering of everything.
(Regarding the *Piṇḍapitṛyajña*):
If one does not know their names, [he should call them] "Father, Grandfather, and Great-grandfather.
(Piṇḍapitṛyajña)
AśvSS 2.7/1: He should address the scattered [remnants] with the mantra: "O fathers, rejoice here; come to your respective portions like bulls.

(The Piṇḍapitṛyajña) AśvSS 2.7/2: Turning to the left, having turned toward the north, and having sat down without breathing for as long as he is able, he should turn back and say: "The fathers have rejoiced; they have come to their respective portions like bulls."
(Piṇḍapitṛyajña) AśvSS 2.7/3: He should consume the sacrificial porridge by taking it into his breath.
(Piṇḍapitṛyajña)
AśvSS 2.7.4: The pouring out [of water] is performed daily.
(The Piṇḍapitṛyajña) AśvSS 2.7.5: "O so-and-so, anoint yourself; O so-and-so, smear yourself"—thus [he says] over the rice-balls regarding the ointment and the collyrium.

In the Piṇḍapitṛyajña, he should give a garment, or a fringe, wool, or a lock of hair; for one over fifty years of age, his own hair [is given]. He says: "O Fathers, this is your garment; O Fathers, do not yoke us to anything other than this.
(Piṇḍapitṛyajña)

Then he should pay homage to them with: "Homage to you, O fathers, for food! Homage to you, O fathers, for strength! Homage to you, O fathers, for vigor! Homage to you, O fathers, for the non-terrible! Homage to you, O fathers, for life! Homage to you, O fathers, for sap!
Svadhā to you, O fathers! Homage to you, O fathers! Homage! These are yours, O fathers; these are ours. May we be living ones here while you are living! (The Piṇḍapitṛyajña).
(Regarding the Piṇḍapitṛyajña: [He offers] with the three verses beginning "Homage! We invoke... (AśvSS 2.7/8).
Then he should dismiss them with the verse: "Depart, O Soma-loving fathers, by your ancient, deep paths" (AśvSS 2.7/9).
"Grant us wealth that is auspicious; bestow upon us riches consisting of all heroic sons.
(The Piṇḍapitṛyajña, Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 2.7.10): Having returned toward the fire, [he recites] "O Agni, [drive away] him today with hymns as one drives a horse... and so forth.
(Regarding the Piṇḍapitṛyajña:

"Whatever [sin] we have committed against the atmosphere, the earth, or the sky, or whatever [sin] we have done to harm our mother or father—may Agni Gārhapatya release me from that transgression; may he make me free from sin. Thus [he says].
