"Agni is praised in heaven, Agni is praised on earth; sing forth for Parjanya! The winds blow, the lightnings fall"—these verses, beginning with the *agnyādheya* and ending with the *upāṃśu-havis*, [are] for the Soma sacrifice and for expiations.
The cakes on one potsherd are for Anvāyātī.
(General rule) Everywhere, except for those dedicated to Varuṇa. (General rule) At the Cāturmāsya sacrifices, there is also one for Savitṛ. (General rule)
Some [teachers] say that the principal oblations are also [to be offered].

(General rule) The *pitryā* and *upasat* rites are performed with their own specific ritual procedures (*satantra*). (General rule) And the rite pertaining to the re-establishment of the sacred fires (*paunarādheyika*) is performed up until the final *anuyāja* offering. (General rule)
Alternatively, the *tantras* may be very simple.
(General rule) The *āgūḥ*, the *praṇava*, and the *vaṣaṭkāra* are always pronounced loudly.
(General rule) Likewise, at the *Āgrayaṇa* sacrifice, the first [portion] is [offered]. (General rule)
But the *praṇava* connected with the vital breath (*prāṇasaṃtata*) is to be drawn out (*āhārya*) for the *puronuvākyā*.
Likewise, the *āguḥ* and *vaṣaṭkāra* are [drawn out] for the *yājyā*.
For the *upāṃśu* [offering], the accents of the ritual procedure (*tantra*) are high.
The *mandra* tones are for the *upāṃśu* recitations.

(General rule) At the morning *vaiśvadeva* sacrifice, having been prompted, he recites the verses for kindling the fire (*agnimanthanīyāḥ*) after the place for the *sāmidhenī* verses, standing at a distance of one *pada*, and having uttered the *abhihiṅkāra*.
(Vaiśvadeva)

AśvSS 2.16.2: Having recited the half-verses of the three [verses] beginning with "abhi tvā deva savitar," "mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ," and "tvām agne puṣkarād adhi," he should pause until the formal summons (*saṃpraiṣa*).
AśvSS 2.16.3: Even in other cases, when there is no natural pause within a verse (*antarṛca*), the pause occurs at this very point.
(Cm: Vaiśvadeva) AśvSS 2.16.4: One should insert the hymn beginning with "O Agni, you slay the Atriṇ" again and again until birth [is achieved].
(Cm: Vaiśvadeva)
Having heard that [the child] has been born, one should continue the remainder with the *praṇava* immediately following.
With the remainder, one should perform the subsequent [rite].
(Cm: Vaiśvadeva) AśvSS 2.16.7:

[The Hotṛ] should begin with the half-verse, "And let the people say, 'This one has eaten with his hand,'" and conclude with the verses, "Forward the god for the feast of the gods," "By Agni is Agni kindled," "For you, O Agni, by Agni," "They have won him, the wise one," and "By means of sacrifice the gods sacrificed to the sacrifice. He should perform the concluding verse (*paridhāna*).
(Cm: Vaiśvadeva) AśvSS 2.16/8: In all cases, one should know that the final verse is the *paridhānīyā*.
(Cm: Vaiśvadeva)

AsvSS_2.16/9: There are two *dhāyyā* verses, two *virāj*s, and nine *prayāja*s; before the final one, he should insert four [verses]: "May the doors of Agni partake of the clarified butter," "May Dawn and Night, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter," "May the two divine Hotṛs, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter," and "May the three goddesses, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter.
(Cm: [this is] for the Vaiśvadeva). AsvSS_2.16/10:
Agni, Soma, Savitṛ, Sarasvatī, Pūṣan, the Maruts, the self-strong ones, the All-gods, Heaven and Earth.
(Cm: Vaiśvadeva) Ā viśvadevaṃ satpatiṃ vāmam adya savitaḥ, vāmam u śvaḥ pūṣan tava vrate vayam; śukraṃ te anyad yajataṃ te anyad; iheha vaḥ svatavasaḥ pra citram arkaṃ gṛṇate turāya. (Cm:
Vaiśvadeva)
There are nine after-offerings (*anuyāja*s). Six follow after the first: "May the goddesses, the Doors, partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of winning wealth!
May the two goddesses, Dawn and Night, partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of winning wealth!
May the two goddesses, the Delighters (*joṣṭrī*), partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of winning wealth!"*AśvSS* 2.16/12.

May the two goddesses, Ūrjā and Āhutī, partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining wealth. May the two divine Hotṛs, the gods, partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining wealth.
May the three goddesses—the three goddesses—partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining wealth.
(Cm: Vaiśvadeva) AśvSS 2.16/13:
After the *anuyājas*, the *sūktavāka*, or the *śamyuvāka*, one offers the *vājina* to the *vājins* without having invoked [them] by name.
(Cm: Vaiśvadeva)

AsvSS 2.16.14: With the verse, "May the Vājins be auspicious to us in our invocations; O Vājins, protect us in every contest for booty," he recites the *yājyā* without pausing and with his knees raised.
(Cm: Vaiśvadeva). AsvSS 2.16.15: The *anuvaṣaṭkāra* for the Vājina is "O Agni, partake! or "O Agni, partake of the Vājina."
In whatever case there is a single *sampraiṣa* but two *vaṣaṭ*-calls, one should recite the consecratory formula twice for both together; however,
there is no *āgūr* in the latter instance.
(Cm: Vaiśvadeva) Having received the portion of the *vājina* as if it were the *iḍā*, he should seek for an invitation (*upahava*). (Cm:
Vaiśvadeva)
"Adhvaryu, invite! Brahman, invite! Agnīdh, invite! (Cm:
Vaiśvadeva).
"Whatever semen of mine is spilled, or whatever enters me, or whatever is born again..."
"By that, may auspiciousness enter me; by that, make me swift.
"Of that [Soma] of yours, which has been drunk as a steed and invited, being invited myself, I partake"—with these words, he should perform the *prāṇabhakṣa* (the ritual consumption by inhalation).
(Cm: Vaiśvadeva)
In this manner, the Adhvaryu, the Brahman, and the Āgnīdhra [perform the Vaiśvadeva].
The sacrificer and the other initiated ones perform it directly.
(Cm: Vaiśvadeva) Having performed the Full Moon sacrifice, one should undertake the vows of the Cāturmāsya rites. (Cm:
Vaiśvadeva)
He should have his hair cut short.
He should have his beard shaved.
He should sleep on the ground;
he should avoid honey, meat, salt, women, and ointments. (Cm:
[this refers to] the Vaiśvadeva).
2.16/25: He should approach his wife during her season.
2.16/26: Shaving [of the head] occurs on all festival days (*parvan*).
(Cm: Vaiśvadeva) Or [the offering may be made] at the beginning and at the end. (Cm: Vaiśvadeva) AśvSS 2.16/27: At the first and the last. (Cm: Vaiśvadeva)

On the fifth full moon, [one performs] the Varuṇapraghāsa offerings. Having sat down behind the altar used for the New and Full Moon sacrifices, when prompted, he begins the rites for the carrying forward of the fire (*agnipraṇayana*).

(Cm: Varuṇapraghāsa) With the verse "pra devam devyā dhiyā" [he recites] three verses; at the half-verse of "iḷāyās tvā," he should stop at the word "deva. Sitting, he recites the first verse in a low voice (*upāṃśu*), including the *praṇava*.
(Cm: Varuṇapraghāsa) Regarding the transition from one position to another therein, having paused with the syllable *praṇava* and not exhaling, he proceeds to the next [verse].
(Cm: Varuṇapraghāsa)
"It is known from tradition that [the offering] is continuous with the breath.
While walking toward the northern fire, he recites the subsequent [verses].
(Cm: Varuṇapraghāsa) For a Kṣatriya or a Vaiśya, however, the first two [verses] are: "This strength for the great assembly... and "This one was first established here by the establishers...
(AśvSS 2.17.7). (Cm: Varuṇapraghāsa)
Having stood behind the northern altar;
however, in the case of the Soma sacrifices, it is at the high altar (*uttaravedi*).

(Cm: Varuṇapraghāsa) When the fire has been established, he should recite the two verses: "Sit down, O Hotṛ, in your own place, being wise; the Hotṛ, knowing [the rite], sits down on the Hotṛ’s seat. Having performed the two concluding rites (*paridhāna*), and having sat down in that very same seat, he should release his speech with the words: "Bhūḥ bhuvaḥ svaḥ. (Cm: Varuṇapraghāsa)
AśvSS 2.17/11: Also in other cases where he should follow while reciting [the mantra].
(Cm: regarding the Varuṇapraghāsa sacrifice) AśvSS 2.17/12: He should remain standing during the formal directions (*sampraiṣa*); in that same way, there is the release of speech.
(Cm: Varuṇapraghāsa) From the fire-churning onwards, [the ritual] is the same as that of the Vaiśvadeva.
(Cm: Varuṇapraghāsa)
AśvSS 2.17.14: But in place of the oblations beginning with the sixth, [the verses for] Indra-Agni, the Maruts, Varuṇa, and Ka [are used].

AśvSS 2.17.15: "O Indra-Agni, come with protection; you pierce Vṛtra and win booty. "In whose house the Maruts dwell like spokes or like the days. "Hear this of mine, O Varuṇa. "That I implore of you, praising with a sacred prayer. "With what [splendor] will he appear to us, the Golden Embryo? "He who arose from the existent. "O Agni"—thus the Pratiprasthātṛ [recites] the third [verse] at the *vājina* offering.
(Cm: Varuṇapraghāsa) When [the sacrifice] has been completed, they proceed to the purificatory bath (avabhṛtha).
(Cm: Varuṇapraghāsa)
In that regard, the Avabhṛtha sacrifice may be performed or not performed.
We shall explain it later; for two months, there is an animal sacrifice dedicated to Indra and Agni.
In the same manner, from that point,
follow the Sākamedha offerings.
On the preceding day, there are three offerings at each of the three pressings. In the first [offering], Agni Anīkavant is the deity.
We invoke Agni, who possesses a host, with our songs for his protection;
may he carry us across our enemies.
With his host, the bounteous one [is] for him—thus [it is said] in the subsequent [verse], where the two [verses] contain the word *vṛdhan*.

"The Maruts, the Sāṃtapanas; O Sāṃtapanas, this is the oblation; whoever, O Maruts, is ill-disposed toward us"—this [is for] the Maruts Gṛhamedhins. The subsequent [offering] consists of the two portions of clarified butter (*ājyabhāga*) as the first part and ends with the *iḍā*. (Cm: the Sākamedha sacrifice)
AsvSS_2.18/4: "The householders have come; the Prabudhnya deities exert their splendors.
(Cm: [This refers to] the Sākamedha.
AsvSS_2.18/5: The two Virāj verses used as the *saṃyājya* offerings are those containing the word *puṣṭi*, and they are recited without the *anigada*.
(Cm: Sākamedha) AśvSS 2.18/6: This also applies elsewhere when there is no invocation. (Cm: Sākamedha)
At the invitation for the ancestral rite (*pitryā*) and at the animal sacrifice (*paśu*), [the same applies].
On this night, they should provide abundant food.
(Cm:
Sākamedha) At its conclusion, they should offer a full ladleful at the full moon sacrifice.
(Cm: Sākamedha)
When a bull bellowing; or when there is thunder.
Some cause the Āgnīdhra fire to roar, calling it the "son of the Brahman. (Cm: Sāka-medha) AśvSS 2.18/12.
If they should urge the Hotṛ, his *yājyā* and *anuvākyā* verses are as follows:
"O full ladle, fly away; well-filled, fly back again.
Like goods for sale, let us barter food and strength, O Śatakratu."
"Give to me! I give to you! Give back to me! I give back to you!
Thus, like the gathering of waters, the mother says, "He gives, he gives.
(Cm: *sākam-eda*)
The [offering] for the Maruts, the sportive ones, is the northern one. Also,
the two verses for Vṛtra-slayer recited behind the scenes are "And let the people say" and "This one is the doer, ungraspable."
Your host,
O Maruts, is sportive; they who are the Maruts are as swift-moving as coursers.
The two *saṃyājyā* verses are: "juṣṭo damūnā" and "agne śardha mahate saubhāgyāya.
The ritual for Vājinī is said to be like that of the Varuṇapraghāsas, with the exception of the *avabhṛtha* (concluding purificatory bath).
(Cm: [This refers to] the Sākamedha.)
For the oblations beginning with the seventh, Indra Vṛtrahan, Indra Mahendra, or Viśvakarman occupy the place. [The verses are:

"Come hither to us, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra," "To thee has been given for thy great power," "O Viśvakarman, increasing by the oblation," and "Those which are thy highest abodes and those which are thy lowest."
(Cm: sāka.medha) Having carried forward the fire from the southern fire, [the sacrifice] for the ancestors (*pitryā*) takes place. (Cm:
pitryā) That [sacrifice] ends with the *śaṃyu* formula. (Cm: pitryā)

AsvSS 2.19/3: The *hotṛ* priest omits the murmuring (*japa*), the *vaṣaṭ*-utterance, the consecration formula (*anumantraṇa*), and the *abhihiṃkāra*. (Cm: pertaining to the ancestral rite). AsvSS 2.19/4: At that [rite], the fivefold ritual actions constitute the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). (Cm: pertaining to the ancestral rite). AsvSS 2.19/5: The other [elements] follow the same sequence. (Cm: pertaining to the ancestral rite).

The *sāmidhenī* verses are those beginning with "uśantas tvā nidhīmahi," recited three times without pausing. At the end of these, with the final *praṇava*, the concluding formula is: "Bring the gods and the ancestors for the sacrificer.
In place of the words "Bring Agni for the office of the Hotṛ; bring his own greatness," one should invoke "Agni Kavyavāhana."
And at the final *prayāja* offering, he should cause [the sacrificer] to recite the formulas before the *ājyapāḥ* verses. (Cm:
pertaining to the ancestral rite) And at the *sūktavāka*, in place of the formula "Agni with the office of the *hotṛ*," [he should recite the appropriate formula]. (Cm:
pertaining to the ancestral rite) Here, there is no measuring of the distance with the handspan. (Cm: pertaining to the ancestral rite)
AśvSS 2.19/13: There is no wiping. (Cm: pertaining to the ancestors) AśvSS 2.19/14: In the *sūktavāka*, there is no mention of names. (Cm: pertaining to the ancestors) AśvSS 2.19/15:
Having been looked at, or addressed with "Sit down, O Hotṛ," he should sit down. (Cm: pertaining to the ancestors)

AsvSS 2.19/16: Wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder (*savya-uttarīya*) and with the sacrificial cord suspended over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvītin*), they perform the oblations with the *jīvātumat* verses while standing in the *upastha* posture; [these are] the rites for the ancestors (*pitryā*).
AsvSS 2.19/17: The Āgnīdhra stands to the south and the Adhvaryu to the north. There are two *anuvākyā* verses for each [offering].
[He recites] the *adhyardhā* [verse] without pausing. (Cm: pertaining to the ancestors) AśvSS 2.19/18: "Oṃ svadhā" is the call for response (*āśrāvaṇa*).
"Let there be svadhā" (*astu svadhā*) is the response (*pratyāśrāvaṇa*).
"Anusvadha! Svadha!"—this is the call for direction (*sampraiṣa*).
"Ye svadhā" or "Ye svadhā-maha"—this is the response (*āgūḥ*).
"Svadha namaḥ"—this is the *vaṣaṭ*-call. (Regarding the ancestral rites).

The *pluti* vowels are always [used]. (Cm: pertaining to the ancestors). The ancestors accompanied by Soma; or Soma accompanied by the ancestors; the ancestors seated on the sacrificial grass (*barhiṣad*); the ancestors consecrated by fire (*agniṣvātta*); and Yama. (Cm: pertaining to the ancestors).

"May the lower ones rise up, and the higher ones; for by you, O Soma, our fathers were invited of old. The Soma-loving fathers have been summoned. You, O Soma, are wise through your insight. Soma [gives] the milch-cow; Soma [gives] the swift steed. You, O Soma, in harmony with the fathers, [come] hither for the sake of the fathers seated on the sacrificial grass. I have found the well-disposed fathers. Let this homage be to the fathers today. O Agniṣvātta fathers, come here! Those fathers who are here and those who are not here, those who were cremated by fire and those who were not cremated—O Yama, sit down upon this sacrificial seat. Thus [he recites] two [verses], beginning with "He who has gone forth along the great slopes... and ending with "...this sacrificial seat."
(Cm: pertaining to the ancestors) AsvSS 2.19/23: If the middle *yājyā* verse belongs to Vaivasvata, [it is as follows]. (Cm: pertaining to the ancestors) AsvSS 2.19/24:

"Those who have thirsted among the gods, exerting themselves—through thee, O Agni, for poetic wisdom, through thee for inspired thoughts, together with ancient ones, winning thousands at birth. (Cm: pertaining to the ancestors)

Agni Sviṣṭakṛt is Kavyavāhana. From this point onward, the procedure follows the original model. And in the performance of the *vaṣaṭ*-call, it is as in the original, except for the omission of other mantras after the two *ājyabhāga* offerings.
AsvSS_2.19/28: There is one invitatory verse (*anuvākyā*) for each [offering].

(Cm: pertaining to the ancestors). AsvSS_2.19/29: "O Agni, who carries the raw flesh" (*yo agniḥ kravyavāhanaḥ*) and "O Agni Jātavedas, being thus invoked" (*tvam agne īḷito jātavedaḥ*) are the two concluding verses (*saṃyājye*). (Cm: pertaining to the ancestors). AsvSS_2.19/30: Having consumed the portions of the breaths (*prāṇabhakṣa*) during the consumption rites, they should throw [the remnants] onto the sacrificial grass (*barhis*). When the rite is completed, or before the after-offerings (*anuyāja*), they, turning toward the south, worship the southern fire (*dakṣiṇāgni*).
(Cm: pertaining to the ancestors) AsvSS 2.19/31: Without turning back, when the practice is not excessively advanced. (Cm:
pertaining to the ancestors) AsvSS 2.19/32: "Most active, engendering mighty deeds, for he is glowing; he is a wide path for the granting of boons."
"He has risen up with the support of the essence of honey, when he extended his own body within [his] body. (Cm: pertaining to the ancestors).
Having turned around, however, [he performs] the other two. (Cm: pertaining to the ancestors).
[He offers] to the Āhavanīya fire with the *paṅkti* verse beginning, "Thee, who art beautiful to behold... (Cm: pertaining to the ancestors).

AsvSS 2.19.35: [They go] to the Gārhapatya fire with a single ṛc, "I think of that Agni," and not with a whole hymn. AsvSS 2.19.36: Then they approach it while muttering, "Do not neglect us, O Agni; do not abandon us. AsvSS 2.19.37:
Having completed the hymn to the east of the Gārhapatya, they turn to the left, avoiding the Tryambaka offerings.
AśvSS 2.19.38: Therein the ritual duties of the Adhvaryu are studied. AśvSS 2.19.39: Having returned, they perform the Ādityā offering.
AśvSS 2.19.40: The two Virāj verses are the Puṣṭimat dhāyyās.
On the fifth full moon day, one performs the Śunāsīrīya sacrifice;
or at any time prior to that, as circumstances permit.
(Cm: śunāsīrīya) AŚvSS 2.20/3:
With the exception of the *vājina* offering, the [procedures] are the same as for the Vaiśvadeva sacrifice.
However, in place of the oblations beginning with the sixth, [the deities are]: Vāyu Niyutvat, or Vāyu, or Śunāsīrau, or Indra Śunāsīra, or Indra, or Sūrya as the last.
(Cm:

śunāsīrīya) Ā vāyo bhūṣa śucipā upa naḥ prayābhir yāsi dāśvāṃsam accha. Sa tvaṃ no deva manasā īśānāya prahutiṃ yas ta ānaṭ. Śunāsīrau imāṃ vācaṃ juṣethām. Śunaṃ naḥ phālā vikṛṣantu bhūmim. Indra vayam śunāsīrau me asmin pakṣe havāmahe. (Cm: śunāsīrīya)
"May he protect us in the contests for booty;

desiring horses, desiring cattle, desiring booty, let us invoke with a cry of 'Success! the bountiful Indra. Desiring horses, desiring cattle, desiring booty—the all-beautiful, swift one has risen, the brilliant face of the gods. These are the invitatory and offering verses for the Śunāsīrīya sacrifice.
Having completed [the Soma sacrifice], one should sacrifice with Soma; if unable, with an animal sacrifice (the Śunāsīrīya). Or again, the Cāturmāsya sacrifices; or again, the Cāturmāsya sacrifices.
(Cm: śunāsīrīya) AsvSS 3.1/1:
[The rite] regarding the animal sacrifice. (paśubandha) AsvSS 3.1/2:
The *iṣṭi* is performed either on both occasions or on one of them.
(Animal Sacrifice) Or it may belong to Agni. (Animal Sacrifice) AśvSS 3.1.3.
AśvSS 3.1/4: Or [the offering] belongs to Agni and Viṣṇu. (Animal Sacrifice) AśvSS 3.1/5: Or both [offerings belong to Agni and Viṣṇu]. (Animal Sacrifice)
AśvSS 3.1.6: One of the two [fires] is placed in front.
(The Animal Sacrifice) AśvSS 3.1.7: The carrying forward of the fire has been explained.

(paśu.bandha) AśvSS 3.1.8: Having sat down behind the altar used for the animal sacrifice (paśubandha), when he is prompted [by the Adhvaryu], he should begin with the half-verse from the last line of the verse: "The god-seekers anoint you at the sacrifice while you are being sprinkled for the sacrificial post.
(paśu.bandha)

(Regarding the Animal Sacrifice: He should recite the two verses, “O Lord of the Forest, grow tall, being supported in front of the kindled fire” and “Upright for our protection,” and he should pause at the half-verse of “Born, he is born again in the auspiciousness of days.
He should conclude with the verse, “The youth, well-dressed and girt about, has arrived.
(Animal Sacrifice)

AśvSS 3.1.10: Where there are many animals in a single ritual procedure, one should chant the *saṃstuti* after performing the final *paridhāna*, without the *abhihiṅkāra*, with the six verses beginning, "The men who, seeking the gods, have set you up... (RV 3.8.4–9). AśvSS 3.1.11: Or with five [verses].
"Some say there is no repetition.
(Regarding the animal sacrifice: It has been stated that the fire-drilling is performed, as well as the two *dhāyyā* verses; the two *ājyabhāga* offerings may be performed or not.
In the invocation (*āvāhana*), after the deities of the animal sacrifice, one should invoke Vanaspati immediately thereafter.
(Paśubandha) Having cleansed [the ladle] with the cleansing-brushes (*sammārjana*), one should offer the *pravṛta* oblations. (AśvSS 3.1.13)
(paśubandha) AśvSS 3.1.14: "May I be pleasing to Speech; may I be pleasing to the Lord of Speech, O Goddess Speech!
Place me in that which is the sweetest of speech. Svāhā to Sarasvatī, to Speech!"
Taking it up again with five portions: "Svāhā to Speech! Svāhā to the Lord of Speech! Svāhā to Sarasvatī! Svāhā to Sarasvant! Svāhā to the great ones! Svāhā to the exceedingly great ones!
(In the animal sacrifice, some say: "To Soma" [is added]).

(Paśubandha) Having led the *praśāstṛ* forward by way of the *tīrtha*, he should hand him the staff with both his right and left hands, saying: "I hand you over by the arms of Mitra and Varuṇa, by the command of the two *praśāstṛ*s.
(Paśubandha)

AśvSS 3.1.17: With those two [verses] thus joined, the other [verse] is recited: "With the arms of Mitra and Varuṇa, by the command of the Praśāstṛ, I receive you; may I be free from crookedness and unimpaired. (Paśubandha) AśvSS 3.1.18:

Having received [the animal], he should pass beyond the Hotṛ to the north; he should carry the staff to the south, and he must not touch himself or anyone else with it until the call for the *praiṣa* has been uttered.
(Animal Sacrifice) AŚvSS 3.1.19: One should not allow anything else that has been used as a sacrificial implement to intervene between oneself and the sacrificial ground (*vihāra*).
(Animal Sacrifice)
AśvSS 3.1.20: Leaning forward from the Hotṛ’s seat toward the south and resting his staff upon the altar, he should utter the *praiṣas* and the directions.
AśvSS 3.1.21: He should recite the invitatory verse (*anuvākyā*) together with the *praiṣa*, the former preceding the *praiṣa*.
(Paśubandha) AśvSS 3.1.22: The *paryagni* rite, the *stoka* verses, the *manotā*, and the *unnīyamāna-sūkta*.

In the *Dīkṣaṇīyā* [offering] of the *Soma-pravacana*, there are two *dhāyyā* verses in the *virāj* meter addressed to Agni and Viṣṇu. In the *Dīkṣā* [rite] of the *Soma* [sacrifice], [the verses are] addressed to Agni and Viṣṇu.
Agni was the first mouth of the deities; Viṣṇu was the last among those assembled.
Having gathered the gods for the sake of the sacrificer, [O Agni and Viṣṇu], initiate us and come to this our oblation.
O Agni and Viṣṇu, you two, the mighty ones, have indeed performed supreme heat and great penance for the protection of the consecration.

"O you two who are in agreement with all the gods worthy of sacrifice, bestow consecration (*dīkṣā*) upon this sacrificer. (Soma: Consecration) AśvSS 4.2/4: [The deities are] Vaiśvānara, Ādityas, Sarasvatī, and Aditi. (Soma: Consecration) AśvSS 4.2/5:

Initiation) And here there is no substitution of the name. (Soma:

There are either one or three *dīkṣā*s, three *upasads*, and the day of the *sutyā* is the last. At the conclusion of the *dīkṣā*, the purchase of the King (*Soma*) takes place.

(Soma: Prāyaṇīya-iṣṭi) AśvSS 4.3/2a:

Pathyāsvasti, Agni, Soma, Savitṛ, Aditi—may there be well-being for us on the paths and in the desert wastes. [He recites] two verses: "O Agni, lead us by a good path to wealth," and "We have gone upon the path of the gods. "O Soma, you are wise through your insight.
(Prāyaṇīya-iṣṭi)

"Those abodes of yours which are in heaven and those on earth; [we invoke] the Lord of the assembly, the protector of all gods, who is the good guardian of all these created beings, the Earth, the Heaven, the faultless one, the great mother of those who observe good vows—may he indeed be Agni among the Agnis," thus [it is said]. "Let there be others," [these are] the two *saṃyājyā* verses ending with *śaṃ*.
(Soma: Prāyaṇīya Iṣṭi)

While they are about to drive it forward, he should stand between the two tracks at a distance of three steps behind the cart, and being prompted, [he recites]: "O Agni, from the *abhihiṅkāra*, you are the sage, you are the poet, you who maintain all things.
(Soma:

Soma-purchase) "Drive away the fear of enemies," [reciting this] while not letting the hind hoof touch the ground with the forefoot; having thrice raised the dust with his right foot, he should recite: "Go forth from good to better; let Bṛhaspati be your leader."
Then, standing [there], he says: "Bring him hither from the choice place of the earth; drive away the enemies, O hero of all!
While following after [the Soma], he walks between the two tracks on the north side.
(Regarding the purchase of Soma:

*somakrayaṇa*) [The Adhvaryu recites] the three verses beginning with "Those Somas of yours which are health-bringing," and the half-verse beginning with "All rejoice at the glorious one who has arrived; O God, you have come with the seasons; may he increase our dwelling.
When the cart has come to a halt, having stepped forward from the right side of it, he stands facing the King (Soma).

When the [offering] has been completed, those intending to perform the *tānūnaptra* rite touch the clarified butter (*ājya*) with the formula: "Thou art unassailable, unassailable; the vigor of the gods, a protector against imprecation.
May we, free from imprecation, straightway attain truth. Place me in well-being."
(Soma: Ātithyeṣṭi) Having touched water, they cause the King [Soma] to swell. (Soma: Ātithyeṣṭi) AśvSS 4.5/4: Having touched water, they cause the King [Soma] to swell. (Soma: Ātithyeṣṭi)

(Soma: Pravargya)

Pravargya) AśvSS 4.6.3: "The Brahman, first born, from the navel of the world, the radiant one, has shone forth for you, O seers."
With my whole being, I have reached his manifestations, the source of both the existent and the non-existent.
This [earth] belongs to the Father; he stood at the beginning for the first birth, established in the fullness of being.
For him, I offer this brightly shining oblation.
They mix the warm milk at the first draught;

the Great One, having been born, propped apart the two great worlds. The Father established the celestial abode and the earthly realm. From the foundation he rose up by his very birth; Bṛhaspati is the sovereign deity thereof.

I praise that god Savitṛ, the source of protection for both worlds, whose will is wisdom, whose impulse is truth, and who bestows treasures—the beloved sage of inspired thought. Whose lofty inspiration shone forth to me at the time of his impelling; he, the golden-handed one of excellent power, has measured out [the world] with his form, whether as *svasṛpā* or as *svar*.
(Soma: Pravargya)
While he is being seated, [the verse] "Be seated; you are great" (*saṃsīdasva mahān asi*) is recited.
While he is being anointed, [the verse] "The wise anoint him as they spread him out" (*añjanti yaṃ prathayanta iva viprāḥ*) is recited. [Then follow] the two verses:

"The winged one, anointed by the magic power of the sun, who is our kinsman—may he not harm us, O Agni; be well-disposed toward us, O Agni, when we have approached" (*pataṅgam aktaṃ asrasya māyayā yo naḥ sanutyo abhidāsad agne bhavā no agne sumanā upetau*). These are the two *ṛca*s.
(Regarding the *pravargya* ritual in the Soma sacrifice):

"Make wide your power like a broad expanse" (*kṛṇuṣva pājaḥ prasitiṃ na pṛthvīm*), these five [verses]; "Around you, O lover of songs, the songs," "Upon two [stones] he has placed the hymn and the word," "Bright is one [form] of yours, sacrificial is the other," "I have seen the herdsman who never rests," "Into the mouth of the drop," "This Vena has impelled those whose womb is the speckled cloud," "Your filter is spread out, O Brahmanaspati"—these two; "The two worlds have stretched out the filter," "The two bowls have woven the filter," "They bear the glowing *gharma* while pronouncing the *praṇava*s.
(Regarding the *pravargya* ritual in the Soma sacrifice)
"In the midst of the ocean, they have meditated upon the name of the far-seeing Sun three times a day.

With the first verse of this hymn beginning "I beheld you, the foremost of the hosts," he looks at the sacrificer; with the second, at his wife; and with the third, at himself. Then there are nine verses beginning, "What offering shall please you, O Aśvins? (Soma: Pravargya).

*Soma: Pravargya* AŚvSS 4.6 /3d: [The Adhvaryu recites: “Agni shines like the pressing-stones; I praise Heaven and Earth. Prior to the final verse, he should insert [the verse]: “The dappled one, foremost, has caused the Dawn to shine. With the second half-verse, he should look at the wife. When the final verse has been concluded, having made them stand up, the Adhvaryus cause them to recite; such is the first section. *Soma: Pravargya*
Now follows the subsequent [rite]. (Soma:
Pravargya) When [the priests] have sat down, the Adhvaryu calls for the cow that yields the Gharma; this is the formal direction (*saṃpraiṣa*) for the subsequent [rite].
(Regarding the Pravargya ritual in the Soma sacrifice:
Without uttering the *hiṃ* sound.
(Soma: Pravargya)

Having invoked [the cow] with the two verses beginning, “This well-milking cow,” and “O God Savitṛ, toward you...”; [and with] “Like a calf with its mothers,” “Like a calf with its mothers,” “That breast of yours which is inexhaustible, which is refreshing,” “The cow has lowed after the blinking calf,” “With reverence approach her who sits nearby,” “Sitting together, in harmony, with the ten fingers of Vivasvat they milk the one [cow],” and “Kindled is Agni, O Aśvins; the *gharma* is heated for you;
come! (Soma: Pravargya).

The cows are milked; here the bulls and milch-cows [yield their gifts]; O wonder-workers, the singers rejoice. Agni is kindled; O bulls, the delight of heaven is yours; the heated cauldron is milked for you as honey for nourishment.
For we, the singers, being your most frequent [invokers], call upon you, O Aśvins, at the shared feasts.

(Soma: Pravargya) AśvSS 4.7 /4c: Now, this ritual action of his is most manifest: the sky, possessing a self, is milked for ghee and milk. Having recited the verse, "Arise, O Brahmanaspati," he stands by while it is being milked. When it has been milked, [he recites]: "He has milked the swelling nourishment. While it is being brought forward, [he recites]: "O cowherd, come hither with the milk; pour the milk of the cow into the *gharma* vessel! (Soma: Pravargya)

"Vinaṅ akhyat Savitā vareṇyo nu dyāvāpṛthivī supraṇītī" when it is being poured; "nūnam aśvinor ṛṣiḥ" when [the milk] from the cows is poured; "siñcata śriyam" when the clarified butter is poured; and "samutye mahatīr apaḥ" for both [the soma and the clarified butter].
(Soma: Pravargya)

(Soma: Pravargya) AsvSS 4.7/4f: "The heated *gharma* approaches you two; the excellent Hotṛ [approaches]. (suhotā)
The Adhvaryu priest moves before you, bearing the sacrificial food.
O Aśvins, enjoy and drink of the milked honey for the sake of progeny; drink from the active, radiant cow.
(Soma: Pravargya)
With the verse, "Drink both, O Aśvins," he offers with both [formulas] without taking breath. The *anuvashat-kāra* is either "O Agni, enjoy the Gharma" or "O Agni, enjoy the Gharma.
At the *vaṣaṭ* call and at the *anuvashat* call, the Brahman priest mutters: "From the south, all the quarters; all the gods, you have come here as gods.
Drink, O Aśvins, of the honeyed Gharma over which *svāhā* has been uttered. In the same way, it is performed for the afternoon rite.
O Aśvins, that ghee and milk which has been offered into the cows—that is your portion; come hither!
O lovers of sweetness, upholders of the assembly, lords of the virtuous, drink the heated *gharma*, the Soma-like honey!

"O Aśvins, drink of this!"—thus urged by the *praśāstṛ*, the Hotṛ recites at the *anuvaṣaṭkāra*: "Hail! The Gharma is pure among the gods; it is that which is the cup of the Aśvins, the drinking-vessel of the gods.

(With *samīvatsam*. AśvSS 4.7.4j:
"Him all the immortals, taking pleasure in it, receive back from the Gandharva’s mouth.
Vena raises the wave from the ocean; when the drop goes toward the ocean, O friend, turn toward your friend!—and 'Upward for us, for our protection,' these two [verses]."

[The mantra: "Like a falcon, [I go] to my seat, the womb made by wisdom, wherein the seven Vasus may ascend—the ancient ascent.

(Soma: second *upasad* day)

AśvSS 4.8/17: On the day of preparation (*aupavasathya*), both [the *gharma* and the *upasad*] are performed in the forenoon.
(Soma: Second Upasad Day) AśvSS 4.8/18:
When the first Upasad has been performed, the initiated Hotṛ, being prompted, recites the verses for the piling of the soil-layer (*purīṣya-citi*). Thus it is said.
(Soma: Second Upasad Day)
AsvSS 4.8/19: [This applies] when the sacrificer has not been initiated.
(Soma: Second Upasad Day) AsvSS 4.8/20:

Having stood at a distance of one footstep behind [the fire], and having uttered the *abhihiṃkāra*, he recites three times in a low voice (*upāṃśu*) with the *praṇava*: "O fires dwelling in the soil... (*purīṣyāso agnayaḥ*).
(Regarding the Soma sacrifice on the second *upasad* day:
Or rather, [he recites] "sumandram.
(Soma: second *upasad* day)
AsvSS_4.8/22: While they are walking, he should follow after them.
(Soma: second upasad day) AsvSS_4.8/23: When they are standing still, having released his speech, he should say, "Lead forward [the fires]."
(Soma: Second Upasad Day) AŚvSS 4.8/24: Then he should chant the *anugīta* in accordance with the piled fire-altar (*agni-saṃcita*).
(Soma: Second Upasad Day)
Having sat down behind the tail of the fire-altar and having uttered the *abhihiṃkāra*, he recites "I am Agni, Jātavedas by birth" three times in a medium tone of voice.
(Soma: second *upasad* day) On this very seat, he performs the sacrifice for Vaiśvānara.
(Regarding the Soma sacrifice on the second *upasad* day:
These three [rites] are performed in the case of one who has established the fire-altar (*agni-citi*).
(Soma: second *upasad* day)
AśvSS 4.8/28: Having murmured the *apratiratha* hymn, the Brahman sits to the south of the fire, outside the sacrificial altar, until the offering on the *audumbarī* post.
(Soma: second *upasad* day) AśvSS 4.8/29: The carrying forward of the fire has been explained.
(Soma: Second Upasad Day) AśvSS 4.8/30:
But the initiated one should approach the stream of wealth (vasor dhārā).
(Soma: Second Upasad Day)
They move the *havirdhāna* shed forward.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day: Moving the *Havirdhāna*)
This has been explained by means of the *soma-pravahana* [of the third *upasad* day: the moving forward of the *havirdhāna*].
The two feet [of the cart] pass between the wheel and the track of the northern wheel of the southern *havirdhāna* shed.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day: Moving the *Havirdhāna*)

*“yuñje vām brahma pūrvyaṃ namobhiḥ | protaṃ yajñasya śambhuvā yuvām | yame iva yatamāne yadaitam adhidvayor adadhā ukthyaṃ vacaḥ” — with these words he should begin [the movement of the *havirdhāna* carts], provided that the two queens (*rarāṭī*) have not yet separated.* (Soma: Third Upasad Day:
Movement of the *Havirdhāna*)
"O Sage, you put on all forms"—with these words [he establishes] the arrangement.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day: Setting in Motion the Havirdhāna Carts)
(Regarding the Soma sacrifice on the third *upasad* day: the moving forward of the *havirdhāna* carts.
When the two *methī* pegs have been set in place, he should conclude [the rite] with the verse: "Around thee, O Nirṛti, flow the songs. (AśvSS 4.9/6)
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:

Moving the Havirdhāna Carts) When they are about to lead forth Agni and Soma, [the Adhvaryu], having entered by the *tīrtha*, having passed to the north of the Āgnīdhrīya shed and the *sadas*, and having entered the *patnīśālā* by the eastern door, having gone past the *śālāmukhīya* fire to the north, and having sat down behind it, should recite the invitatory verses when prompted: "O God, impel for the first father; bestow upon him height, bestow upon him breadth."
"Then, O Savitṛ, impel us toward complete well-being, day by day, toward abundant cattle"—thus [he recites] while seated.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:
Agni-Soma Leading Forth)
While following after [the fire], he recites the subsequent [verses].
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:
The Leading Forth of Agni and Soma)

"May Brahmanaspati go forth; the immortal god Hotṛ; from the front, O Agni, day by day, O illuminator, [may he come] to you, the beloved, who bestows gifts"—at this half-verse he should pause. When the [fire] has been placed on the Āgnīdhrīya altar and the offering is being made, he should complete it with "O Agni, enjoy it, welcome that speech," and then cease with the *praṇava*.
(Soma: third upasad day)
Regarding the leading forth of Agni and Soma:

while they are passing by the north of the Āgnīdhrīya fire, having passed by it, he should stop at the half-verse with the words: "Soma goes forth, the knower of the way, for the gods; him King Varuṇa and the two Aśvins [protect].
(Soma: third upasad day).
Regarding the leading forward of Agni and Soma (agnīṣomapraṇayana):
one should follow the King [Soma] as he enters.

One should conclude [the rite] with the verse, "Thou art Aditi within; like a hawk, thou hast settled in the dwelling-place prepared by wisdom; the Asura, all-knowing, has propped up the sky," or else with the following verse during the performance of the rest-period (kṣema).
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:
Agni-Soma Pranayana) "Thus indeed, do thou praise Varuna."
The Brahman priest, having entered in this very same manner and having passed beyond the rear of the altar, shall sit down to the south of the *śālāmukhīya* fire.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:
Agni-Soma Pranaṇa)
Without rising after the Hotṛ, he should walk in front as he went, if he is to lead forward King Soma.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day: Leading Forward Agni and Soma)
It has been stated regarding one who does not lead forward [the fires].
(Soma: Third Upasad Day: Leading Forward of Agni and Soma)

Having reached the two *havirdhāna* sheds and handed over the King [Soma] to the *gṛhapati*, he should walk past the front or the back of the *havirdhāna* sheds and sit down to the south of the *āhavanīya* fire.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:
The Leading Forth of Agni and Soma)
The tail of the fire-altar [is placed] upon the fire-hearth.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:
The Leading Forth of Agni and Soma)
This is the seat of the Brahman priest during the animal sacrifice.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:
The Leading Forth of Agni and Soma)
And [the rite continues] in the morning until the offering of the omentum.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:
The Leading Forth of Agni and Soma)
But if he should approach by the front while [the fire] is being led forward.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day: Leading Forward of Agni and Soma)
Then they proceed with the offering to Agni and Soma.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day: Agni-Soma Animal Sacrifice)
On the northern altar, from the point of handing over the staff until [the end of the rite].
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:
Agni-Somīya Animal Sacrifice)

Having handed over the staff and having placed the Maitrāvaruṇa at the front, he passes to the north of the two *havirdhāna* sheds, enters the *sadas* by the eastern door, passes to the north of his own and the other *dhiṣṇya* hearths according to their respective positions, and sits down behind his own *dhiṣṇya* as the Hotṛ priest.
(Soma: third *upasad* day; *agnīṣomīya* animal sacrifice)
The other stands by.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:
Agni-Somīya Animal Sacrifice)

AśvSS 4.11/5: If they should offer the oblations for the Devasū deities, [the order is]: Agni Gṛhapati, Soma Vanaspati, Savitṛ Satyaprasava, Bṛhaspati Vācaspati, Indra Jyeṣṭha, Mitra Satya, Varuṇa Dharmapati, and Rudra Paśumān (or Paśupati).
(Soma: Third Upasad Day; Agnīṣomīya Animal Sacrifice)

O Agni, you are the one of great vitality, the bearer of oblations; Agni is our ageless father. And you, O Soma, by our will, are the Brahman of the gods, the path-maker of the seers. We have not forgotten the Lord of the All-Gods, who is the protector of the good and the lord of the divine host.
(Soma: third *upasad* day; *agnīṣomīya* animal sacrifice)

O Bṛhaspati, you have first seized the foremost point of speech; like swans, O much-invoked one, you have overcome the enemies with your clamoring companions. You, O Indra, have become great through the sacred word (*brahman*); may we be free from disease, rejoicing in the nourishing food.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day: Agni-Soma Animal Sacrifice)
"May the mortal man be a true friend, offering oblations; having found you, he asks for greatness. Bound by you, he seeks to be released.
By your law (*dharman*), you protect him from every world; by your law, you protect him even from the Sun.
"Whatever here, O Varuṇa, among the divine folk, I have performed as hymns of praise, like a herdsman [tending his flock],"—these two verses.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day;

Agni-Soma Animal Sacrifice) AśvSS 4.12/1a: If, however, all the *pṛṣṭha* chants are performed, [the deities and meters are as follows]: Agni is associated with the *gāyatrī* meter, the *trivṛt* stoma, and the *rathantara* sāman, belonging to spring; Indra is associated with the *triṣṭubh* meter, the *pañcadaśa* stoma, and the *bṛhat* sāman, belonging to summer; the Viśvedevas are associated with the *jagatī* meter, the *saptadaśa* stoma, and the *vairūpa* sāman, belonging to the rainy season.

(Mitra and Varuṇa are connected with the Anuṣṭubh metre, the twenty-one-fold stoma, the Vairāja sāman, and the autumn season; Bṛhaspati is connected with the Paṅkti metre, the twenty-seven-fold stoma, the Śākvara sāman, and the winter season; Savitṛ is connected with the Aticchandas metre, the thirty-three-fold stoma, the Raivata sāman, and the cool season; Aditi is the wife of Viṣṇu, and Anumati is [the deity].)
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:
Agni-Soma Animal Sacrifice) AśvSS 4.12.2a: May Madhava, who lies in the direction of the fuel-sticks, who possesses the light, whose seed is honey—may he protect us.
May the divine Agni, difficult to overcome and invincible, protect this sovereignty and guard us.
May the *Rathantara* protect us with the *Sāmans*; may the *Gāyatrī*, the omniform among meters, protect us.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day)
(The Agni-Soma animal sacrifice: "The Trivṛt is the stoma for the distribution of the days; may the ocean, the wind, this vigor, fulfill [us].
The fierce one, the overcomer of the quarters, the bestower of strength, the pure one among the powerful ones on the bright day."
May Indra, the sovereign lord, protect us from this; uphold this great dominion on every side.
The *Bṛhat* Sāman is the bearer of dominion, increased and virile; the *Triṣṭubh* is strength, made beautiful with fierce heroes.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day)
(Regarding the animal sacrifice for Agni and Soma: "O Indra, with the fifteen-fold *stoma*, protect this middle [region] together with Vāta and the ocean.
The eastern direction among the quarters is glorious and full of splendor; all the gods [protect it] with the rainy season of days, full of light."
"May this kṣatra be invincible; may it be unassailable power, victorious and mighty."
May I be able to accomplish that here through the Vairūpa Sāman; may I cause him to enter among the people through the Jagatī.
O All-Gods, through the seventeenfold [Stoma], bestow this fierce kṣatra-power, which is like the ocean and the wind.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day)
(Agnīṣomīya animal sacrifice):
"The upholder of the quarters, he has maintained this sovereignty; may the strength of the regions be like that of Mitra.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you who are wise, bestow great peace upon this kingdom for the sake of autumn and the days."
(Soma: Third Upasad Day;
Agni-Soma Animal Sacrifice) AśvSS 4.12/2f: Upon the Vairāja Sāman is my inspired thought; through the Anuṣṭubh is gathered heroic power and might.
This kṣatra, friendly and yielding moisture, protect it, O Mitra and Varuṇa, under your sovereignty!
The sovereign of the quarters, powerful and mighty, may the winter season fulfill our needs through its distribution.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day)
(Regarding the animal sacrifice for Agni and Soma:

May the *avasyu*, *vātā*, *bṛhatī*, and *śakvarī* meters protect this sacrifice for us; may the butter-sprinkling goddess protect us. May the heavenly, well-milking, milk-abounding goddess of the quarters protect us; may the butter-sprinkling goddess protect us.
O Bṛhaspati, you are the protector, the one who goes before and the one who follows; with those two, join our speech.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:
Agni-Somīya Animal Sacrifice)

May the upward direction, the delight of the quarters, the hope of the plants, Savitṛ with the year among the days, the Raivata Sāman, the Atichandas metre, the Ucchandas, and the Unborn Enemy be gracious to us.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day)
(At the Agni-Soma animal sacrifice:
In the Trayastrimsha-stoma, [I pray] to Bhuvanasya Patnī, Vivasvat, and Vāta: "Protect us with your praise!
O Savitṛ, under your sovereignty, may there be for us a refreshing quarter, rich in ghee and full of milk."
Dhruvā is the wife of Viṣṇu among the quarters; she is not terrible, the sovereign of the mouth, she who is the mind-born power of strength.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:
Agni-Somīya Animal Sacrifice)

May Bṛhaspati, Mātariśvan, and Vāyu, and the roaring winds, favor us. She who is the pillar of heaven, the support of earth, the sovereign mistress of this world, the wife of Viṣṇu— may she, far-seeing, refreshing, auspicious, and well-disposed, be gracious to us in the lap of Aditi.
(Regarding the Soma sacrifice on the third *upasad* day:
the animal sacrifice for Agni and Soma) AŚvSS 4.12/2k: May Anumati favor our sacrifice today among the gods.
And may Agni, the bearer of oblations, be a source of delight for the donor.
O Anumati, do thou indeed grant us thy approval and bestow peace upon us.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day)
[For the animal sacrifice] to Agni and Soma:
"Impel us toward ritual power and skill; may he prolong our lifespans.
The ninth [offering] is dedicated to Vaiśvānara, and the tenth is the Kāya offering.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:
Agni-Soma Animal Sacrifice) AsvSS 4.12.3: "Who yokes today the two oxen to the pole of Order?"—these two [verses].
They should proceed without enclosing [the altar] with the embers from the supplementary offerings (*aupayaja*).
(Soma: Third Upasad Day: Agni-Somīya Animal Sacrifice) (Prajāpati).
If [the fire is brought] from the Āgnīdhrīya, it is to the north of the Hotṛ.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:
Agni-Somīya Animal Sacrifice)
If [the path] is from the *śāmitra* fire to the south, the *maitrāvaruṇa* cup is drawn.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:
Agni-Somīya Animal Sacrifice)
Having made the fast-day the priority and having gone out, he should take up the Veda.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:
Agni-Somīya Animal Sacrifice)
In these and other such cases, the heart-spike is not used prior to the *anūbandhyā* sacrifice.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day:
Agni-Somīya Animal Sacrifice)
When the [offering] has been completed, they carry around the *vasatīvarī* waters; those who have been consecrated (*dīkṣita*) should carry them around.
(Soma: Third Upasad Day: Agni-Soma Animal Sacrifice)

Now, at the time of the departure of this night, before the birds begin to call, having been summoned for the morning litany (*prātar-anuvāka*), he should enter by the *tīrtha* where speech is restrained, bend his knee over the *āgnīdhrīya* fire, and offer an oblation with the mantra:
"Protect me from the mantra of the mouth; [protect me] from any curse, svāhā! (Soma:
Day of the Soma-pressing).
(Prātar-anuvāka) AśvSS 4.13/2: Into the Āhavanīya fire [he offers]: "May Speech go at the head; may she go at the head for Sarasvatī, for Speech, svāhā!
May the divine Speech, led by the mind, the sovereign, the fierce, the victorious, the most excellent—may she come here as our portion."
"May we board that [boat], like the boat of the Ādityas, which carries us across by approved paths—*svāhā*! Thus he offers the second oblation.
(Soma: Sutyā Day:
Prātar-anuvāka)
From this point on, the procedure for the Brahman priest is the same as that for the others.
(Soma: Sutyā Day:
Prātar-anuvāka)
Having reached the *havirdhāna* shed, he touches the *rarāṭī* beam with the formula: "Pervade the wide mid-air.
(Soma: Sutyā Day:
Morning Litany)
"To the two pillars at the door, the goddesses who are the doors: do you two, O world-makers, create for me a world that is not unattained.
(Soma: Sutyā Day:
Prātar-anuvāka)
Having entered [the sacrificial hall] and sat down between the two yoke-poles, being prompted, he should recite the *prātar-anuvāka* in a low tone.
(Soma: Sutyā Day:
Prātar-anuvāka)

From the two hymns beginning with "O Waters, rich in wealth, you indeed dwell in riches" (*āpo revatīḥ kṣayatha hi vasvaḥ*) and "Come forward" (*upa prayanta*), and from the two hymns beginning with "Protect us, O Agni" (*avā no agne*) and "I praise Agni, Agni the messenger; put on [the garment]" (*agnim īḷe 'gnim dūtam vasiṣva hi*), one should omit the final verse of each.
(Soma: Sutyā Day:
Morning Recitation)

One should extract the final verse with "tvam agne vratapāḥ. Then there are nine verses beginning with "tvam no agne mahobhiḥ," the two hymns beginning with "ime viprasya" and "yukṣvā hi," and eighteen verses beginning with "pra īḍyam pra te agne bṛhad vayaḥ.
[This concludes] the Soma-pressing day: the Prātar-anuvāka.

The hymn beginning with "arcantas tvā," the hymn beginning with "agne pāvaka dūtam vaḥ," the three verses beginning with "agnir hotā no adhvaraḥ," and the four verses beginning with "agnir hotāgne iḷā.
(Soma: Sutyā Day: Morning Anuvāka)

AśvSS 4.13: One should recite *pra vo vājā upasadyāya*, *tam agne yajñānām*, and [the next] three; one should omit the last [verse] of these. Then [one recites] *agne haṃsi*, *agnim hinvantu naḥ*, *prāgnaye vācam*—these constitute the hymn (*sūkta*). From the three beginning with *imām me agne samidham*, one should omit the last [verse]. This is the Gāyatra [section] (for the *prātar-anuvāka* on the day of the Soma-pressing).
*tvam agne vasūn*, *tvam hi kṣaitavad agnāyī*, *hotā ajaniṣṭa*, *pra vo devāya agne*, and *katā ta iti*—these five [verses].
(Soma: Sutyā Day:
Morning Recitation)

Regarding the *ānuṣṭubha* [section]: from the two hymns beginning with "O friends, dwell together" (*sakhāyaḥ saṃ vas*) and "Thee, O Agni, we approach with oblations" (*tvām agne haviṣmantaḥ*), one should omit the fourth and ninth verses from each of the ten-verse hymns; furthermore, from the first three [of these], one should omit the last verse of each.
(Soma: Sutyā Day:
Prātar-anuvāka)
"Abādhy agniḥ samidhā," "prāgnaye bṛhate pravedhase kavaye," "tvam no agne varuṇasya vidvān"—these four [verses] beginning with these constitute [the Prātaranuvāka].
(Soma: Sutyā Day:
Prātaranuvāka)

The five verses beginning with *ūrdhva ū ṣu ṇaḥ*, *sasasya yat*, and *vi yuta*; the hymn *bhadraṃ te agne*; the three verses beginning with *somasya mā tavasam* and *praty agnir uṣasaḥ*; and from the ten verses beginning with *ā hotā*, one should omit the third verse in the eighth position.
(Soma: Sutyā Day; Prātar-anuvāka)

From the two hymns beginning with *divas pari*, one should omit the final verse of the first; from the six verses beginning with *tvam hy agne prathamaḥ*, one should omit the second; and [from the four verses] beginning with *puro vo mandram*, one should omit four.
(Soma: Sutyā Day:
Prātar-anuvāka)
"tam supratīkam" (AśvSS 4.13), "ṣaḍ huve vaḥ sudyotmānam," "ni hotā hotṛṣadanam"—these two hymns; "trir mūrdhānam," three [verses]; "vahnim yaśasam upaprajinvan," three [verses].
(Soma: Sutyā Day:
Prātar-anuvāka)

From the hymn *kā.u.upetaḥ*, one should extract the three verses beginning with *hiraṇyakeśaḥ*; from the hymn *apaśyam asya mahataḥ*, two verses; from the hymn *virūpe*, [two verses]; and from the eight verses beginning with *agne naya* and *agre bṛhan*, one should extract the last three.
(Soma: Sutyā Day:
Prātar-anuvāka)

"O Agni, you who are easy to invoke, delightful to behold"—these five [verses]; "Agni, your god..."—of these ten, the third and fourth [verses] are to be extracted; this is the *traiṣṭubha* [section].
(Soma: Sutyā Day:
Morning Recitation)
"Enā vo agnim," "pra vo yahvam," "agne vivasvat," "sakhāyas tvā," "ayam agnir," "agna ā yāhy accha naḥ śīraśociṣam"—these are the six [verses].
(Soma: Sutyā Day:
Prātar-anuvāka)
*adarśi gātu-vittama* and *sapta* constitute the Bārhata [section]; *agne vājasya*, three verses beginning with *puru tvā* and *tvām agne īḷiṣva hi* constitute the Auṣṇiha [section].
(Soma: Sutyā Day:
Prātar-anuvāka)

"Janasya gopāḥ," "tvām agne ṛtāyavaḥ," "imam ū ṣu vo 'tithim uṣarbudham"—these nine [verses]; the hymn beginning with "tvam agne dyubhiḥ"; and the five verses beginning with "tvam agne prathamo aṅgirāḥ," "nū cit sahojāḥ," and "amṛto nitundate.
(Soma: Sutyā Day; Morning Anuvāka)

Regarding the *vediṣada* verses: one should extract the third verse from each of the six [groups]. [The verses are]: "This hymn for the worthy one" (*imaṃ stomam arhate*), "With those who have awakened" (*saṃjāgṛvadbhiḥ*), "O bright one, like a child" (*citra it śiśoḥ*), "Of great wealth, like a Vasu" (*vasum na citramahasaṃ*), the *Jagatī* verse, and the *Paṅkti* verse, "That Agni I honor" (*agniṃ taṃ manye*).
(Soma: Sutyā Day; Morning Recitation)
Thus ends the Āgneya sacrifice.
(Soma: Sutyā Day;
Morning Recitation).
Now follows the rite for the morning [libation].
(Soma: Sutyā Day; Prātar-anuvāka)
*Pratiṣyā sūnarī akṣa uṣaḥ*—these three verses form a *gāyatra* hymn.
*Uṣo bhadrebhiḥ* forms an *ānuṣṭubha* hymn.

*Idaṃ śreṣṭham*, *pṛthūrathaḥ*, *pratyarciḥ*, and the eight verses beginning with *dyutadyāmānam*, followed by the two hymns *uṣo vājena* and *idam u tyat*, and the six verses beginning with *vyuṣā ā vo divijāḥ*—these constitute a *traiṣṭubha* hymn.
(Regarding the Soma-pressing day: the morning recitation) [AsvSS 4.14.2c]:
"It has appeared again with its bounty," is a verse in the Bṛhatī meter; "Bring us that wonderful wealth, O Dawn," is a triplet in the Uṣṇih meter.
"Etā ūtī" (these aids)—these four [verses] are in the Jagatī meter; "Mahe no adya"—this is in the Paṅkti meter. Thus ends the morning recitation for Uṣas.
(Soma: Sutyā Day:
Prātar-anuvāka)
Now follows the offering to the Aśvins.
(Soma: Sutyā Day;
Morning Recitation)
*Eṣo uṣāḥ prātar yujā*—these four [verses] for the Aśvins; *yajvarīr iṣaḥ*, *āśvinā aśvāvatyā gomat*, and *ū ṣu nāsatyā*—this triplet [for the Aśvins].
(Soma: Sutyā Day:
Prātar-anuvāka)

From afar, "right here," [he recites] three [verses]; he should omit the last one; "the most carrying of your invocations," four [verses]; "arise both of you," and "to my invocation," [which is] in the Gāyatrī meter.
(Soma: Sutyā Day:
Prātar-anuvāka)
In the hymn beginning with "yad adṛśram" (AśvSS 4.15.2c), the verse "ā no viśvābhiḥ," and "tyam cid atrim"—these are in the Anuṣṭubh meter.
(Soma: Sutyā Day; Prātar-anuvāka)
The hymn *ābhāti agniḥ*, the three verses beginning with *grāvāṇeva nāsatyābhyām*, and the two hymns *dhenuḥ pratnasya* and *ka u śravat*.
(Soma: Sutyā Day;

(Soma: Sutyā Day; Midday Pressing)
(Regarding the *hotraka* recitations:

*tarobhir vaḥ vidadvasum*, *taraṇir it siṣāsati*—these two *pragāthas* serve as the *stotriya* and *anurūpa*. The verse *ud inv asya ricyate* is to be excised; instead, one should insert *bhūya id imām ū ṣu*. In all cases, the *yājyā* is *pibā vardhasva tava dyāḥ sutāsaḥ*.
(Soma: Sutyā Day)
Midday:
(The Śastras of the Hotrakas) AśvSS 5.17.1: Now follows the third pressing, to be performed with the highest tone.
(Soma: Sutyā Day: Evening: Āditya-graha, etc.)
They proceed with the Āditya-graha.
(Soma: Sutyā Day: Evening)
(Regarding the Āditya cup, etc.):
"With the newest protection of the Ādityas, let the Hotṛ sacrifice to the dear Ādityas who possess dear abodes; may the Ādityas and Aditi rejoice!
One should not look at this cup while it is being offered.
(Soma: Sutyā Day: Evening: Āditya-graha, etc.)

Having performed the *manotā* and subsequent rites up to the *paśviḍā* at the *ārbhavapavamāna* laud after having distributed the embers, he performs the animal sacrifice ritual as prescribed, beginning with the *puroḍāśa* offering and ending with the placing of the *nārāśaṃsa* cups.
(Soma: Sutyā Day; Evening)

When [the cups] have been set down—[namely] the Āditya cup and so forth—from the most soft portion of the *puroḍāśa*, they should offer three balls each from their respective cups to their own ancestors, saying: "O fathers, rejoice here; come to your portions as you wish!
(Soma: Sutyā Day)
Evening (such as during an eclipse of the sun, etc.):
Having reached the Āgnīdhrīya fire-altar by circling to the left, all should consume the remnants of the oblation.
(Soma: Sutyā Day: Evening: Āditya-graha, etc.)
"God Savitṛ has become worthy of praise for us; let the Hotṛ worship the god Savitṛ. The god Savitṛ, the domestic one, is most excellent, bestowing jewels upon the fathers in their lifespan.
May he drink the Soma; the sacrifices have gladdened him. Even Parjanya rejoices in his ordinance"—with these words, at the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, the Hotṛ should recite the Vaiśvadeva Śastra.
(Soma: Sutyā Day)
Evening (during the Sāvitra-graha and other rites):
when about to recite, he should meditate upon all the directions.
One should not perform [the ritual] on that day on which one has an enemy.
(Soma: Sutyā Day; Evening)
AśvSS 5.18.4: At the third pressing, during the beginning of the *śastra*s and other rites such as the *sāvitra* cup-offering, the invocation is "O Adhvaryu! Oṃ śauṃsāvaum!
(Soma: Sutyā Day).
Evening: (The *sāvitra* cup, etc.
AśvSS 5.18/5: "We choose that of Savitṛ; O God Savitṛ, do not harm us"—these are the introductory verse (*pratipad*) and the following verse (*anucara*) for the *vaiśvadeva* offering.
"O God, you have come with one, with ten, O Svabhūti, with two for our sacrifice, and with twenty;

with three and with thirty *niyut* teams you carry [the oblation], O Vāyu—unharness them here. "For aid, they fashioned this chariot for Dyāvā," etc., [is] the *Dīrghatamasa* hymn. "They fashioned the chariot for the sake of help, for the one who fashions fair forms; this Vena has impelled those whose mother, the speckled one (*pṛśni*), swells with honeyed milk. Thus [be it] for the Father, the Bull, the possessor of all gods. "May auspicious insights come to us from every side"—these nine verses are dedicated to the Viśvedevas.
(Soma: Sutyā Day; Evening; Sāvitra-graha, etc.)
In the hymns of the Vaiśvadeva, Āgnimāruta, and [other] offerings, one should insert the *nivid*s beginning with those dedicated to Savitṛ.

Evening: (the Sāvitra-graha and so forth).
AśvSS 5.18/8: The three northern [verses] are on the northern [side].
(Soma: Sutyā Day: Evening: Sāvitra-graha, etc.)
Of the hymns, that [deity] is indeed the deity;
for that is the deity of the Soma-pressing day.
The end of the hymn is determined by the deity [of the verse], as in the case of the *sāvitra* cups and so forth; [this applies] up to the *nivid*.
(Soma: Sutyā Day)
Evening: (the *sāvitra* cup, etc.).
AśvSS 5.18/11: And here the *dhāyyā* verses are inserted one by one.
(Soma: Sutyā Day; Evening; Sāvitra-graha, etc.)

He should conclude with the verse, "Aditi is heaven, Aditi is the mid-region," at every Vaiśvadeva [offering]. He recites it twice: first by pādas, then by half-verses, while touching the ground once.
(Soma: Sutyā Day; Evening: Āgnimāruta Śastra)
Having recited the *śastra* with the formula, "The hymn has been spoken for Indra, for the gods; for hearing thee," he should mutter [the *yajyā*]:
"O All-Gods (*viśve devāḥ*), hear this my invocation. This is the *yajyā*.
(Soma: Sutyā Day: Evening: Sāvitra-graha, etc.)
"O Soma, being in harmony with the fathers"— this is the *yājyā* for the offering to Soma.
(Regarding the *saumyacaru*:
They sacrifice on both sides of it silently with clarified butter as the *yājyā*.
(Soma: Sutyā Day)
Evening:
(The *saumya* oblation). Agni has the ghee as his fuel, the ghee as his back; he rests in ghee; ghee is his abode.
"May thy bay steeds, dripping with ghee, carry thee; drinking the ghee, O God, worship the gods"—this [he recites] first.
"O Viṣṇu, stride out widely; make wide room for our dwelling;
drink the ghee, O thou whose source is ghee; further and further extend the lord of the sacrifice"—this [he recites] afterwards.
If [the fire] is on either side, he should murmur only in a low voice: "O Agni and Viṣṇu, your great abode is dear to you both.
(Soma: Sutyā Day; Evening)
Regarding the *saumyacaru*:
having first taken the portion of Soma that has been brought forward, he should look at it with the mantra:
"That eye of yours which is in heaven, which is in the Suparṇa, with which you, O Lord, won the sole sovereignty."
"May Soma, who beholds men, bestow upon me that long and infinite eye of Aditi."
(For the *saumyacaru*):
"Touching the heart, touching the sacrifice, bestowing splendor—bestow splendor upon us!
That mind of mine which has gone to Yama, or that which has strayed elsewhere—"
"O King Soma, we maintain that [power] within us;
and [we pray]: 'May we hear what is auspicious with our ears, O Gods.
(Soma: Day of the Soma-pressing)
In the evening:
(the *saumya-caru*);
with the thumb and the ring finger, he should anoint his eyes with clarified butter and offer it to the Chandogas.
(Soma: Soma-pressing day: Evening: Saumya caru)
When the śalākā sticks have been distributed, the Āgnīdhra offers the Pātnīvata oblation with the verse, "Come hither, O Agni, on the same chariot with these [gods]," reciting it only in a whisper.
(Regarding the *saumyacaru*):
Having approached the Neṣṭṛ by the path for moving between the non-aligned [spaces], and having sat down in his lap, he should consume [the portion].
(Soma: Sutyā Day)
Evening: (the *saumya-caru* offering).
Then, as they had come.
(Soma: Sutyā Day; Evening: Āgnimāruta Śastra)
The *agni-māruta* [offering] is performed immediately.
(Soma: Sutyā Day; Evening Pressing)
(Regarding the *agni-māruta* litany:
Of that [litany], if it is to be recited verse by half-verse (*pacchas*), one should recite the first verse verse by half-verse.
(Soma: Sutyā Day)
Evening:
(The Āgnimāruta Śastra);
the other [verse] by half-verses.
(Soma: Sutyā Day: Evening:
Āgnimāruta Śastra)
The continuity [is established] by means of the final formula.
(Soma: Sutyā Day: Evening)
(Regarding the *agni-māruta* śastra):
*vaiśvānarāya pṛthupājase*, *śaṃ no karaty arvate*, *pra tvakṣasaḥ pratavaso*, *yajñā yajñā vo agnaye*, and *devo vo draviṇodāḥ*—these are the two *pragāthas* serving as the *stotriya* and *anurūpa*.
(Soma: Sutyā days).
Evening:
(The *agni-māruta* śastra).

[He recites] *pratavyasīm*, *tavyasīm*, and the three verses beginning with *āpo hi ṣṭha*. While touching water and being touched by those who have uncovered their heads, he performs the invocation for each verse beginning from this point: two verses beginning with *uta no ahiḥ budhnyaḥ śṛṇotu*, two verses beginning with *devānām patnīr uśatīr avantu naḥ*, and two verses beginning with *rākām aham*.
(Soma: Sutyā Day; Evening: Āgnimāruta Śastra)

*Pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuḥ; imaṃ yama prastaram ā hi sīda; mātali kavyair yamo aṅgirobhir udīratām avare utparāsaḥ; āhaṃ pitṝn suvidatrān avitsi; idaṃ pitṛbhyo namo astv adya; svāduṣ kilāyam iti catasraḥ.* (The four verses beginning: "The daughter of the lightning, of variegated life-span; O Yama, sit down upon this sacrificial grass; may Mātali with the Kavyas and Yama with the Aṅgirases rise up; may those who are below and those who are above [rise]; I have found the benevolent fathers; let there be this homage today to the fathers; for it is indeed sweet. (Soma: Sutyā Day; Evening Libation)

(Regarding the *agni-māruta-śastra*): There is an invocation in the middle [of the verses]: "We rejoice in the gods; we delight in the gods. These are their responses (*pratigara*). [The verses are: "By whose power the worlds were propped up, who by their heroic deeds are most manly and most powerful;
they who advance unassailed by their might" (or: "the two who advance unassailed by their might").
Viṣṇu and Varuṇa have come at the first invocation.
(Soma: Sutyā Day, Evening)
(At the Āgnimāruta-śastra:
He should conclude with the verse, "Viṣṇoḥ nu kaṃ vīryāṇi pravocaṃ tantuṃ tanvan rajasobhānumanvihi | evā na indro maghavā virapśī," while touching the ground.
(Soma: Sutyā Day; Evening: Āgnimāruta Śastra)
With the final utterance, one should await the pouring down of the *dhruva* vessel.
(Regarding the *agni-māruta* *śastra*):
Having recited the *śastra* with "The hymn (*uktha*) has been spoken for Indra; for the gods who have heard thee," he should mutter [the *yajyā*]:
"O Agni, with the Maruts, the radiant singers... This is the *yajyā*.
Thus ends the Agniṣṭoma; [this is] the Agniṣṭoma.
(Soma: Sutyā Day: Evening)
(Regarding the *agni-māruta* litany: But for the *hotraka*s, it is the *uktha*.
(Soma: the *ukthya* sacrifice.)

AsvSS_6.1/2a: “Come hither, O you who speak aloud; Agni has come, the Bhārata, the supporter of the people; that which the Asura supported”—these two triplets [are used]; and for the *indrāvaruṇa* [offering], the *yājyā* is: “O Indra and Varuṇa, you two kings; O Indra and Varuṇa, of the most sweet [Soma]...

AsvSS_6.1/2b: For the *ukthya* [soma], the *pragāthas* are: “We indeed [serve] thee, O matchless one; he who [did] this and that in the past”; all [verses] are in the *kakubh* meter; and the *yājyā* is: “To him who is most gladdening, the one swimming in waters; we have approached Indra; O Bṛhaspati, you two and Indra [rule] over wealth.”
(Soma: Ukthya) AśvSS 6.1/2c:
"For now, O Indra, lover of songs; come, O Indra, lover of songs! The rite is the progenitor...
Now may the mortal become a friend. He [is so] through your deed, O Indra and Viṣṇu, lords of the exhilarations. This is the *yājyā*.
(Soma: Ukthya) Thus ends the Ukthya.
(Soma: Ukthya)
Now follows the *ṣoḍaśī* (the Soma-pressing for the *ṣoḍaśin* cup). "The Soma has been pressed for you, O Indra"— these are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses.
(Regarding the *ṣoḍaśin* [Soma sacrifice]:
"May the bay steeds bring thee hither"—these three verses are in the *gāyatrī* meter.
(Regarding the *ṣoḍaśin*.)
AsvSS 6.2.4: "Upo ṣu śṛṇuhi giraḥ," "Susaṃdṛśaṃ tvā vayam maghavan"—these are one [verse] and two *paṅkti* verses.
AsvSS 6.2.5: "Yad indra pṛtanājye" and "Ayaṃ te astu haryataḥ"—these are two triplets (*ṛcau*) in the *auṣṇiha* and *bārhata* meters.
*ā dhūrṣv asmai* is a *dvipadā*;
*brahman vīra brahmakṛtiṃ juṣāṇaḥ* is a *triṣṭubh*.
This is Brahmā, who is timely; he is celebrated by the name Indra and is praised. O Indra, as the paths are well-known, hundreds [of hymns] flow toward you.
(Soma: Ṣoḍaśin)
"O Lord of Strength, our songs go forth to you like [horses] being yoked"—these are three *dvipadā* verses.
"I shall proclaim for your great [deeds], your two bay steeds"—these are three *jagatī* verses.
"The buffalo at the *trikadruka* [sacrifices], having drunk the barley-mash," and "Forward for him, the chariot-leader"—these two triplets are in the *aticchandas* meter.
(Soma: Ṣoḍaśin) AŚvSS 6.2/7: [He recites] first by quarters, then in two parts.
(Soma: Ṣoḍaśin)
The subsequent [verse] is in the form of an Anuṣṭubh and a Gāyatrī. (Soma:
Ṣoḍaśin) "O wise one, be mindful; drink and rejoice, O you whose will is desire; establish for us great Truth and favor, O Vasu!"—this is the Anuṣṭubh.
"Sing forth the *triṣṭubh* for food; sing it forth!"—these three verses beginning with "He who made the worlds tremble" are in the *anuṣṭubh* meter.
Having left out the last [verse] of the final [stotra], one should insert the final *nivid*.

(Soma: Ṣoḍaśin) AśvSS 6.2/11: We shall explain [the ritual] by means of its characteristic marks and the sequence of the verses: "He devoured the serpent, Vṛtra; he quickened the waters, the source of abundance; he raised up the ocean and the mountains here in heaven.
(Soma: Ṣoḍaśin)
"Ud yad bradhnasya viṣṭapam" is the concluding verse. Having murmured, "Evā hy eva evā hi indram;
evā hi śakro vaśī hi śakra," [he performs the ritual].
He recites the verse: "O Lord of the bay horses (*harivaḥ*), you have drunk of the pressed juices of the ancients.
(Soma: *ṣoḍaśin*) He offers the oblation with the verse:
"O Indra, enjoy [the portion] that has been distributed; come hither, O Hero, with your two bay horses (*harī*)."
Drink of the pressed juice, O Indra, you whose mind is bent toward it, desiring it, lovely for intoxication; fill your belly anew with the honey, as if from heaven.
(Soma: Ṣoḍaśin)
Of this pressed juice, the sweet-sounding exhilarations have approached you;
Indra, the overcomer of the swift, like Mitra, has slain Vṛtra as a Yati;
he shattered the strength like Bhṛgu, and in the intoxication of Soma, he conquered his enemies.
Hear our invocation like Indra; enjoy our songs like the wielder of the thunderbolt.
O Indra, with your companions, bow down to the flashing weapon for the great sport of exhilaration.
May they enter the self like inspired poets; O Indra, may you [be] like Tvaṣṭṛ for our sons.
Fill your two flanks like Soma; O hero, be pleased with our prayer, for it is as effective as a seeker, as a craftsman, as a hero, and like a drinking-cup.
"Like a traveler, like Viṣṇu, yet he is not [merely] that; he is of equal wisdom"—these are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses.
After the *stotriya* and *anurūpa*, one should distribute that very same *śastra*.
(Soma: Ṣoḍaśin) Having placed a footstep between each [verse], he should recite by half-verses.
(Soma: Ṣoḍaśin)
AsvSS_6.3/4: The first verses of the preceding [hymns] are [to be used]. (Soma: the Ṣoḍaśin) AsvSS_6.3/5: The Gāyatrīs are [to be joined] with Paṅktis.
(AśvSS 6.3/6: Regarding the *ṣoḍaśin* [soma]:
Of the *paṅkti* verses, however, two remain; with those two he should chant the *praṇava*.
(Regarding the *ṣoḍaśin* soma.)
With *uṣṇih* and *bṛhatī* [verses], one should make two *uṣṇih* verses out of the final feet;
[in the case of the *ṣoḍaśin* soma sacrifice],
the first [foot] consists of four syllables.
(AśvSS 6.3/9): Having divided the first *dvipadā* into four parts, one should join it with *triṣṭubh*s, and the subsequent ones with *jagatī*s.
(Soma: *ṣoḍaśin*)
AsvSS_6.3/10: Of the last [verse], the fourth syllable is the final [syllable] of the preceding [pāda] and the first syllable of the following [pāda].
(Soma: the *ṣoḍaśin*) AsvSS_6.3/11: One should place [the *ṣoḍaśin*] at the end of the second and third pādas of the two [verses].
"O thou of keen intellect" in the first [verse], and "O thou who art keenly intelligent" in the second.
Having made the other feet the sixth [feet] in the subsequent verses, he should recite them in the form of *anuṣṭubh*s. (Soma: Ṣoḍaśin) AśvSS 6.3/12.
(After the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses), the *ṣoḍaśin* chant is performed with the [verses] distributed from that point onward.
(Soma: the *ṣoḍaśin*)
In that case, the response (*pratigara*) is: "Othāmo daiva! Mademade! Aso daivotha!
(Soma: *ṣoḍaśin*). One should join [the recitation] with the murmuring of the *yājyā* verse.
(Regarding the *ṣoḍaśin* [Soma cup]:
"Thus indeed, O Lord of Bay Horses (*harivas*), you have drunk the pressed juice of the ancients; thus indeed, O Indra, this libation is yours alone.
Thus indeed, O Śakra, intoxicate yourself with the honeyed Soma; for you, O Indra, are the self-controlled Śakra. Pour it down into your belly like rain during the monsoon! Thus [he recites].
(Soma: Ṣoḍaśin) Everything else is the same. (Soma: Ṣoḍaśin) AśvSS 6.3/17: Everything else is the same. (Soma: Ṣoḍaśin)
