(Soma: Caturviṃśa Day) They consume the *ukthapātra* and the goblets between the *atigrāhya* cups during the *niṣkevalya* litany.
(Soma: Caturviṃśa Day) AŚvSS 7.3/23:
The recitation of the *bhakṣa* formulas is obligatory.
(Soma: Caturviṃśa Day)
AsvSS_7.3/24: Those who consume [the Soma] from the *ṣoḍaśin* vessel [do so].
(Soma: Caturviṃśa day) AsvSS_7.4/1:
[The same applies] for the *hotraka*s.

AsvSS_7.4/2a: “*kayā naś citra ābhuvat*, *kayā tvam na ūtyā*, *mā cid anyad viśaṃsata*, and *yac cid dhi tvā janā ime*—these are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses for the Maitrāvaruṇa on the Caturviṃśa day.
(Soma: Caturviṃśa day: Hotrakas)

*AsvSS_7.4 /2b*: "That [Soma] of yours, O wonder-worker, which overcomes death... that strength of yours I seek... toward the one who bestows great wealth, the one well-known as a giver of great wealth... for we, having pressed the juice, [call upon you]... who indeed knows [him] in the pressing? ...the hero who overcomes all hostile armies; that Indra I invoke... O Indra, whatever exists, bring it hither"—thus one verse and two [others].
(Soma: Caturviṃśa Day; Afternoon; Hotrakas)

Indra has grown strong for exhilaration, for at every intoxication he is the giver to us. For our aid, [we call] the maker of fair forms; for our aid, the most powerful one. Like those stretching forth toward the sun, you are indeed great, O Sūrya. Up has risen that visible splendor; up have risen these most honey-sweet [rays]. O Indra, you are preeminent in the races; O Indra, you are glorious. O Indra, bring us wisdom; O Indra, bring us the highest [wisdom]. May a thousand come to you, may a hundred come to you—“I am yours when the sun has risen,” thus [is the hymn] of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.
(Soma: Caturviṃśa Day; Afternoon: Hotrakas)

*Tarobhir vo vidad vasum*, *taraṇir it siṣāsati*, *tvām idāhno naro vayam*, *enam idāhyo yo rājā carṣaṇīnām*, *yaḥ satrahā vicarṣaṇiḥ*, *svādor itthā viṣūvataḥ*, *itthā hi soma in made*, *ubhe yad indra rodasī*, *ava yat tvaṃ śatakrato*, *nakiṣ taṃ karmaṇā naśan*, *na tvā bṛhanto adrayaḥ*, *ubhayaṃ śṛṇavat ca naḥ*, *ā vṛṣasva purūvaso*, *kadācana starīr asi*, *kadācana prayucchasi*, *yad indra bhayāmahe*, *yathā gaura apākṛtam*, *yad indra prāg udag yathā gaura apākṛtam*—these are for the Acchāvāka.
(AśvSS 7.4/5): Regarding the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses, if they should chant the *anurūpa*, the *stotriya* becomes the *anurūpa*.
(Afternoon:

Hotṛakās) Following the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses, the *pragāthas* containing the word *ka-* are: "Who [is] that Indra?", "Thou, O Vasu...", "What new [deed] of the flaxen plants?", and "What indeed has not been done by him? (AśvSS 7.4/6).

AsvSS 7.4/7: "O Indra, drive away all enemies from the front; with the sacred word (*brahman*), I yoke thee who art yoked by the sacred word. O Knower, lead us to a wide world. These are the *ārambhaṇīyā* verses containing the word *kad*.
After the Ārambhaṇīyās, the Maitrāvaruṇa recites daily as his *śastra*: "Sadyo ha jātaḥ" and "Asmā id u pratavase śāsad vahnir," which are the two *ahīna-sūktas*.

(Regarding the Soma sacrifice on the twenty-fourth day: the afternoon session of the Hotrakas) AśvSS 7.4/9: "Ā satyo yātu" is the second *ahīna-sūkta* for the Maitrāvaruṇa; "Ud u brahmāṇi" and "Abhi taṣṭeva" are the other two, to be recited day after day.
(Regarding the *Soma* sacrifice on the twenty-fourth day: the afternoon session of the *Hotraka* priests) AsvSS 7.4/10:
The final [verse] ends with "nūnam sāta."
(Regarding the Soma sacrifice on the Caturviṃśa day, afternoon: the Hotrakas) AŚvSS 7.4/11:
When inserting the stotriya verses of the Ṣaḍaha, they insert the Ahīna-sūktas.

(Regarding the Soma sacrifice on the twenty-fourth day: the afternoon session of the Hotrakas) *ud u ṣya devaḥ savitā hiraṇyayā*—these three [verses]; *te hi dyāvāpṛthivī yajñasya vo rathyam*—this is for the Viśve Devās.
(Regarding the Soma sacrifice on the twenty-fourth day: Afternoon;
The Hotrakas) "For the nourishing, virile host of the virile one, increase through sacrifice"—this is the Āgnimāruta hymn.
(Soma: Caturviṃśa Day;
Afternoon; Hotṛkas) AŚVSS 7.4/14: This day is an Agniṣṭoma.
(Regarding the Soma sacrifice on the twenty-fourth day:
the afternoon session of the Hotrakas) Or it may be an Ukthya. (AśvSS 7.4/15)
(Soma: Caturviṃśa Day; Afternoon; Hotṛakās):
The Abhiplava and Pṛṣṭhya [rites]. ĀśvSS 7.5/1: The Abhiplava and Pṛṣṭhya [rites].
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) The odd days have the *rathantara* as their *pṛṣṭha* chant.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha)
The other [days] have the *bṛhat* as their *pṛṣṭha* chant. (Regarding the *Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*:
on the third day and those following, the *pṛṣṭhya* sequence has, respectively on each day, the *vairūpa*, *vairāja*, *śākvara*, and *raivata* chants for the second [day] onwards.)
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) AśvSS 7.5/5: When performing these according to their proper place, one should recite the *yonis*.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha)
In all cases, the verse-form (*yoni*) belongs to the Aśvin [stotra], except for the [Aśvin] stotra itself. (Soma:
Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) However, even when the *yajñāyajñīya* is not being performed, one should recite its verse-form along with the *anurūpa*, interchanging them after the other *anurūpa*.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) Having extracted the remaining *āvāpa* [verses] for the *hotraka* priests.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha)

*mitram vayam havāmahe*, *mitram huve pūtadakṣam*, *ayaṃ vāṃ mitrāvaruṇā no mitrāvaruṇā*—these are the triplets. (Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) From the four [verses] beginning with *pra vo mitrāya*, one should omit the second; then *pra mitrayor varuṇayoḥ* [six verses], *kāvyebhir adābhyaḥ* [three verses], *mitrasya carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ* [four verses]—these are the Mitra-verses; and *yac cid dhi te viśaḥ* is the Varuṇa-verse.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) AśvSS 7.5/10:
For this [Abhiplava], the Maitrāvaruṇa should insert an additional triplet beyond the regular one, on account of the requirement of the Stoma.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha)
In the fifth and seventeenth [months];
in the ninth and twenty-first;
in the twelfth and twenty-fourth.
Fifteen in the third [turn];
twenty-one in the thirty-third;
thirty-two in the forty-fourth.
Thirty-six [verses] on the forty-eighth day.
(Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) Or there may be one fewer. (AśvSS 7.5:12)
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) In the one-day rites, there may be either one or more [stotras].
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha)
AsvSS 7.5/14: The *ārambhaṇīyā* verses do not occur; the final *tṛcas* of the one-day rites (*aikāhika*) take the place of the *paryāsa* verses.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) AsvSS 7.5/15: For the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, there are six hymns beginning with "surūpakṛtnum ūtaye."
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) Regarding the insertion, it is prescribed by the Maitrāvaruṇa priest.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha)

AsvSS_7.5/17: For the Acchāvāka, [the verses] are "O Indra and Agni, O Indra and Agni, come hither" (RV 7.93.1–2), "I invoke those two for whom this [world exists]" (RV 7.94.1–9), nine verses beginning with "This prayer of yours" (RV 7.95.1–11), and one verse beginning with "For you two are the lords of the sacrifice" (RV 7.96.1).

AsvSS_7.5/18: For the first day of the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, the Marutvatīya [śastra] consists of the hymn beginning with "May Indra come for our aid" (RV 4.20.1–25), and the Niṣkevalya [śastra] consists of the hymn beginning with "Come to us, O Indra" (RV 4.21.1–10).
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) AŚvSS 7.5/19:
When the word "midday" has been uttered, one should attend to these two Śastras.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha)

AsvSS_7.5/20: At the very place of the *ahīna* hymns, the *sampāta* verses are: *evā tvām indra*, *yan na indra*, *kathā mahām indra*, *pūrbhid ya eka id*, *yas tigmaśṛṅga*, *imām ū ṣu*, *icchanti tvā*, *śāsad vahniḥ*.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) AsvSS_7.5/21: For each [verse], there are three [of these].
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) AśvSS 7.5/22: [The rites] have been declared by means of the Marutvatīya offerings.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha)
AsvSS_7.5/23: "They harness the mind here and there," and "He invokes the gods"—these four [verses] constitute the Vaiśvadeva [offering].
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) AsvSS_7.6/1: For the second [day], the Ājya [Stotra] is performed with the Caturviṃśa [Stoma].

(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha: Second Day) AśvSS 7.6/2: Two [verses] beginning with *vāyo ye te sahasriṇaḥ*; one [verse] beginning with *tīvrāḥ somāsa ā gahi*; two [verses] beginning with *bhā devānām api spṛśaḥ*; one [verse] beginning with *śukrasyādya gavāśiraḥ*; and five triplets (*tṛca*) beginning with *ayaṃ vāṃ mitrāvaruṇā*. (Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha: Second Day)
They call this the *Gārtsamada-prauga*.

(Soma: Second day of the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) For the *Marutvatīya* śastra, the opening verses (*pratipad*) and the following verses (*anucara*) are "The Lord of all men, the Master of wealth" and "O Indra, you alone are the Soma-drinker. The midday pressing consists of "O Indra, come to the Soma," "Your aid is most near," and so forth.
(Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha: second day) If Bhāradvāja is the Hotṛ, it is according to the archetype.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha: second day)

The third pressing consists of the Caturviṃśika stoma. "Viśvo devasya netuḥ" is one verse; "tat savitur vareṇyam" consists of two verses; and "ā viśvadevaṃ saptatim" are the opening and following verses for the Vaiśvadeva laud.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha: second day) The Ājya and Prauga śastras, as well as the opening and following verses for both, are thus [arranged] in the even days of the Abhiplava.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha:
Second Day) For the third [day], the midday [pavamāna-stotra] consists of the triplet *yo jāta eva* (TS 2.4.14.1).
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha: Third Day)

AsvSS 7.7/2: For the third [day], there is the Vaiśvadeva [śastra] consisting of the verses "tad devasya ghṛtena dyāvāpṛthivī" and "anaśvo jātaḥ parāvato yaḥ"; the Āgnimāruta [śastra] consisting of "vaiśvānarāya dhiṣaṇām," "dhārāvarā marutaḥ," and "tvam agne prathamo aṅgirāḥ"; and the Niṣkevalya [śastra] consisting of "ugro jajñe. AsvSS 7.7/3: For the fourth [day], the Vaiśvadeva [śastra] consists of "hvayāmy agnim," "asya me dyāvāpṛthivī," three verses beginning with "tatam me apaḥ," and so forth.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha:
Fourth Day) [The verses] beginning with "Vaiśvānara, with the mind" constitute three; and "Those who adorn themselves, the guardians of the people" constitutes the Āgnimāruta hymn.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha: Fourth Day)
AsvSS 7.7/5: For the fifth [day], the midday [stotra] consists of the hymn *kayā śubhā yas tigmaśṛṅgaḥ*.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha: Fifth Day) AsvSS 7.7/6:
However, the ninth and final verses of the *kayāśubhīya* [hymn] are used elsewhere wherever there is a placement of the *nivid*.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha: Fifth Day) AśvSS 7.7/7: "ghṛtavatī bhuvanānām abhiśrīḥ" and "indra ṛbhubhir vājavadbhiḥ"—these two triplets [are used]; "kad u priyāya" is the Vaiśvadeva hymn.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha: Fifth Day)

AsvSS 7.7/8: *pṛkṣasya vṛṣṇo vṛṣṇe śardhāya nū cit sahojā*—this is the *āgnimāruta* [śastra] for the sixth day; the *sāvitra* and the *ārbhava* [śastra] with the third [verse]; and the *vaiśvānarīya* [śastra]. *katarā pūrvā uṣāsānaktā*—this is the *vaiśvadeva* [śastra]. *prayajyavo imam stomam*—this is the *āgnimāruta* [śastra]. (Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha: Day Six) AsvSS 7.7/9: Thus concludes the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha.
(Regarding the *Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*):
It has two *agniṣṭomas* on both sides,
with *ukthyas* in the middle.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) At the Ukthya [sacrifices], there are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha)
Of the Maitrāvaruṇa.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha)

"Come, let me tell you; Agni, the descendant of Bharata, has come to you. "Forward, O Vājas, toward the heavens; forward with your vehicle toward the spoils! "Sing forth to the most bountiful one! Forward, O Agni, with your aids! "We choose for ourselves Agni, your increasing one, at this sacrifice and rite—the most excellent sacrificer. "To him who has kindled [the fire] with an oblation, we would kindle you, O Agni, with fuel. "O radiant one, [bestow] both kinds of clarified butter. (These two verses and one more. "I think of that Agni who is the Vasu. "May Vatsa win your mind. "When he gave, O Agni... "Bring us solid wealth, O most beloved guest, the best, O youngest descendant of Bharata! "Auspicious is Agni when offered to; when indeed he is offered with clarified butter. "Those who kindle Agni—let these [songs] resound toward them."

(Aśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 7.8 / 2a: Now, the *brāhmaṇācchaṃsin* [recites]: "O you who have no rival, you who are not subject to old age; as you are, so indeed are you full of heroes. For such is his gracious bounty (*sūnṛtā*). We celebrate that exhilaration of yours; sing forth toward it! And we, O matchless one..."
(Regarding the *ukthya* days of the *Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*: Soma) AŚvSS 7.8 / 2b:

O friends, let us sing this very *sāman* for Indra as we did of old; may we obtain our blessings. He alone bestows [wealth], he who is the sole Soma-drinker, O Indra. Come, O Indra, to us; indeed, come to the more intoxicating sweetness. Come now, O friends, let us praise Indra.
(Regarding the *ukthya* days of the *Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*:
Soma) "Praise Indra as Vyaśva did"— [or] "as Viśva did."

"O Indra, bring [the wealth]; we indeed [call] you, O matchless one—[you who were] not here before; come hither to these drops"—this is the *samāhārya* (collective) *anurūpa* (corresponding verse), which is without a rival (*abhrātṛvya*) and without a peer (*anā*). "Do not [be like] one who does not grow old for thee"—thus [it is].
(The *ukthya* days of the *Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha* of the Soma sacrifice).

Now, for the Acchāvāka: "Indra, all [the Maruts] have strengthened thee; the hymn is to be recited for Indra. Hear the call! O Tiraścī, hear with attentive ears! Hear the call! Soma has been pressed, O Indra; drink this, O Indra! O Indra, since you, wondrous and mighty, are most effective for our aid—the breaker of forts, the youthful sage—for you are a bull for the sake of bestowing bounty. The singers of Gāyatrī verses sing to you; you are the soul of songs, like a charioteer. (Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha: Ukthya days)
Having left out one hymn from each of the *sūktas*, they should insert [the inserted verses].
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha: Ukthya days)
When the Stoma is increasing:
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha: Ukthya days).

The Maitrāvaruṇa [recites] according to the purpose: the three verses beginning with *imā u vām bhṛmayaḥ manyamānāḥ*, the two hymns beginning with *indrā ko vām*, and from the hymn beginning with *śruṣṭī vām yajño yuvām narā punīṣe vām*, the verses beginning with *imāni vām bhāgadheyāni*.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha: Ukthya days)
The Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin [recites] the hymn beginning with "yas tastambha yo adribhid yajñe divaḥ" and "asteva suprataram āyātvin draḥ svapatis imām dhiyam.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha: Ukthya days)
For the Acchāvāka, the hymn is "viṣṇor nu kam" and the verse "paro mātrayā.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha: Ukthya days)
The first two days of the *pṛṣṭhya* [ṣaḍaha] are explained by means of the *abhiplava*; they are performed according to the first two [days].
(Soma: *pṛṣṭhya* ṣaḍaha:
Days 1–3) And the third pressings (*tṛtīyasavana*) are likewise performed day after day.
(Regarding the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*:
first three days) On the first day, the *ājya* [laud] begins with "upa prayantaḥ";
on the second day, it begins with "agniṃ dūtam".
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha:
Days 1–3) At the third [day], the Ājya[-śastra] is "yukṣva hi.
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha: Days 1–3)

AśvSS 7.10/5: *vāyav ā yāhi vītaye*—one verse; *vāyo yāhi śivā divaḥ*—two verses; *indraś ca vāyav eṣāṃ sutānām*—of these two [verses], one of them twice; *ā mitre varuṇe vayam*, *aśvināv eha gacchatam*, *ā yāhy adribhiḥ sutam*, *sajūr viśvebhir devebhir uta naḥ priyāpriyāsu*—this is the *auṣṇiha-prauga*.
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha: Days 1–3) AśvSS 7.10/6: In the last [verse], there are four-syllable repetitions after each *ṛc*.
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha: Days 1–3) AśvSS 7.10/7: Or rather not. (Soma:
Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha: Days 1–3)
The midday pressing is prescribed by the third *ābhiplavika* [day].
For the *marutvatīya* śastra, the opening verse (*pratipad*) and the following verses (*anucarau*) are "These three Soma-draughts of Indra for great bounty.
If the *pṛṣṭha-stotra* is the Vairūpa, the two *pragāthas*, "O Indra, when the hundred heavens... and "As many as you are, O Indra...", serve as the *stotriya* and *anurūpa*.
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha: First–Third Days) AśvSS 7.11/1: On the fourth day, the nyūṅkha occurs at the beginning of the first half-verse of the morning litany (prātar-anuvāka).
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha: Fourth Day)
A second *o*-vowel, consisting of three morae (*trimātra*), acute (*udātta*), is recited three times. (Soma:
Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, Fourth Day) Following each of these, one should recite an unlimited number—or five—of half-*o*-vowels (*ardha-okāra*) which are grave (*anudātta*).
(AsvSS 7.11/4): But for the last [day], three [verses].
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha: Fourth Day)
When the *nyūṅkha* is being performed, the first syllable is struck down.
We shall cite that as well for the sake of illustration. (Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, Fourth Day) AsvSS 7.11/6.
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-Ṣaḍaha: Fourth Day) AśvSS 7.11/7: *Om Iṭṭeḍ*. (Soma:
Pṛṣṭhya-Ṣaḍaha: Fourth Day)
AsvSS 7.11.8: "Agni with his own chosen hymns"—this is the *ājya* [stotra].
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, Fourth Day) AsvSS 7.11.9:
In its third quarters, excluding the last one, there is the *nyūṅkha* and the *ninarda*.
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, Fourth Day) The nyūṅkha has been explained.
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, Fourth Day)
The *catur-ninarda* [chant] begins with the *svara* (intonation) and ends with the syllable *o*; it consists of four *ninardas*.
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, Fourth Day) The first and the last [syllables] are acute (*udātta*).
The other two [syllables] are anudātta;
the following one is anudāttatara.
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha: Fourth Day)
The first [syllable] is protracted;
the last ends in the letter *m*.
We shall provide an example to illustrate this as well.
(For the Soma sacrifice: the Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, Fourth Day) ĀśvSS 7.11/14:
"Like Agni with our own chosen hymns, we choose you as the Hotṛ."
Om Iṭṭeḍ.
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha: Fourth Day) AśvSS 7.11/15: Om Iṭṭeḍ. (Soma)
*Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*:
(Fourth day) Alternatively, there is the fourfold *ninarda* consisting of "the acute from the grave," "the circumflex," and "the acute.
(Soma: *Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*: Fourth day)
AsvSS_7.11/17: Om Iṭṭeḍ. (Soma:
Pṛṣṭhya-Ṣaḍaha, Fourth Day) AsvSS_7.11/8: From the first half-oṃkāra, the Adhvaryu should perform the nyūṅkha.
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha: Fourth Day) From the first or from the second [stotra].
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha: Fourth Day)
AśvSS 7.11/20: Some [teachers] say there should be a cessation.
AśvSS 7.11/21: Or rather, it should be performed in whatever way they may intend to accomplish it.
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, Fourth Day) AŚvSS 7.11/22:

(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, Fourth Day) When the Stoma is increasing, they should insert eight-verse hymns beginning with "Who today, the manly one... (*ko adya naryaḥ*), "With the wood... (*vanena vāya*), and "Come hither, toward us" (*ā yāhy arvāṅ*); these are the *Ariṣṭāt* hymns of Parucchepa.

They should also insert those verses that are not excessively praised, which are addressed to Indra, composed in the Triṣṭubh metre, and do not contain the word "Maruts.

(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-Ṣaḍaha: Fifth Day) AśvSS 7.12/4: At the morning pressing, [he recites] with one or two [verses].

(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, Fifth Day) For the fifth [day], there are nine verses for the Ājya-stotra, beginning with "imam ū ṣu vaḥ" and "atithim uṣarbudham."

(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha: Fifth Day) *Ā no yajñaṃ divispṛśam*—these two [verses]; *ā no vayo mahetana*—this one; *rathena pṛthupājaseti bahavaḥ sūracakṣasaḥ*, *imā u vāṃ diviṣṭayaḥ*, *pibā sutasya rasinaḥ*, *devaṃ-devaṃ vo avase*, *devaṃ-devaṃ bṛhad u gāyiṣe vācaḥ*—thus is the Bārhata Prauga.
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha: Fifth Day)
Some [recite] the *pragāthas*, excluding the second and the last. (Soma:

If the *pṛṣṭha-stotra* is based on the *Śākvara-sāman*, the *stotriya* consists of the *Mahānāmnī* verses.
Including the *adhyardhakāra*, there are nine [verses] according to the original form; thus they become three.
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, Fifth Day) AśvSS 7.12/11: With these, one should continue the *purīṣapadas*.

Or rather, all [the verses] according to the conclusion of the night.

At the conclusion of those two [stotras], for the Marutvatīya, [the verse] is "O Śatakratu, you who have won the spoils" (RV 8.96.14). For the Niṣkevalya, [the verse] is "O Lord of Might, blameless one" (RV 6.51.1). This applies to each Niṣkevalya.
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-Ṣaḍaha:
Fifth Day) At the morning pressing of the sixth day, having placed other [verses] before the *prasthitayājyās*, they sacrifice with both [the *yājyā* and *anuvākyā*] without pausing.

AśvSS 8.1/2: “O bull Indra, the drops are for the bull-drinker; we have pressed [the juice] with the stones—come hither! For the one who presses gains a dwelling through abundance. [He recites: “I consider Agni to be the munificent Hotṛ-priest; Dadhyañc, the ancient Aṅgiras, [knew] my birth.

"Free from disease in speech, most gracious— may that god Savitṛ, the lord of wealth, impel [us] for both well-dwelling realms, O skillful one. These two are the opening verse (*pratipad*) and the following verse (*anucara*) for the Vaiśvadeva laud.
Having extracted the last three hymns, [he recites them]. (Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, sixth day) AśvSS 8.1/19: Having extracted the last three hymns.

Vālakhilya)

The first [verse] of the former [day] with the second of the latter;

(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, sixth day) In this manner, with mutual interlacing, [he recites] by half-verses for the latter [day]; in this manner, with mutual interlacing, [he recites] verse by verse for the latter [day].

Again, by triplets, by half-verses, and by feet; the seventh [time] likewise.

Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 8.2.16: "O you two kings," etc., is the regular [chant] belonging to the one-day rite.
(Soma: Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, last day)
Thus [are] the two *hauṇḍinas*. (Soma:
Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, sixth day) Now follows the Mahāvālabhida.

Regarding the first *pṛṣṭha-stotra*:

The Viṣuvat day is characterized by the *divākīrtya* chant.

when it has been recited, the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin [recites].

The *kāyānaścitras* [is the stotra],
the *kas tvā satyaḥ* [is the śastra];
the *acchāvāka* [recites] the *kāleya*.
(With the *Soma* hymn *Viśvajit*: "May he who finds wealth through his powers find you;
the swift one indeed desires to win."

"By your songs, find the possessor of wealth.

The *sāmans* and *sūktas* beginning with "satrāmadāsaḥ," "yo jāta eva," and "abhūr ekaḥ" are prescribed for the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*). The third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*) is as previously described. On the final day of the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*, the opening hymn (*pratipad*) and the following hymn (*anucara*) are those belonging to the one-day sacrifice (*aikāhika*). If the *bṛhat-sāman* is used for the *agniṣṭoma-stotra*, the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses are "tvam agne yajñānām. This constitutes the nine-night rite (*navarātra*).
(Soma: Viśvajit; Commentary on the Navarātra).
The Abhijit with *svarasāman* chants, the Viṣuvat, the Gargatrirātra with *svarasāman* chants, and the Viśvajit—all together are Agniṣṭomas.
(Soma sacrifice: Viśvajit)
Some [teachers] say that the *uktha* chants have the *svara-sāman* melodies.

The Gaurivīta and Āyuṣya [stotras] follow.

From the even days arranged as a *ṣaḍaha* comes the *gauh*; from the odd days, the *āyus*.
(Soma: Viśvajit)
In the ten-night [sacrifice]:
(the Viśvajit Soma sacrifice) consists of the Pṛṣṭhya Ṣaḍaha, the first Tryaha, and again the Candomas.

At the Vaiṣuvata, the Nivid is placed both before and after [the stotra].

(Soma: Viśvajit) For the second [stotra], the Marutvatīya consists of: "Recite! Great art thou," "Even the great, O Indra," "Drink the Soma," "Toward him," "Heaven and Earth," "Great is Indra," and "Like a man."

(Soma: Viśvajit) AśvSS 8.7/23: "The unprecedented ones, the most numerous... (*apūrvyā purutamāni*); "At this pressing, proclaim that fame of yours, O great Indra, who [prevailed] even from heaven... (*sute kīrtim tvam mahān indra yo ha divaś cid asya*); "You are great, O Indra, for you... (*tvam mahān indra tubhyam iti*). This is the *niṣkevalya* śastra. "Indra has sung the *svāhā*-hymn; mount your two bay horses, O exhilarating one; these [songs] are for you... (*indraḥ svāhā gāyat sāma tiṣṭhā harī pramandina imā u tvā iti*). This is the *marutvatīya* śastra. (Soma: Viśvajit)

The *niṣkevalya* [śastra] consists of the hymn beginning with "And they have come together" (*sam ca tve jagmuḥ*), followed by "May the Truthful One come" (*ā satyo yātu*), "I have become" (*aham bhuvam*), and "Therein is power" (*tatra indriyam*). Then follow the two-footed verses (*dvipadā*) beginning with "Come with thy wood" (*ā yāhi vanasā*), "Now these" (*imā nu kam*), and "The brown one alone" (*babhruḥ ekaḥ*). These are placed before the *vaiśvadeva* hymns.
(Soma: Viśvajit; Vaiśvadeva hymn:)
"This [hymn] of yours, from this thought"—
thus is the *samūḷha* [chant].
(The *viśvajit* [soma sacrifice]).
If the *pṛṣṭhya* [stotra] has been expanded (*vyūḍha*), one should insert the *nivid*s during the midday pressings on the three subsequent days, after reciting the *gāyatra* triplets:

"I now invoke this Mayin," "That one of yours, the ever-conquering," "The bountiful Indra, the Marut-like," "We seek to win that Indra," and "This indeed, by which this [world] exists; come to our pressed [soma] with your bay steeds. (Soma: The Expanded Ten-Day Rite)
(Soma: the expanded ten-night sacrifice) AśvSS 8.8/3: Their third pressings consist of *triṣṭubh* verses.

On the fourth day: "May the god go forth" (Ā devo yātu) and "Toward the heavens" (pra dyāvah)—these are the Vasiṣṭha verses; "Toward the Ṛbhus" (pra ṛbhubhyaḥ) and "The bright one shall go forth" (pra śukra etu)—these are the Vaiśvadeva verses; "In the favor of Vaiśvānara" (vaiśvānarasya sumatau), "Who indeed? (ka īm), "The distinct ones" (vyaktāḥ), "Agni, O men! (agnim naraḥ)—these are the Āgnimāruta verses.
In the last [round], there are eighteen Virāj verses.
(Soma: expanded ten-night rite) In the eleventh day, there are two *dvipadā* verses, the *māruta* hymn, the twenty-one-fold stoma, and the *vaiśvadeva* hymn.
(Soma: expanded ten-night rite)

For the fifth [day]: "ud u ṣya devaḥ savitā damūnā" (AŚS 7.1.20)—these three; "mahī dyāvāpṛthivī iha jyeṣṭhe" (AŚS 7.2.1)—these four; and "ṛbhuḥ vibhvā stuṣe janaṃ" (AŚS 7.3.1)—this is for the Viśvedevas.
For the [next] day: "vapuḥ nu tad agniḥ hotā gṛhapatiḥ sa rājā" (AŚS 7.4.1)—these three; this is for Agni and the Maruts. The last [verse] of the Vaiśvadeva hymn is that which belongs to the Sādhyas.
The *jātavedasya* [śastra] is the best. (Soma:
the expanded ten-night sacrifice) AśvSS 8.8.7:
In all cases, having combined the *adhyāsa*s, one should chant the *praṇava*.

(Soma: Expanded Ten-Day Rite) AśvSS 8.8: For the sixth day, [the Śastra] consists of the Gārtsamada hymn beginning with "ud u ṣya devaḥ," the thirteen verses of the Ārbhava hymn beginning with "kim u śreṣṭhaḥ," and from the Vaiśvadeva hymns, one should omit the final triplet; this constitutes the Vaiśvadeva Śastra.
(Soma: Expanded Ten-Day Rite)
"ahaś ca kṛṣṇam," "madhvo vaḥ nāma saprathāḥ"—with these [verses], the Āgnimāruta [śastra] is performed.
Thus concludes the Pṛṣṭhya [day].
(Soma: the Vyūḍha Daśarātra)
Now follow the *chandomas*.
(Soma: the expanded ten-night sacrifice;
first *chandoma* day)

"From the ocean, a wave... (RV 7.49.1); "O Vāyu, come hither, drinker of the pure, to us with thy teams; thou goest toward the donor... (RV 7.92.1); "With thy hundredfold teams, O Vāyu, come to our sacrifice... (RV 1.135.1); "The swift presser has stood forth at the sacrifices; O Vāyus, gladdening Indra... (RV 1.135.2); "Those hundred teams of yours, those thousand... (RV 1.135.3)—these are the *ekapātinī* verses. "As we compete for you, O Mitra and Varuṇa... (RV 1.152.1); "Come to us, O Nāsatyas, on your chariot rich in cattle... (RV 1.47.1); "O God, come to us with power, O Śuṣṇin... (RV 1.176.1); "The god-fearing have praised you in the sacrifices... (RV 1.176.2); "With water and nourishment he has flowed forth... (RV 1.176.3)—this is the *prauga*.
At the midday pressing, having exchanged the two hymns (*sūkta*), one should place the *nivid*s in the other two [hymns].
In this same manner, [the procedure is followed] for the fourth and fifth days of the subsequent [portion]. (AśvSS 8.9/4: Thus for the two following [days], the fourth and the fifth.)
(Regarding the Soma sacrifice with the expanded ten-night rite:

the first Chandoma day) [The verses] "O God Savitṛ, toward you," "May the two auspicious ones of the sacrifice go forward," and "This [offering] for the god's birth"—these three ṛcs [are used]; and "With these, O Agni, for our service" is the Vaiśvadeva hymn.
(Regarding the Soma sacrifice: the expanded ten-night rite;
the first Chandoma day) AśvSS 8.9/6: The *dvipadā* hymns are recited as the regular [verses].
(Vyūḍha-ten-day Daśarātra:
First Chandoma Day) AśvSS 8.9/7: "Vaiśvānara has generated..."—this is the first [verse]. "He has ordained everything; the self-controlled one releases the seasons."
May you extend the vigor of the sacrifice. O purifying Agni Vaiśvānara, shine forth as a bull with radiant splendor,
being invoked by the Jamadagnis.
"Prayad vas triṣṭubham dūtam vaḥ"— this is the Āgnimāruta [śastra] for the first Chandoma day of the ten-night rite in its expanded form.
For the second [day]: *agnim vo devam* [is the yājyā]; *kuvid aṅga*, *namasā ye vṛdhāsaḥ*, *pīvoannān rayivṛdhaḥ*, *sumedhāḥ*, *ucchann uṣasaḥ sudinā ariprāḥ*—these are the *ekapātinī* verses.
(Soma: Vyūḍha-daśarātra: Second Chandoma day)

"Rich in food, increasers of wealth" (AśvSS 8.10/1b); "The two willing messengers, protectors against the roaring [foe], as much as there is speed in their bodies, as much as there is vigor"—this is one verse; and two verses: "Toward you both at the rising of the sun with hymns; the cow milking the desirable [milk] of the ancient one; O wise Indra, come to the prayers; Agni, standing upright, has sent forth his favor for the sake of wealth; and may this Sarasvatī be pleased with us"—this is the *prauga* (for the Soma sacrifice: the expanded ten-night rite).
On the second *chandoma* day:
"hiraṇyapāṇim ūtaye" (four verses), "mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ" and "yuvānā pitarā punar" (two *ṛc*s), and "devānām id ava" constitute the *vaiśvadeva* śastra.
(Soma: the *vyūḷha-daśarātra*)
On the second Chandoma day:
"We implore the observer of cosmic order, Vaiśvānara, the lord of the light of cosmic order,
the imperishable heat."

(In the *Cm* commentary, this refers to the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*).
The animal to be bound at the end is dedicated to Bṛhaspati.
(In the *Cm* commentary, this refers to the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*).
In place of the Varuṇapraghāsa offerings, there is a two-day period.
(pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha in Cm) On the morning of the following day, they should cause the Varuṇapraghāsa oblations to follow after the sacrificial cakes at the morning pressing.
(pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha in Cm)
AsvSS 9.2/10: There are two animals dedicated to the Maruts and Varuṇa.
(In the *Cm*, this refers to the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*).
AsvSS 9.2/11: The *anūbandhyā* cow is dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa.
In the place of the Agniṣṭoma and Aindrāgna [stotras],
[the Pṛṣṭhas are performed] during the Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha.
In place of the Sākamedha, there is a three-day period ending with an Atirātra [following the Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha].
On the second day, at each pressing, the sacrificial cakes (puroḷāśas) take the place of the oblations offered on the preceding day.
(pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha in Cm) On the third day, having offered the Upāṃśu and Antaryāma cups, [he offers] the Paurṇadarva;
at the morning pressing, the Kraiḷina.
At the midday [pressings] of the Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, there are the Māhendras.
Between the *ghṛta-yājyā* and the *dakṣiṇa*, the *mārjālīya* fire is used for the ancestral rites (*pitryā*).
(In the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*, according to the *Cm* commentary).
Therein, the attendance [of the fires] is as it is for those who perform the rite without over-kindling.
(pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha in Cm) After the animal-cake offering of the Anūbandhyā cow, they should cause the Āditya [offering] to follow.
(pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha in Cm)
The sacrificial animals are dedicated to Agni, to Indra-Agni, and to the eleven [deities]. (In the *Cm*, this refers to the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*).
The *anūbandhyā* cow is dedicated to Sūrya.
In the place of the Śunāsīrīya sacrifice, there is an Agniṣṭoma within the Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha.
At the morning pressings, they should offer the oblations of the Śunāsīrīya in addition to the sacrificial cakes (puroḷāśa).
(pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha in Cm) An animal sacrifice dedicated to Vāyu.
(pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha in Cm)
The *anūbandhyā* animal sacrifice belongs to Aśvinī.
(In the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*,
according to Cm) fifty cows are given as sacrificial fees every day.
(Regarding the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha* in Cm):
Now follow the *Rājasūya* sacrifices. (The *Rājasūya*) 2.
Prior to the full moon of the month of Phālguna, he should perform the *abhyārohaṇīya* Agniṣṭoma sacrifice with the *pavitra* rite. (The *Rājasūya*)
AsvSS_9.3/3: One performs the Cāturmāsya sacrifices on the full moon day of Phālguna. (Rājasūya) AsvSS_9.3/4: The seasonal junctions (*parvan*) are obligatory. (Rājasūya) AsvSS_9.3/5:
However, they proceed with the two wheels during the intervals between the junctions. (Rājasūya)
A reversal of the day or a reversal of the fortnight. (Rājasūya) At the end of the year, within the same fortnight, the Abhiṣecanīya and Daśapeya sacrifices take place.
(Rājasūya) The Abhiṣecanīya is an Ukthya sacrifice with the Bṛhat-pṛṣṭha stotra and both Sāmans. (Rājasūya)

AśvSS 9.3.9: When the Marutvatīya [offering] has been completed, sitting on a golden cushion to the south of the Āhavanīya fire, he shall recite the Śunaḥśepa narrative for the king who has been consecrated and is surrounded by his sons and ministers. AśvSS 9.3.10: Sitting on a golden cushion he recites; sitting on a golden cushion he receives it. Gold is indeed glory (*yaśas*); thus he endows him with glory. AśvSS 9.3.11: "Om" is the response (*pratigara*) for the triplet of verses; "evam tathā" is the response for the *gāthā*. (Rājasūya)

"Om" indeed belongs to the divine, and "tathā" belongs to the human. By means of both the divine and the human, he releases him from evil sin. (Rājasūya) Therefore, whatever king has been victorious, even if he is not performing a sacrifice, he should have this narrative of Śunaḥśepa recited; for not even the slightest sin remains in him.
He should give a thousand [cows] to the narrator. (Rājasūya)
A hundred [cows] for one who recites excessively. (Rājasūya) Each according to his own seat.
(Rājasūya) Having performed the Saṃsṛp offerings, he should sacrifice with the Daśapeya. (Rājasūya)
AśvSS 9.3/18: There, they should consume the goblets one by one, ten persons each.

AśvSS 9.3/19: Having enumerated those who are permanent [participants], they should cause the others to approach. AśvSS 9.3/20: Those who have maintained their lineage for ten generations on both the mother’s and father’s side through learning, austerity, and meritorious deeds—those whose Brāhmaṇahood has not been led away from on either side—[they should cause to approach].
AsvSS 9.3.21: "From the father," say some. (Rājasūya) AsvSS 9.3.22:
Regarding the two [hymns] beginning with *navagvāsaḥ sutasomāsa indram* and *sakhā ha yatra sakhibhir navagvaiḥ*, these are the first of the Nivid-hymns. (Rājasūya) AsvSS 9.3.23:
One should recognize that these have been described as being at the head of the hymns (*sūktamukhīya*). (Rājasūya)

AśvSS 9.3.24: During the waxing fortnight of the moon, there is an Atirātra sacrifice with the Bṛhat-sāman as the Pṛṣṭha-stotra, at which the hair is shaved. (Rājasūya) AśvSS 9.3.25: After two months have passed, there is a two-day Vyuṣṭi sacrifice.
(Rājasūya) AśvSS 9.3.26: The first day is an Agniṣṭoma.
The *sarvastoma* *atirātra* follows.
(Rājasūya) AśvSS 9.3.27: In the subsequent fortnight of the waxing moon, there is the *kṣatrasya dhṛti* *agniṣṭoma*. (Rājasūya) AśvSS 9.4.1: Thus end the Rājasūya sacrifices. (Rājasūya)

In the Rājasūya, the sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇās) are to be determined according to the established rule, except for the Abhiṣecanīya and the Daśapeya. However, at the Abhiṣecanīya, thirty-two thousand [gold pieces] each are given separately to the principal leaders;
sixteen thousand each are given to the second group.

AsvSS_9.4/5: Eight [cows] each for those who receive a third share; four each for those who receive a quarter share. (Rājasūya) AsvSS_9.4/6: For the Saṃsṛp offerings: a golden [cow] for the offering to Agni; a heifer for Sarasvatī; one with a broken back for Savitṛ; a dark-colored one for Pūṣan; a white-backed one for Bṛhaspati; a bull for Indra; and a large castrated ox for Varuṇa.
(Rājasūya) AśvSS 9.4.7: The Daśapeya consists of one thousand [cows]. (Rājasūya) AśvSS 9.4.8: And these are the prescribed sacrificial fees. (Rājasūya)
A golden garland for the Udgātṛ;
(in the Rājasūya) a horse for the Prastotṛ; a cow for the Pratihartṛ. (In the Rājasūya)
A goat for the Subrahmaṇyā priest. (Rājasūya) Two golden mirrors for the Adhvaryu. (Rājasūya) Two silver ones for the Pratiprasthātṛ.
(Rājasūya)
AsvSS 9.4/14: Twelve cows, a sixth of which are to be led away, and pregnant ones are for the Brahman. (Rājasūya) AsvSS 9.4/15: A barren cow is for the Maitrāvaruṇa.
(Rājasūya) AsvSS 9.4/16: A golden plate is for the Hotṛ. (Rājasūya)
In the Rājasūya: a bull for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin;
a garment of cotton for the Potṛ;
a linen mantle for the Neṣṭṛ.

AsvSS 9.4/18: A cart yoked with a single animal and filled with barley belongs to the Acchāvāka. (Rājasūya) AsvSS 9.4/20: A heifer belongs to the Unnetṛ; a three-year-old bull that has not been castrated belongs to the Grāvastut.
(Rājasūya) AsvSS 9.5/1: One who considers himself as if swallowed by poison should perform the sacrifice with the Uśanas-stoma.
(Uśanas-stoma, etc. AśvSS 9.5/2: For the Uśanas-stoma and others, the *sūktamukhīyas* are: "When you came with the Sahasyas, O Uśanas," and "When you protected the waters for Vaśā.

For the Go-stoma, Bhūmi-stoma, and Vanaspati-sava sacrifices, the *sūktamukhīyas* are: "Neither does the horse with dust on its tail reach them," "They do not perish, nor does the thief harm them," "Truly, even the firm places of the mountains," "O Vanaspati, [you who carry] the oblations," and "O Vanaspati, having bound [them] with a rope. These are the *sūktamukhīyas*.
(Regarding the *uśanaḥstoma* and others:
One who desires sovereignty or one who desires spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*) should sacrifice with the *bṛhaspatisava*.
(Regarding the *uśanaḥstoma* and others:)
For that [rite], the *ṛcas* take the place of the *sūktas* (such as the *Uśanas-stoma*, etc.).

*agnir deveṣu rājati* (Agni reigns among the gods)—this is the *ājya* [stotra]; *yas tastambha dhunotayaḥ*—these two are the opening verses of the hymns (*sūktamukhīye*); *indra marutva iha*, *u tvā*, and *ud u ṣya devaḥ savitā hiraṇyayā*, *ghṛtavatī bhuvanānām abhiśriyā*, *indra ṛbhubhir vājavadbhiḥ samukṣitam*, and *svasti no mimītām aśvinā bhagaḥ*—this is the *vaiśvadeva* [stotra]; having mentally perceived Agni Vaiśvānara with the thought "Agni," [the verses] *prayantu vājās taviṣībhir agnayaḥ* and *samiddham agnim samidhā girā gṛṇe*—this is the *āgnimāruta* [stotra]. After the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses, the *hotraka*s should recite the first and last triplets (*ṛca*s).
But at the midday [pressing], [the recitation] is from the *pragāthas* (AśvSS 9.5/6).
(The *uśanaḥ-stoma*, etc.)
At each pressing, there are eleven sacrificial gifts each.
(The Uśanas-stoma, etc. Or else, there are eleven thousand [cows] each.
(Uśanas-stoma, etc.
Or [one hundred] hundreds. (Uśanas-stoma, etc. AśvSS 9.5/9: Or [one hundred] hundreds. (Uśanas-stoma, etc.)
AśvSS 9.5/10: At the midday pressing, a horse is added [to the sacrificial animals] (such as in the Uśanas-stoma and others).
AśvSS 9.5/11: One who has rivals and desires to overcome them should perform this sacrifice.
(Uśanas-stoma, etc.
AśvSS 9.5/12: One who desires heaven [should perform] the Sadyaskriyā, the Anukriyā, or the Parikriyā. (Uśanas-stoma, etc.)
One who desires food should perform [the sacrifice] with the *ekatrika* or the *tryeka* [stomas] (such as the *uśanas-stoma*,
etc.). One who desires that his offspring should be inclined toward giving should perform [the sacrifice] with the *gotama-stoma*.
The recitation for these seven [sacrifices], beginning with the *uśanas-stoma*,
has been explained by means of the *bṛhaspati-sava*.

You are the image of the earth; you have become great through the sacred word (*brahman*), O Indra. As soon as you were born, you became a youthful bull; even as soon as you were born, O Indra, the gods indeed followed you for the sake of slaying [Vṛtra]. To the great Indra, [this] was offered. (The *Uśanas-stoma*, etc.)

AsvSS 9.5: “How indeed do you attend [to me], O wise one?”—these two [verses]; “Of even one of me, the powerful one, is your strength”; “Now you alone, the lord of the people, belonging to the five tribes”; “Aryaman among men at the assembly of the gods”; “Forward now the great deeds of this great one”; “For thus indeed, O Soma, in intoxication, Indra has grown strong for exhilaration”—these are the opening verses of the hymns (the *sūktamukhīyas*, such as those of the *Uśanas-stoma*).
AsvSS 9.6.1: They perform the Gotama-stoma, which is an *antar-ukthya*.
(ṅotama.stoma) AśvSS 9.6/2:

If there is an Ukthya following the cups, one should insert [the verses] "O Agni, drink with the Maruts, the singers; O Indra and Varuṇa, rejoice; O Indra and Bṛhaspati; O Indra and Viṣṇu, together" into the Āgnimāruta [laud] before the concluding verse (paridhānīyā).
(ṅotama.stoma)
AśvSS 9.6.3: There is an invitation for both. (The *gotamastoma*. AśvSS 9.6.4: Some say there is [an invitation] for only one of the two.
If [the *ukthya* sacrifice] occurs during the *stotriya* verses, it is performed with the *yajñāyajñīya* [sāman]; or, according to the *gotama-ṣṭoma*, with its own [verses].
(ṅotama-ṣṭoma) AśvSS 9.6/5: Or with its own [verses]. (ṅotama-ṣṭoma)
Having called [the Hotṛ] once, [he recites] the stotriyas;
likewise the anurūpas. (The Gomat-stoma)
In other cases as well, it is the same when there is a conjunction of the *stotriya* and the *anurūpa*.
(The *gotama-stoma*) But if, indeed, [the *yajñāyajñīya*] occurs in its own source (*yoni*), then it should be according to the original form with all the *ukthya-sāmans*. In that case, it is so.
(ṅotama.ṣtoma) One practicing sorcery should sacrifice with the Śyena and Ajira [rites]. (Śyena, etc.
The midday [pressings] are performed with the verses: "I am Manu in the womb," "Now he is born together with thee," and "O Manyu, he who is thine, O Manyu. (Śyena, etc.)
The remainder [of the ritual] is according to the Bṛhaspatisava. (Śyena, etc.
The sacrificial grass (*barhis*) is made of *śara* reeds. (Śyena, etc.
The enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) are made of *musala* wood. (Śyena, etc.)
A fuel-stick of *vaibhītaka* wood; (the Śyena, etc.
Or a butcher; (the Śyena, etc. Having made a threatening gesture, he should cause the announcement to be made; (the Śyena, etc.)
And he should cause the response to be made. (The Śyena, etc.
He should utter the *vaṣaṭ* as if cutting [the offering]. (The Śyena, etc.
He should offer as if striking with a stone.
(Śyena, etc. (Like a tree-trunk.
For one who intends to perform the Sādyaskra sacrifice, the altar is excellent. (Śyena, etc.
The threshing-floor is the northern altar. (Śyena, etc.)
AsvSS 9.7.15: The threshing-post serves as the sacrificial post (*yūpa*). (The Śyena and other [altar-forms]. AsvSS 9.7.16:
A sacrificial post with a wooden shovel for its top serves as the sacrificial post. (The Śyena and other [altar-forms]. AsvSS 9.7.17:
It is without a crest-ring (*caṣāla*). (The Śyena and other [altar-forms].)
The *kalāpī* and the *caṣāla*. These are the adventitious modifications known by the Adhvaryus. Other [modifications] as well are known by the Adhvaryus.
AśvSS 9.7.21: But when the crop has been harvested, there should be a sequence of formal injunctions for the Hotṛ.
AśvSS 9.7.22: One who is obscured by ill-repute or afflicted by a great disease, or one who, though capable of procreation, does not obtain offspring—he should sacrifice with the Agniṣṭut.
AśvSS 9.7.23: "Tiṣṭhā harī" and "Yo jāta eva"—these are the midday [laud]. If the entire sacrifice is dedicated to Agni, the stotriya and anurūpa verses should be addressed to Agni.

Alternatively, one may direct all the words denoting deities toward Agni alone. If that is done, one should perform the Indra-stuti according to the sequence of the texts. "Indra, [drink] the Soma; praise Indra"—this is the midday [stotra].
One who desires prosperity, or a village, or offspring, should sacrifice with the *upahavya* [sacrifice] (such as the *śyena*, etc.).

For one desiring offspring, at midday, he should sacrifice with the *kulāya* of Indra and Agni, using the verses "imā u tvā" and "ya eka id. For one seeking victory, at midday, he should sacrifice with the *ṛṣabha*, using the verses "tiṣṭhā harī" and "tam u ṣṭuhi."
AsvSS 9.7/31: "Marutvān indra yudhmasya te" is the midday [pressing] for one desiring food with the Tīvrasoma sacrifice. (Śyena, etc.
AsvSS 9.7/32: "Kva sya vīras tīvrasya abhivayasaḥ" is the midday [pressing].
Performing the *abhicāra* rite according to the procedure of the *śyena* and other [rites], the recitation for that [rite] is to be done with rapidity.
(Śyena, etc.
AsvSS 9.7:33: For that [rite], the *śasya* is to be chanted with speed. (Śyena, etc.)

AśvSS 9.7.34: One who desires heaven [should perform] the *indrāviṣṇu-utkrānti* sacrifice. (The Śyena, etc. AśvSS 9.7.35: With the verses beginning *imā u tvā dyaur na yantv indra*, the midday pressing belongs to him who desires, "May I go from evil to a state of non-enmity"; he should sacrifice with the *ṛtapeya*. (The Śyena, etc. AśvSS 9.7.36: With the verse *ṛtasya hi śurudhaḥ santi pūrvīḥ* as the opening of the hymn (*sūktamukhīya*), they consume the cups (*camasa*) with truth. (The Śyena, etc.)
AśvSS 9.7.37: "Truth is this earth; truth is this fire; truth is this wind; truth is yonder sun. (The Śyena sacrifice, etc. AśvSS 9.7.38:
A Soma-cup is the sacrificial fee. (The Śyena sacrifice, etc. AśvSS 9.8.1:
One who is about to perform the Atimūrti sacrifice should, for one month, perform sacrifices with the two offerings dedicated to Surya and Candramas. (The Seasonal Sacrifices)
AsvSS 9.8.2: [One offers] with a verse addressed to Candra for the white [animal], and with one addressed to Sūrya for the other.

(Ṛtu-yāja) AsvSS 9.8.3: Here he says: "They have perceived the cow; being born, he becomes ever new; the swift one, visible to all—wondrous has the face of the gods risen up. These are the *yājyā* and *anuvākyā* verses. (Ṛtu-yāja) AsvSS 9.8.4: "He stayed that great roaring river by means of sleep, having cast Cumuri and Dhuni into slumber"—these are the opening verses of the hymn. (Ṛtu-yāja)

AsvSS_9.8/5: One who desires glory [should perform] the Sūryastutā [offering]. (Ṛtu-yāja) AsvSS_9.8/6: "Drink the Soma; praise Indra"—with these [verses], the midday [pressing is performed]. One who desires food [should perform] the Vyomna [offering]. (Ṛtu-yāja)
AśvSS 9.8.7: One who desires glory [should perform] the Viśvadevastuta [sacrifice].
(Seasonal Sacrifice) AśvSS 9.8.8: One who desires cattle [should perform] the Pañcaśāradīya [sacrifice].
(Seasonal Sacrifice) AśvSS 9.8.9: For these three [sacrifices], the midday pressing consists of the hymns "kayā śubhā" and "tad id āsa."
The first two [stotras] have both [the *rathantara* and *bṛhat*] as their *sāman*.
(Ṛtuyāja) AsvSS 9.8.10: For the *ukthya* Pañcaśāradīya sacrifice, the *ājya* [laud] is "viśo viśo vo atithim" (Ṛgveda 5.1.7).
(Ṛtuyāja) AsvSS 9.8.11: The *pṛṣṭha* [laud] is the Kaṇvarathantara. (Ṛtuyāja)

The *go-sava* and *vivadha* sacrifices are performed by one desiring cattle. (Ṛtuyāja) "O Indra, let us come to Soma"—this is the midday [offering]. (Ṛtuyāja) Ten thousand [cows] are the sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*). (Ṛtuyāja)
AsvSS_9.8/15: There are sixteen one-day sacrifices (*ekāha*). (The *ṛtuyāja* offerings: AsvSS_9.8/16:
"Āyuḥ" and "Gauḥ," alternating [the order]. (The *ṛtuyāja* offerings: AsvSS_9.8/17:
One desiring heaven [should perform] the *Udbhid* and *Balabhid* sacrifices. (The *ṛtuyāja* offerings:)

AsvSS 9.8/18: "Indra somam," "Indraḥ pūrbhit"—these constitute the midday [pressing]. (Ṛtu-yāja) AsvSS 9.8/19: Having extracted [the Soma], [he recites] the hymns for victory and overwhelming power, and for the arrow and the thunderbolt, as well as the Manyu-sūkta.
(Ṛtu-yāja) AsvSS 9.8/20: One who practices sorcery should sacrifice. (Ṛtu-yāja)
AśvSS 9.8/21: For the *tviṣi* and *apaciti* [offerings], the *saṃrāj*, *svarāj*, *rāj*, and *virāj* [verses] are used, as well as those of the *śadasya* for the one-day (*aikāhika*) sacrifice.
(Ṛtu-yāja) AśvSS 9.8/22: For the *upaśad* [offering], the *rāśi* and *marāya* [verses], as well as the *kayā śubhīyā* and *tad id āsīyā* [verses] are used.
(Ṛtu-yāja) AśvSS 9.8/23: [These are prescribed] for those desiring prosperity, a kingdom, food, sensory power, and splendor. (Ṛtu-yāja)
These desires belong to both [the sacrificer and his wife] respectively. (Ṛtuyāja) The Ṛṣistomas and Vrātyastomas are the Pṛṣṭhya days.
(Ṛtuyāja) The Nākasads, Ṛtustomas, and Diṅstomas are the Abhiplava days. (Ṛtuyāja)
One who desires sovereignty should perform the Vājapeya sacrifice. (Vājapeya) There are seventeen initiation days.
(Vājapeya) Or there may be seventeen concluding rites. (Vājapeya)

AśvSS 9.9/4: Priests wearing golden garlands should perform the sacrifice. (Vājapeya) AśvSS 9.9/5: The *hotṛ*’s [offering] consists of a hundred lotuses with filaments like thunderbolts. (Vājapeya) AśvSS 9.9/6:
The midday pressing consists of the *viśvajit* *ājya* stotra, beginning with the verses "kayā śubhā" and "tad id āsa. (Vājapeya)
When the Marutvatīya offering has been concluded, there is an oblation to Bṛhaspati. (Vājapeya) It begins with the butter-portions and ends with the *iḍā*.
"Bṛhaspati, being born first, Bṛhaspati won all treasures."
“They entreat you, the agile Agni, for the office of messenger—Agni of beautiful luster, of beautiful luster, the fair-to-behold,” [this is] the *saṃyājyā* [verse].

(Vājapeya) AśvSS 9.9 / 8: If, however, the Adhvaryus cause a race to be run, then the Brahman, having mounted a wheel fastened to a peg at the place of the *tīrtha*, should sing the *vājinām sāman* while it is being turned clockwise: “The youths have come forth for the prize; the prize-seekers have arrived. Under the impulse of the god Savitṛ, may the coursers win the heavenly realms; the coursers win the heavenly realms. Or [he may recite]: “...the coursers win the heavenly realms. (Vājapeya)
If he has not studied the Sāman, he should mutter this Ṛc three times.

The third pressing is as described for the *ābhiplavika* [rite]. If they should chant the stotra on the *citravatī* verses, the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* of the Agniṣṭoma-sāman are "tvam naś citra ūtyā agne vivasvad uṣasaḥ," while the *ṣoḍaśī* is used here.
After that follows the *atirikta-uktha* (Vājapeya).

AsvSS 9.9/11: “*pra tat te adya śipiviṣṭa nāma*” and “*pra tad viṣṇuḥ stavate vīryeṇa*” are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses. (Vājapeya) AsvSS 9.9/12: “*brahma jajñānaṃ prathamaṃ purastāt*,” “*yat te ditsu prarādhyam*,” and “*tvām it śavasas pate*” [are the next three].
(Vājapeya) AsvSS 9.9/13: Having recited one verse from the thirteen beginning with “*tam pratnathā*,” and having called out, he should ascend the *dūrohaṇa*. (Vājapeya)

"Bṛhaspati, you two, Indra and [Bṛhaspati], [bestow] wealth"—this is the concluding verse (*paridhānīyā*). "Vibhrāṭ, may he drink the Soma-mead in abundance"—this is the offering verse (*yājyā*). For this [sacrifice], the sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*) consist of seventeen sets of each of the following: hundreds of cows, horse-chariots, horses fit for riding or for draft, large kitchens, female slaves adorned with gold neck-ornaments, and elephants with golden girth-bands.
(The Vājapeya sacrifice) There are ten other groups of sacrificial fees consisting of wealth, each group numbering at least one hundred, and no fewer than that. (The Vājapeya sacrifice)
Or he may practice the preceding [verses] in groups. (Vājapeya) He should bring them to completion in groups of seventeen each. (Vājapeya) Thus ends the Vājapeya. (Vājapeya)
Having performed that [sacrifice], a king should perform the Rājasūya;
a Brāhmaṇa, the Bṛhaspatisava.
For the Anirukta [Soma sacrifice], the morning pressing and the third pressing consist of the Caturviṃśa [Stoma]. (Anirukta)
AsvSS 9.10.2: "tam pratnathā" (TS 2.5.7.2)—this is the Vaiśvadeva [śastra] consisting of thirteen verses; it is *anirukta* (unexpressed). AsvSS 9.10.3:
"kayā śubhā" (TS 4.1.11.1) and "tad id āsa" (TS 4.1.11.2)—this is the midday [pressing]; it is *anirukta*. AsvSS 9.10.4:
After the *pragāthas*, the *hotraka*s should recite the first *sampāta*s; they are *anirukta*.
Or [one may recite] the *ahīna-sūktas*.
(Unspecified) In this same manner [the procedure applies] at the morning pressing (*pūrva-savana*) for those *bṛhat-pṛṣṭha* [stotras] that have not been specifically prescribed.
(Unspecified) The *viśvajit-śilpa* [sūkta] is used according to one's preference. (Unspecified)
For that [rite], it is the same up to the *pragāthas* as in the *Viśvajit*. (The *ājya-śastra* is) unexpressed (*anirukta*).
For the *Bṛhaspatisava*, the *ājya-śastra* consists of the two *ṛc*-verses for the *Niṣkevalya* and the *Marutvatīya* [śastras]. (These are also) unexpressed.
But before those two [stotras], the [chants] belonging to the one-day sacrifice [are performed].
(Unexpressed) The Hotrakas should recite the *śilpa* hymns, which are unmodified, after the *pragāthas*.
(Unexpressed) And they should also recite the *sāmasūkta* hymns. (Unexpressed)
The first *ṛc*s of the *sūktas* used in the *ahīna* sacrifices [are recited] in the unexpressed (*anirukta*) form.
The last ones of the *aikāhika* sacrifices [are recited] in the unexpressed form.
The third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*) is the same as that of the *Bṛhaspatisava*.
The *Nābhānediṣṭha*, however, comes here before the *vaiśvadeva* triplet. (Anirukta) AśvSS 9.10/16:
The *evayāmarut* [comes] in the *āgnimāruta* [section], after the *māruta* [hymn]. (Anirukta) AśvSS 9.10/17:
The method for reciting these two has already been stated. (Anirukta)
He whose cattle do not thrive, or who desires to lead his people to other regions, should sacrifice with the Aptoryāma.
(Aptoryāma) At the midday pressing, it is performed as described for the Viśvajit, with the exception of the *śilpayoni* [verses].
(Aptoryāma) It is performed as a one-day sacrifice (*ekāha*). (Aptoryāma)
If they should chant the *garbhakāra* stotra, the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses are to be performed in that same manner.
(Aptoryāma) First with the *rathantara*, then with the *vairāja*, then again with the *rathantara*.
(Aptoryāma) Or alternatively, with the *bṛhat* and *vairāja*; in this very same way. (Aptoryāma)
AśvSS 9.11.8: Or the Śyaita and Vairūpa [Sāmans].
(Aptoryāma) AśvSS 9.11.9: The Kāleya and Raivata [Sāmans] are for the Acchāvāka.
(Aptoryāma) AśvSS 9.11.10: Following the Sāman, two Pragāthas each are recited without the insertion of the *garbha*. (Aptoryāma)

But here it is an *atirātra*. (Aptoryāma) If there is no *dvipadokthya*, the third pressing belongs to the *vaiṣuvata*. (Aptoryāma) After the *āśvina* cup, the additional *ukthya* recitations follow. (Aptoryāma)

AsvSS_9.11/14: *jarābodha tad viviḍḍhi jaramāṇaḥ samidhyase agninā indreṇa ā bhāti agniḥ kṣetrasya patinā vayam iti paridhānīyā; yuvam devā kratunā pūrvyeṇa iti yājyā.* AsvSS_9.11/15: *yad adya kac ca vṛtrahan ud gha id abhi śrutā maghā māno viśvābhiḥ prātaryāvāṇā kṣetrasya pate madhumantam ūrmim iti paridhānīyā; yuvām devās traya ekādaśāsa iti yājyā.* (Aptoryāma)

*AsvSS_9.11/16*: "We impel that Indra for strength; Indra is great who [rules] by might; now, O Aśvins, that chariot of yours..."—with these verses beginning "The sweet plants, the heavens, and the waters," the *paridhānīyā* is concluded. "O Aśvins, that deed of yours is to be praised"—this is the *yājyā*. *(Aptoryāma)* *AsvSS_9.11/18*: Or else, the final verse of the *anurūpa*, "From here may the gods protect us," is used. *(Aptoryāma)*

AsvSS 9.11/19: “I praise Heaven and Earth, both of them; now indeed the two divine Hotṛs, the first appointed priests”—this is the concluding verse (*paridhānīyā*). “This portion has been set down for you, O worshipful ones”—this is the offering verse (*yājyā*). (Aptoryāma) AsvSS 9.11/20: If he should not recite [the preceding], then the four offering verses beginning with “Your ancient home, your auspicious friendship” are used. (Aptoryāma) AsvSS 9.11/21: “Sing this for you at the pressing; sing a hymn to Indra”; or “That one of yours who conquers all together; truly, the subjects follow after you”—these are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses. (Aptoryāma)
AśvSS 9.11/22: The sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*) are unlimited, exceeding one thousand.
(Aptoryāma) AśvSS 9.11/23: And a white [horse], as well as mules for each Hotṛ priest.
(Aptoryāma) AśvSS 10.1/1: The Jyotis [sacrifice] is for one who desires prosperity.
(Special Atirātra):
For one desiring offspring, [the sacrifice] consists of nine and seventeen [stomas].
(Special Atirātra)
The *viṣuvat-stoma* is for one who has rivals.
(A special *atirātra*) The *gaura* and the *abhijit* [are also used].
The *gaura* [Atirātra] with both *sāmans* and all *stomas* is for one who desires to become prosperous.
(Special Atirātra)
AsvSS_10.1/6: [The Viśvajit] for one suffering from a long-term illness;
(a special Atirātra).
AsvSS_10.1/7: The Viśvajit for one desiring cattle.

The *pṛṣṭhya* days are performed from the beginning separately for those desiring celibacy (*brahmacarya*), power (*sāmarthya*), progeny (*prajā*), and stability (*pratiṣṭhā*), each according to their respective desires.
Thus end the *atirātras*.
Of these, the first three are to be recited as the *śastra* hymns of the one-day (*aikāhika*) sacrifices.
(Special *Atirātra*)
Thus end the one-day sacrifices (ekāhas).
Now follow the multi-day sacrifices (ahīnas).

(Special Atirātra) The [sacrificial sessions] lasting from two days up to twelve nights, beginning with the Agniṣṭoma and ending with the Atirātra, conclude within a month and involve an unlimited number of initiation days (*dīkṣā*).
(Special Atirātra)
In that [sacrifice], the number of days is calculated as ending with a six-day period, excluding the *abhiplava*.
(Special *atirātra*) The *atirātra*, however, is the final [day] for the purpose of completing the count of those [days] already taken.
In the case of a deficiency [of stotras], the Vaiśvānara [śastra] is added.
(Special Atirātra)
The Āṅgirasa [rite] is for one who desires heaven. Or it is for one who is virtuous but lacks [prosperity], and who does not desire further advancement.
(2–5 Sutyā-day sacrifices):
The Caitraratha is for one desiring food;
the Kāpivana is for one desiring heaven. These are two-day sacrifices.
(2–5 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AśvSS 10.2/4: But for the first of the subsequent days, the third pressing belongs to the third savana.
AsvSS_10.2/5: And the clarified butter [is offered] with the verse, "For thou art indeed a master of the field" (*tvam hi kṣaitavat*).
(2–5 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AsvSS_10.2/6: One who desires heaven should perform this Gava-trirātra sacrifice.
(2–5 Sutyā-days) AśvSS 10.2/7: For that middle day, the Vāmadevya is the *pṛṣṭha*;
the *viśoviśīya* is the *agniṣṭomasāman*.
(2–5 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AśvSS 10.2/8: The Vāravantīya [is chanted] on the final [verse].
(2–5 Sutyā-day sacrifices)
AsvSS_10.2/9: "O Agni, you [bring] the Vasus," and likewise the *ājya* [hymns].
(2–5: Sutyā-day sacrifices) AsvSS_10.2/10: One who desires sovereignty should perform the Veda-trirātra sacrifice.
(2–5 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AśvSS 10.2/11: All [these] are *atirātra*s with the *trivṛt* [stoma].
(2–5 Sutyā-day sacrifices)
AsvSS 10.2/12: One who desires cattle should perform the Chandoma and Pavamāna sacrifices with the Antarvasu verses.
(2–5 Sutyā-days of the sacrifice) AsvSS 10.2/13: One who desires heaven should perform the Parāka and Chandoma sacrifices with the Parāka verses.
(2–5 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AśvSS 10.2/14: Thus end the three-day periods.
(2–5 Sutyā-day sacrifices)
AsvSS 10.2/15: The Garga-trirātra sacrifices are to be praised.
(2–5: Soma-pressing days and other sacrifices) AsvSS 10.2/16: One who desires sons should perform Atri’s Caturvīra sacrifice.
(2–5 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AśvSS 10.2/17: Its ājya offerings contain the word *vīra*.
(2–5 Sutyā-day sacrifices)

On the second day, the *ājya* [laud] is "O Agni, best winner of booty" (*yam agne vājasātama*). On the third day, it is "The mortal who [serves] Agni" (*agnā yo martyaḥ*). On the fourth day, it is "Agni, the hero among men" (*agnim nṛn*).
The fourth [soma sacrifice] is accompanied by the *ṣoḍaśin* cup.
(2–5 Sutyā-day sacrifices)

For that [sacrifice], the *rathantara* is the *pṛṣṭha* chant on *gāyatrī* verses beginning with "abhi tvā vṛṣabha suta" (AśvSS 10.2/20). On *anuṣṭubh-bṛhatī* verses, the *bṛhat* is used (AśvSS 10.2/21).
(2–5 Sutyā and other sacrifices) AśvSS 10.2/22: Or [he recites] "O thou, the peerless one, who wast born from the strength of the possessor of cattle on the fourth day.
(2–5 Sutyā and other sacrifices)
A person desiring prosperity should perform the Jāmadagna sacrifice.
Its Upasad days consist of offerings of sacrificial cakes (puroḍāśa).
(2–5 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AśvSS 10.2/25: One who has rivals should perform the Vaiśvāmitra sacrifice; one desiring offspring should perform the Vasiṣṭhasaṃsarpa.
Thus [are] the four-day sacrifices.

(2–5 Sutyā-day sacrifices) One desiring cattle should perform the Sārvasena; one who has rivals should perform the Daiva; one desiring cattle should perform the Pañcaśāradīya; one desiring long life should perform the Vratavat; and one about to speak eloquently should perform the Vāvara.
(2–5 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AśvSS 10.2/28: Thus [are] the five-night sacrifices.
(2–5 Sutyā-day sacrifices)

In the Pañcaśāradīya sacrifice, there are seventeen bulls dedicated to Indra and the Maruts, together with seventeen heifers dedicated to the Maruts; fifteen five-year-old animals have fire carried around them and are the Savanīya victims.
(2–5 Sutyā days) For these, they should immolate three at each of four days.
The remaining five [rites] are in the fifth [day].
(2-5 Sutyā-days) AśvSS 10.2/31: But in place of the third day, which involves the observance of vows, there is the Mahāvrata.
(2–5 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AśvSS 10.2/32: The last [day] consists of the Pṛṣṭhya five-day period.
(2–5 Sutyā-day sacrifices)
AsvSS 10.3/1: [The sacrifice] of the seasons (*ṛtu*) is for one who desires a firm foundation; it consists of six days (*ṣaḍaha*). (Soma-pressing days 6–10).
AsvSS 10.3/2: It is the *pṛṣṭhya* [ṣaḍaha], either performed in its complete form (*samūḷha*) or in its expanded form (*vyūḷha*).
(6–10 Sutyā and other sacrifices) AśvSS 10.3: One who desires cattle should perform the *pṛṣṭhya* sacrifice with the *avalamba* [offering].
(6–10 Sutyā and other sacrifices)
AsvSS 10.3/4: The Viśvajit sacrifice is joined with the repetition of the Pṛṣṭhya-pañcāha.
(6–10 Soma-pressing days). AsvSS 10.3/5: One who desires long life [should perform] the Sambhārya sacrifice.
The *pṛṣṭhya* triad and the first *abhiplava* triad [constitute the first six days].
(6–10 Soma-pressing days). A seven-night rite for one desiring prosperity [is performed] by a seer (*ṛṣi*). (AśvSS 10.3.6)
One desiring offspring should perform the *prājāpatya* [observance];
one desiring cattle should perform the *chandomapavamānavrata*;
one desiring food should perform the *jāmadagna*.
These four [days] consist of the *pṛṣṭhya* and the *mahāvrata*.
(6–10: Soma-pressing days) AśvSS 10.3.7: The *pṛṣṭhya* and the *mahāvrata*.
(6–10 Sutyā-day sacrifices) However,
at the first [sutyā], the vow consists of its own *stoma*.
(6–10 Sutyā-day sacrifices)
The seventeenth [stotra] is on the second day.
(6–10 Sutyā-day sacrifices) The Chandoma-pavamāna is on the third day.
(6–10 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AśvSS 10.3/11: The Bahiṣpavamāna chant is twenty-fourfold; the remainder is seventeenfold; this is the fourth day.
(6–10 Sutyā-day sacrifices)
AśvSS 10.3/12: One who desires to obtain offspring other than those born of Indra [should perform these].
(6–10 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AśvSS 10.3/13: The Trikadruka, Abhijit, Viśvajit, Mahāvrata, and Sarvastoma.
(6–10 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AśvSS 10.3/18: One who desires prosperity [should perform] the Janaka-saptarātra:
the Abhiplava-caturaha, the Viśvajit, the Mahāvrata, and the Jyotiṣṭoma.
(6–10 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AśvSS 10.3/15: For one desiring cattle, the seventh [day] consists of the Pṛṣṭhya-stoma and the Viśvajit.
(6–10 Sutyā-day sacrifices)
For one desiring divinity, there is the eight-night sacrifice. (The Soma-pressing days and other sacrifices.
The Pṛṣṭhya, the Mahāvrata, and the Jyotiṣṭoma.
(6–10 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AŚvSS 10.3/18: One who desires long life [performs] the Navarātra; [it consists of] the Pṛṣṭhya [Ṣaḍaha] and the Trikadruka days.
(6–10 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AśvSS 10.3/19: The Trikadruka, Pṛṣṭhya, and Avalamba [soma sacrifices] are for one who desires cattle.
(6–10 Sutyā-day sacrifices)
Thus [is the procedure] for the nine-night sacrifice (the Soma-pressing days 6–10). The *pṛṣṭhya* [ṣaḍaha] consists of three *kakubh* verses and one and a half [verses].

The nine-night sacrifice is arranged with the *mahā-trikakub* [stoma] in the *vyūḍha* (expanded) form; it is also arranged with the *samūḷha-trikakub* in the *samūḷha* (contracted) form. (Soma-pressing days and other sacrifices)
The Abhiplava [six-day period] consists of the Catuṣṭoma, the Trikakubh, and the Adhyardha.
One who desires preeminence among his own people should sacrifice with these four [Abhiplavas]. (6–10 Sutyā-days)
One who desires supernatural power [should perform] the Kusurubindu sacrifice.
Of the three *pṛṣṭhya* days, one performs each one three times. (The Soma-pressing days, etc.)
One desiring cattle should perform the *chandoma* [sacrifice].
The *chandomas* consist of the days preceding the *viśvajit*, together with the tenth day, within the *pṛṣṭhya* period.
(The six *sutyā* days of the sacrifice).
AsvSS_10.3/25: One who practices sorcery [should perform these] before [the regular sacrifices].
(6–10 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AsvSS_10.3/26:
The Jyotis, the Gāuḥ, the Abhīṣṭoma, the Gaurīvita, the Abhijit, the Viśvajit, and the Āyuṣa.
(6–10 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AśvSS 10.3/27: One who desires prosperity [should sacrifice] with a porcupine quill that is reddish-brown.
(6–10 Sutyā-day sacrifices)
AsvSS_10.3/28: The *abhiplava* triad of days comes first three times.
(6–10 Soma-pressing days) AsvSS_10.3/29: Thus are the ten-night sacrifices (*daśarātra*).
(6–10 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AśvSS 10.4/1: The Pauṇḍarīka sacrifice is for one desiring prosperity.
It consists of the Pṛṣṭhya-stoma, the Chandomas, the Gotamastoma, and the Viśvajit.
The Navarātra is expanded [into a ten-night sacrifice], or rather, it is the Mahāvrata and the Vaiśvānara.
(Regarding the Soma-pressing days and other sacrifices: AśvSS 10.4.2: Now follow the two *sambhāryas*.
(11 Sutyā-day sacrifices) AṣvSS 10.4/3: An Atirātra, a Caturviṃśa, an Adhyardha-abhiplava, and either a Pṛṣṭhya [Ṣaḍaha].
(11 Sutyā-day sacrifices)
AsvSS_10.4/4: One who has rivals [should perform] the Indra-vajra.
(11 Sutyā-days of the sacrifice) AsvSS_10.4/6: After that, the Mahāvrata.
(11 Soma-pressing sacrifices) AśvSS 10.5/1: Now, there may be twelve-day rites. (The Twelve-Day Sacrifice)
They may be Sattras,
or they may be Ahīnas (the twelve-day sacrifice).
(The twelve-day rite.)
The ten-night rite has been explained. (The twelve-day rite:
whether it is contracted or expanded.
(Dvādaśāha) AsvSS 10.5/5: On both sides of that are two Atirātras.
(Dvādaśāha)
Or, for two wives who are to be supported, he should place the Vaiśvānara brick [at the end of] the twelve-day rite;
one desiring prosperity should do so at the end of a year-long [rite].
The Atirātra, the Caturviṃśa, the Viṣuvat excluding [the central day], the Navarātra, and the Mahāvrata;
[this is] the Dvādaśāha. Now follows the Bharata-Dvādaśāha.
(Dvādaśāha) AsvSS 10.5/9:
They should perform this very one-day rite with the various separate terminuses.
(Dvādaśāha)
Atirātra first, then Agniṣṭoma, then eight Ukthyas, then Agniṣṭoma, then Atirātra. (The Twelve-Day Rite.
Thus is the twelve-day rite.

(Dvādaśāha) AsvSS 10.5/12: Desiring to prosper for themselves, about to propagate through offspring and cattle, and about to enter the world of creation, they desired preeminence among their own people; they should either approach [the sacrifice] or perform it.
(Dvādaśāha)
"(They should approach with six [cows]; he should sacrifice with eleven [cows]":
thus there is a distinction.
(The twelve-day rite.)
Now follows the general [rule].
(The twelve-day sacrifice.
Because dharma is immeasurable, we shall state its specific applications.
(Twelfth Day) AsvSS 10.5/16: Just as a limited number of phonemes attain an unlimited range of speech, even so, from a limited number of days, there arise unlimited combinations. (Twelfth Day)
AsvSS 10.5/17: But for those days that have been successfully completed, whatever their combination may be, the sacrificial offering is indeed successful.
(Twelve-day rite) AsvSS 10.5/18: However, in case of doubt regarding the days, some establish the decision by means of the *stomas*, the *pṛṣṭhas*, and the *saṃsthās*.
(Dvādaśāha) AsvSS 10.5/19: That [is] incomplete, because a transgression is observed.
(Dvādaśāha)

AsvSS 10.5/20: Having made an agreement with the Chandogas regarding the Bṛhat and Rathantara [sāmans] of the day, it should not be recited by those who follow the Rathantara [tradition] using the Ekāha [rite].
(The Dvādaśāha) AsvSS 10.5/21: By means of the second Ābhiplavika [rite], [the recitation belongs] to those who follow the Bṛhat [tradition].
(Dvādaśāha) AsvSS 10.5/22: Or rather, the *kayā śubhīyā* and *tad id āsīyā* alone should be the Nivid-insertions; the other [verses] belong to the one-day sacrifice (*aikāhika*).
(Dvādaśāha)
One who desires to obtain all desires, one who wishes to win all victories, and one who intends to attain all prosperity, should sacrifice with the Aśvamedha.
(Aśvamedha) One who is about to release the horse should sacrifice with two *iṣṭi* offerings. (Aśvamedha) [The first is] Agni Mūrdhanvat. (Aśvamedha)
AśvSS 10.6/4: The two *saṃyājya* verses are [the Virāj meters]. (Aśvamedha) AśvSS 10.6/5:
The second [verse] is dedicated to Pūṣan. (Aśvamedha) AśvSS 10.6/6:
"O Agni, you are far-extending," and "O Soma, those [powers] of yours which are bliss-bestowing"—these two [verses] contain the word *sat*. (Aśvamedha)
AsvSS 10.6/7: “O you of most varied fame, that which is most effective for carrying, that [belongs] to Agni”—these are the two *saṃyājyā* verses.

Having released the horse and appointed guards, there are three daily offerings to Savitṛ, following the ritual procedure (*tantra*) of the Vairāja chant. (Aśvamedha) AsvSS 10.6/8: Savitṛ is the one whose impulse is true, the impeller, the instigator. (Aśvamedha)
AśvSS 10.6/9: “He who has created all these beings,” “May the god Savitṛ come, rich in jewels,” and “May that god Savitṛ, the powerful one”—these two [verses].

(Aśvamedha) AśvSS 10.6/10: When each [section] has been completed, the Adhvaryu, seated on a cushion of gold to the south of the Āhavanīya fire, shall recite the *pāriplava* (the revolving narrative) for the consecrated king, who is surrounded by his sons and ministers.
AśvSS 10.6/11: The Adhvaryu, seated on a golden mat, responds with the appropriate *pratigara*. (Aśvamedha)
AśvSS 10.6/12: Intending to announce [the victim], he should call out, "O Adhvaryu! (Aśvamedha). AśvSS 10.6/13:
The other responds, "Ho, Hotṛ! (Aśvamedha). AśvSS 10.7/1:

On the first day, [he says], "Manu Vaivasvata—his subjects are human beings; they are these who are seated here. Householders should have been gathered together; he points them out [saying], "The Ṛgveda is this Veda," and he should recite a hymn (*sūkta*).

On the second day: "Yama Vaivasvata—his subjects are the Pitṛs; they sit here. Having brought together the elders, he points them out and recites the section of the *Anuvāka*: "The Yajurveda is this Veda. On the third day: "Varuṇa Āditya—his subjects are the Gandharvas; they sit here. Having brought together handsome youths, he points them out and [recites]: "The Atharvaveda is this Veda," and he should recite whatever medicinal charm (*bheṣaja*) has been prepared.

(Aśvamedha) AśvSS_10.7/4: On the fourth day, there is an offering to Soma-Viṣṇu. Its subjects are the Apsarases. [The priest says: "These are sitting here. Beautiful young women should have been brought forward; he points them out, saying, "This is the Veda of the Āṅgirasas. He should recite whatever [verse] is formidable and yet pacified. (Aśvamedha)

On the fifth day, [the offering] belongs to Arbuda Kādraveya; his subjects are the serpents. With the words, "These serpents are sitting here," serpents who are experts in serpents should be brought forward. He instructs them: "The Veda of the science of poisons—this is it! and he should recite the science of poisons. (Aśvamedha)

On the sixth day, Kubera Vaiśravaṇa [is worshipped]; his subjects are the *rakṣases*. "These ones sit here"—referring to those brought forward as *selagas* (thieves) and evildoers—he points them out [saying], "This is that Piśāca-vidyā Veda. Whatever is connected with the Piśācas, even if it be a mere fragment, he should recite that.
(The Aśvamedha)

On the seventh day, [the sacrificer] says: "Asita Dhānvana; his subjects were the Asuras; they are these who sit here. Those who have been brought forward as usurers should be pointed out to him, and he should say: "The Veda is the science of the Asuras; this is it," and he should perform some form of magic (*māyā*).

On the eighth day, [he says]: "Matsya Sāmmada; his subjects were the water-dwellers; they are these who sit here. Fishermen and *puñjiṣṭha* birds should be brought forward, and they should be pointed out to him, and he should say: "The Veda is the science of the Purāṇas; this is it," and he should recite a Purāṇa.

(Aśvamedha) AśvSS 10.7/9a: On the ninth day, [the offering belongs to] Tārkṣya Vaipaścita; his "limbs" (*vayāṃsi*) are these people here. On the tenth day, [the priest] addresses those who have been brought together—namely, young men learned in the Vedas (*śrotriya*) who do not accept gifts—as the subjects of Dharma-Indra with the words: "The gods are his subjects; they are these here. He instructs them: "This is the Sāmaveda, the Veda; sing this *sāman*.

(At the Aśvamedha sacrifice) the Hotṛ asks the Adhvaryu: "Who indeed wanders alone? Who indeed is born again? What indeed is the remedy for the cold? What indeed is the great receptacle?
(The answer is: "The sun wanders alone; the moon is born again."
"Agni is the remedy for cold; the earth is the great vessel," he replies.
"What indeed is the light equal to the sun? What lake is equal to the ocean? What indeed is greater than the earth? Of what is no measure known?"—thus the Adhvaryu asks the Hotṛ. (Aśvamedha)
"The light is equal to the sun; the lake is equal to the ocean.
Indra is greater than the earth, yet the measure of a cow is not found," he replies.
(Aśvamedha) "I ask you for the sake of knowledge, O divine friend, whether you have perceived this with your mind."
"In which three steps has Viṣṇu stood? In which has he entered the entire world?"—thus the Brahman asks the Udgātṛ. "I am in those three steps in which he has entered the entire world;
instantly I encompass the earth and the sky with a single limb, and the quarters are his back," he replies. (Aśvamedha)

AśvSS 10.9/2g: "Into how many has the Person entered? Into how many has the Person placed [his parts]? O Brahman, we ask you this; what indeed will you answer us in this regard? for Dīrghatamas Aucathya and Kakṣīvān are born of the same *gotra*.
(Pravara: Pariśiṣṭa)

marriage is permitted mutually, as well as with all others such as the Jāmadagnyas and so forth. (Pravara-Pariśiṣṭa)

There is no marriage between those who have two *ṛṣis* in their lineage (*dvārṣeya*) when there is a convergence with those who have three *ṛṣis* (*tryārṣeya*). There is no marriage between those who have three *ṛṣis* in their lineage when there is a convergence with those who have five *ṛṣis* (*pañcārṣeya*).
(Pravara: Supplement)
Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni, Bharadvāja, Gautama, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, and Kaśyapa—these are the seven sages (*sapta-ṛṣayaḥ*). (Pravara: Supplement)
They declare that the lineage (*gotra*) is whatever offspring belongs to the seven sages with Agastya as the eighth. (Pravara:
Pariśiṣṭa) As long as even a single sage recurs within the *pravara* lists, [they belong to the same lineage].

In that case, there is equality of lineage (*samāna-gotratva*), except for the groups of Bhṛgu and Aṅgiras; thus, marriage is [permitted] with one who does not share the same *pravara*. This is marriage.
(Pravara: Supplement)
